assets.text: 379 high resolution stills are plain AVIF files, loaded one at a time when you open them (51.9 MB in all). 3033 other images, including card thumbnails and volume stills, sit in 81 pack parts of at most 3 MB (184.0 MB). The stills were rendered natively at the same parameters as the live previews: 1024 px gray and hillshade from one field, a 1600 x 1000 relief, a 768 px volume with 320 march steps, and each real node preset in its own view. The 99 second pass prototypes and the 119 of round 2 have their stills as files at quality 82. 55 discovery images were re-rendered and checked by correlation against the image the lab kept; those are plain AVIF files at quality 82, the others stay at their source size at quality 80. AVIF 4:4:4 at quality 82; family comparisons at quality 58, analysis sheets and sweep grids at quality 42 to 54, at their source resolution up to 1400 px.

ideas.name: CraterGullies

ideas.name: MoonBase

ideas.name: HalftoneSpots
ideas.one_liner: ThinSpots' whole-spot thresholding with LowDiscrepancyDither's ordering: each spot switches on at an IGN, R2 or local-rank value of its cell instead of a random one, so coverage ramps as a halftone screen or a dispersed stipple with no clumps and no bald patches.

ideas.name: QuotaCells
ideas.one_liner: Per-cell rank from a hash-scrambled Morton descent: threshold it and every aligned block holds its exact quota of cells, at every scale, so N villages per region, exact ore counts and non-overlapping placement layers come from one pointwise value.

disp.where: round 2 prototype, panel scored, no plan yet

ideas.name: GrainPacking
ideas.one_liner: CellularCirclePacking run inside an affine frame per triangle: the incircle becomes an inscribed ellipse with its own orientation and aspect, still tangent to the three sides, so the plane fills with rice grains, almonds, scales and pebbles of many sizes that never overlap.

disp.where: round 2 prototype, panel scored, no plan yet

ideas.name: ChainCells
ideas.one_liner: CellularCluster's explicit children joined in their shape order by BondGraph's capsule segments: dotted rings become necklaces, trails become polylines, clumps become molecules, so constellations, circuit traces, beaded chains and ring hedges draw themselves with one parent hash.

disp.where: round 2 prototype, panel scored, no plan yet

ideas.name: GroundedCrystals

ideas.name: SurfaceScatter

ideas.name: ScreeShingle

ideas.name: PeakScatter

ideas.name: PinnedNoise
ideas.one_liner: Conditioned noise: any source is made to pass exactly through chosen values (and slopes) at jittered sites by Matheron's pathwise update, keeping its texture right up to the site, because disjoint compact kernels make the matrix inverse trivial.

ideas.name: BuildSites

ideas.name: GradedNetwork

ideas.name: LandformMask

ideas.name: FlowBeads

ideas.name: ClumpedStrands

families.answer:
A lattice phasor ships, but not the prototyper's 2^D corner kernel, and the other ideas are not all modes of it. Ship the same fixed-window phasor on FastNoise's SuperSimplex vertices: 4 kernels in 2D, and that node's 3D and 4D code has 8 and 16 vertices, the same counts as corners.

FFT reading: the field FFT cannot answer the question. Ensemble axis ratios over 24 seeds are 1.03-1.08 for every kernel at F1.5. The one-tile stat is also blind: corner 5.24 versus hex 5.60, though only the corner sheet shows a visible axis cross. The imprint shows up when gradient energy is folded into one cell.
| Kernel | foldCV | Bragg peak |
|---|---|---|
| Corner F1.5 | .461 | 104 |
| Hex k3 | .522 | 87 |
| Hex k2 | .378 | 71 |
| Splat j.5 | .201 | 30 |
| Splat j1 R1 | .090 | 5.4 |
The prototyper's "spatial, not spectral" is half right. Its conclusion that the imprint is invisible at F1.5 or when steered or fixed is wrong: square tiles show on seeds 1337, 42, 9001 and 777, and in all 12 panels of its own grid including spread .25. Warps and curved seam weights lower the numbers (foldCV .15-.29) but the cut edges stay.

Why hex and not splat: by number splat is the cleanest, and hex is only modestly better than corners. By eye hex loses the square grid and steers best of the three, though not seamlessly. It costs 4.30 ns AVX2 against 5.10 for corners and 11.64 for 3x3 splats (Perlin 1.56). The 4.30 was measured with k=3; k=2 was not measured. Limits: every kernel shows walled domains above about F2.5, and hex is polygonal by F3.7. 2D fixed selection matches brute force to 5.77e-6, but 3D and 4D with this weight are unbuilt; the 3D look test used a searched BCC layout.

Modes, where I disagree with the prototyper:
- phasor-noise is a Layout option of the phasor node, and the 4x4 window should go.
- defect-stripes is the Arms int only. Rough octaves cost 2.83x the base kernel and should stay out of the node.
- dislocation-stripes and transverse-dunes belong on vortex-phase, not the lattice. Coherent + jitter gives squared jogs, while vortex gives clean Y forks. Dunes on the vortex phase have wider flats and clearer merges at equal spacing, a moderate gap.
- vortex-phase ships as its own node, but it is buildable from stock: 21 nodes, 7.39-8.63 ns AVX2, same forks. The node buys ease and about 2x speed (estimate), not a new look. It needs a B source offset: cores sit near lattice points 62.5% of the time without it, 13.9% with it (uniform 6.2%).
- ripple-noise is a showcase, with radial-phasor as its outputs. Interference is real and nothing stock has it, but cost is about 12 ns (estimate) and stock PingPong(Cellular F1) gives clean rings at 4.49 ns.
- steered-band-noise and phase-vortex are dropped.

Open problem: 4D tiling. My scalar torus test of the corner and simplex kernels, and the stock vortex graph through fnlab tile, are seamless or close but lose constant stripe width. Stripes will not tile well through GenTileable2D. No real node was built, so all kernel results come from scalar prototypes plus the direct AVX2 2D harness.
families.proto_answer:
The lattice-phasor kernel ships, and the rest of the stripe cluster are modes of it, with two exceptions (vortex-phase and ripple-noise) that are genuinely different nodes.

Evidence. (1) Side by side at the default F=1.5 cycles/cell the 2^D corner lattice and the 3x3 jittered-splat phasor are visually indistinguishable: same constant-contrast labyrinth, same flat-topped histogram, same ring FFT, c0ratio 6.8 vs 7.2. Scalar cost 4.6x vs 7.1x perlin2 (4 kernels vs 9; in 3D 8 vs 27, in 4D 16 vs 81, so only the lattice makes GenTileable2D affordable). Steered by an angle field the two are again identical and both give the best fingerprint/tiger look in the family. (2) FFT for square-lattice imprint: all kernels show a clean ring plus a faint axis cross; the axis stat does not single the lattice out (lattice 5.2 at F1.5 / 2.9 at F2.5; 3x3 splats 11.0 / 8.6; 4x4 12.9 / 7.3). The lattice imprint is real but spatial, not spectral: with random per-corner directions at F>=2 the orientation domains have straight borders on cell edges, where the splat domains are ragged. At the usable F~1.5, or whenever the direction is steered or fixed, it is invisible. A 4x4 splat window hides it best but costs 13.7x perlin and goes blobby/moire at F2.5. Two rotated lattices made it worse (blobs); a smooth per-lane direction lerp failed (c0 1.1); the 2^D half-jitter splat window failed (coverage holes, c0 1.2). So: ship the corner lattice, optionally keep a Window enum {Corners, Splats 3^D} for the ragged-domain look, and record the seam rule R <= 1.5 - jitter/2 for the splat window. (3) Modes: transverse-dunes is an Output=Dune mode (stoss/slip profile on the phase, |z| taper, stoss-gated ripple); the relief at hscale 25 reads as a dune field and the only extra machinery is a polynomial atan2. dislocation-stripes is the Coherent flag (phase += F*dot(base, corner)) plus Phase Jitter: pjit 0 gives perfect stripes, 0.3 wavy, 0.6 isolated dislocations, 1 many; no explicit dipole cuts needed. defect-stripes is the Arms integer (complex power, 2 multiplies per arm) giving chevron/brain-coral; its Rough octaves work (fur crinkle) but cost 2-3 extra kernel passes and are optional. steered-band-noise is superseded: the carrier-factorised kernel showed ghost double stripes and blocky patches where lattice+angle field is clean. Coherent mode must stay off when the direction varies (it shears the phase into spiral targets). (4) vortex-phase is a keeper as its own graph-level node: cos(phi + q*arg(A+iB)) from two sources, no window, 3.2x perlin, c0 8.0, zebra stripes with real Y forks whose density follows the source frequency, and a 3D spiral q=3 isosurface of folded pastry sheets unlike anything on the sheet. phase-vortex collapses into it as Wave=Triangle. (5) ripple-noise is promising as its own node (radial kernel, time loop, rain mode, 3.3x perlin, c0 8.0) with radial-phasor folded in as CosPhase/Amplitude outputs; its unsolved flaw is that the seamless 3x3 window caps R at 1 so ring systems read as isolated targets, and the Caustic output never looked like caustics.
challenged: '2^D corner lattice and 3x3 splats are visually indistinguishable at F1.5': false. stripes_kernels and new seeds 42 and 9001 show rectangular cuts on the lattice and an organic field on the splats.

'At usable F~1.5, or whenever the direction is steered or fixed, it is invisible': false. Tile borders appear in all 12 panels of the corner grid including spread .25, and steered lattice has short straight seams on seeds 42 and 9001. foldCV stays .215 when steered.

'Orientation domains have straight borders on cell edges': the fold shows the excess energy as a cross through the cell centre, so the seams sit on cell mid lines, where the quintic weight hands over.

'FFT axis stat does not single the lattice out' is true but was used as comfort. The stat is blind: corner 5.24, hex 5.60, though only the corner sheet shows a visible cross. Ensemble field axis ratio is 1.03-1.08 for all kernels, while energy fold and Bragg peaks do separate them (104, 87, 30, 5.4).

Scalar ratios not reproduced: lattice 4.64x measured 6.50-7.11x; splat 7.09x measured 9.20x; ripple 3.34x measured 5.8-6.1x; vortex 3.21x measured 4.11-4.31x; dunes 9.07x measured 16.33x with the same params. The same dune binary measured 6.64x with no params set, so std::map lookups appear to matter a lot; do not rank kernels by this harness.
'Lattice est ~3.5 ns AVX2, 3x3 ~8 ns': direct AVX2 measured 5.10 and 11.64 ns, so the estimates were low and 3x3 costs 2.3x the corner kernel, not 1.5x.

'Coherent + pjit .6 gives isolated dislocations, no explicit cuts needed': the corner kernel shows a large closed loop and squared steps on seed 1337, and squared jogs on seeds 42 and 9001. Vortex phase gives the clean forks instead. The explicit cut form remains untested.
'Dune defect sweep goes cleanly from ridges to junctions to dashes': false. Defect .5 has horizontal gashes and defect 1 is a rectilinear gash network following the lattice.
'Transverse-dunes is an Output mode of lattice-phasor': works, but the vortex phase is better at equal spacing. Plain ridges are also a stock 8 node graph at 6.04 ns.
'4x4 window is the most organic': it is dotty, has an FFT cross, and has a flat grey hole with hard shards in the XZ slice.
'Ripple: the 3x3 window caps R at 1': only at jitter 1. R1.125 j.75 and R1.25 j.5 fill the field at c0 7.99-8.03, per the rule R <= 1.5 - jitter/2 the prototyper itself recorded for splats.

'Vortex scroll sheets at fr14: tightly folded pastry, no analogue': thick slabs at fr14. The folded look needs fr 30, and stock PingPong of |A+iB| at strength 9.5 is the same family at 4.57/7.53 ns AVX2.

'Vortex 4D works by construction': true for seams, not the look. The stock graph tile test has seam ratio 1.00 but few broad bands, because the plane carrier does not hold its frequency on the torus. Tested on the stock graph, not a real node.
'B defaults to A at seed+1': same lattice forces cores at lattice points, 62.5% of low |z| samples against 6.2% uniform, and straight cuts on seed 42. It needs an offset.
'Phase-vortex: keep as Wave=Triangle': that wave only greys the carrier in the q by wave grid, so there is nothing to keep.
'3D isosurface is gyroid-like': the volume is an irregular sponge, not gyroid-regular, and corner, splat and BCC kernels look alike at w6.
kernels: Complex accumulator Z (re, im, wsum, w2); lattice2/lattice3 (2^D corners, quintic weights, hashed direction + phase, Coherent anchoring knob gCoh); splat2/splat3 (3^D jittered compact window, seam rule R <= hi+0.5-jitter/2); half2 (2^D half-jitter, failed); dir2/dir3 (base direction + hashed spread); steerAngle (angle, fbm angle field, or gradient-of-potential); shape() outputs SinPhase/CosPhase/Real/Amp/Saw/Tri/Pulse with integer Arms by complex power; fastAtan2 from lab_proto.h for Saw/Tri/Pulse/Dune
Polynomial atan2 (lab_proto.h fastAtan2) is needed by Dune, Triangle, Pulse and Saw outputs and by vortex-phase Wave modes; SinPhase/CosPhase need only InvSqrt

families.answer:
Winner: caustic-web (the damped back-map with Steps >= 2). The single-sheet det=0 form does not read as pool-floor caustics, and I confirmed that at a seed the prototyper did not show: on the same Simplex height, window and tone map at D=1.1, seed 42, the web scores corr .921 / IoU .53 against the forward ray histogram and the single sheet .565 / .13, and by eye the single sheet is worm loops and blobs with no cells while the web is a closed net of curved Y-junction lines with brightness that varies along each edge, soft bowl floors and faint secondary folds. Seed 42 at a 24-unit window keeps the net with a clean isotropic spectrum and no repetition, so the look is not seed-picked.

The honest real-node baselines (fnlab): pow(1 - warped F2-F1, 4) is a crack net with crisp uniform edges, pyramid-shaded cells and bright pinched blobs where the warp squeezes the Voronoi; multiplying it by a Simplex and adding a soft floor brings the tone closer but it still reads as cracked cells in soft light; pow(warped F1/F2, 5) is thin uniform lines on flat black. The richest of these costs 10.6 / 23.8 / 61.7 ns AVX2 (2D/3D/4D), about what the web is estimated to cost once ported, so the web wins on look, not on cost. A technical artist who wants pool light would not accept those graphs; one who wants cracked cells already has them.

Where I disagree with the prototyper: (1) the corr/IoU score is not a judge of quality. I added a Newton back-map polish and it beat web/3 on the metric (.926 / .62) while looking clearly worse, with speckled double edges and junction debris. Differences under about 0.02 in the depth table mean nothing; the pictures do. (2) CausticMesh is a showcase or bake tool, not a node: 2166 ns scalar measured by me, jumps at fold edges, facets in hillshade, 2D and plane-3D only. (3) Steps 3 is saturated (web/4 scores the same), and Steps 2 is a legitimate economy default at 172 vs 223 ns scalar with a near-identical picture (.906 vs .921), so I would expose it as the cheap setting rather than argue over the default. (4) The plane-wave height of caustic-noise should not ship as an enum at all; caustic-noise is simply Steps = 0 of the same node. (5) The chain-rule soft form deserves to be a second output mode (re-scored .931 / .62 at seed 42, clean at step factor 0.5), with the caveat that at step 0.6 it already grows dark halo rings even though its score rises further.

What stands: check, speed, range, far coords, 3D slices and the vol all reproduce; the D >= 1.6 departure from the true ribbons and bowties is real; lines alias below about 30 px per unit; the relief is spiky and not terrain. The main port risk is the unwritten 4D Simplex kernel with analytic Hessian.
families.proto_answer:
Winner among the three ideas: caustic-web. Single-sheet det=0 does not read as pool-floor caustics, so the judges' split is settled against it.

**How it was tested.** I built the real caustic as a reference: a forward ray histogram (5x oversampled rays, bilinear deposit) of the same height, window and tone map. It is not pointwise and is used only as ground truth. Each candidate was scored by Pearson correlation of log intensity after a 1.5 px blur, plus IoU of the brightest 10%.

**Scores on the same Simplex height (corr / IoU, 480 px, seed 1337):**

| Depth | caustic-web | single sheet | CausticMesh (discovery) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.8 | .97 / .72 | .70 / .25 | .97 / .80 |
| 1.1 | .92 / .53 | .57 / .13 | .96 / .71 |
| 1.6 | .74 / .31 | .50 / .14 | .92 / .46 |
| 2.4 | .46 / .16 | .41 / .11 | .85 / .38 |

- Three other seeds at D=1.1 gave web .921 to .924 and single .565 to .567.
- The score depends on render size: the same comparison at 640 px gives web .91, single .53.

**What the images show:**
- **Truth and web:** the truth and caustic-web read as the same closed net of cells at D up to about 1.1. From about 1.6 the truth grows wide two-edged ribbons and cusped bowties, while web stays a single crisp line.
- **Single sheet:** it draws smooth closed loops and threads, and has no cusps at any Depth. This fits the geometry: det=0 is the critical curve in the lens plane, and cusps only appear after that curve is pushed through the map.
- **caustic-noise at its best (D=2, waves):** corr .41 against the histogram of its own height.
- **fold-caustic as written (A=.8):** corr .38 against the histogram of its own warp, and it reads as separate loops.

**Baselines (real FastNoise nodes, same scale):**
- Abs of warped Simplex to a power looks like single sheet, not like the truth, so single sheet adds little over a graph you can already build.
- Warped ridged reads as marble.
- Warped inverted F2-F1 is the closest rival at a glance: a thin line net. But its floors are flat black, it has no secondary folds, and its edges are more uniform.
- The real-node baselines use different fields, so they cannot be scored against the same truth. A scalar stand-in, ridge of the same height flattered by warping along that height's own gradient, peaked at corr .35, IoU .07.

**3D slices under z change:**
- Plane-lens web stays at corr .88 to .91 against truth for z from 0 to 1.2, and single sheet stays at .57 to .60.
- True 3D web slices also hold a net, with extra loops.
- True 3D noise stays a thread tangle, and true 3D fold stays separate loops.

**The three ideas are one formula.** It is f(det(I + D grad W(q_M(y)))): M=0 with W = grad h is caustic-noise, M=0 with free W is fold-caustic, and M>=1 with W = grad h is caustic-web. A single Steps parameter walks between them. Hence one node, with noise and fold merged in.

**Other results that changed the recommendation:**
- A Simplex height beats Perlin, which shows axis streaks even in its true histogram, and costs less than waves.
- An auto step factor of 1/(1+0.6D) removes the grain and ringing up to at least D=3.

**Caveat:** nothing here is ported, so all AVX2 numbers are estimates from measured scalar ratios.
challenged: The depth-table scores (corr, IoU) rank the candidates by look. Not reliably: a Picard-then-Newton back map I added scored .926 / .62 at D=1.1 seed 42, above web/3 at .921 / .53, yet the image shows speckled double edges and debris at junctions. The 1.5 px blur and 10% IoU reward wider ribbons, so the metric can be gamed and only separates candidates far apart.

CausticMesh is a candidate node. It is a bake tool at best: 2166 ns scalar measured here (42.8x perlin2), true jumps at mesh fold edges, polygon facets in hillshade, 2D and plane-3D only; a true 3D or 4D form would need a window^d of simplices.

fold-caustic as written has a reason to exist. Its default form (A=0.8, single sheet, independent Perlin noises) is separate loops around blobs on a mottled floor with axis streaks; only the back-mapped Simplex form earns a place, and that is an enum on CausticWeb, not a node.
kernels: Simplex value + gradient + Hessian in 2D and 3D (simplex2h, simplex3h); a 4D form is still to write. Measured RMS Laplacian normalisers: 0.296 for 2D, 0.25 for 3D, 0.183 for the xy part of 3D, so Depth means the same thing across kernels.
Plane wave height with analytic gradient and Hessian on a fixed direction table (waves2, waves3), flat cost across dimensions, no lattice.
Small symmetric determinants plus a 4x4 cofactor determinant (det2, det3sym, Det4 in t_caustic_compare.cpp).
Forward ray histogram plus scoring (Truth, Compare in t_caustic_compare.cpp): a reusable ground-truth check for anything claiming to be a caustic or a warp density.
