At mean overlap 4.91, mass kept at K=2 goes from .63 to .80 and K=3 from .84 to .94, and RMS error at K=2 goes from 1.55 to .90.
- Star voids become a hairline web, and K=2 stripes and Perlin now look close to K=4. The price is steeper slopes (dome K=2 from 9 to 24) and a few visible hairlines.
- Dense overlap is shown in grid_dense, grid_dense_stripes, grid_dense_perlin.
- The "K >= pi R^2 Density" rule only holds in 2D. At R=1.5, mean overlap is 14 in 3D and 25 in 4D, so K=4 cannot cover it.
- "-0.94..0.94" is the Perlin case only: stripes reach +-1.40 and craters -2.35 to .60.

Grounded stones: proven, with one correction.
- A per-stone voxel scan on 3 new seeds (333-387 stones per config) found 0.00% floating at default, steep, very steep, rubble and flagstone settings.
- A flood fill of the vol cube in 8 scenes found only pieces clipped by the cube wall, plus one single voxel in bumpy rubble.
- "Half buried" is false at defaults: exposed fraction is .915 at sink .35 and .504 only at sink=1.
- The prototyper's own rest rule floated its flagstones (11.1% tilt=1, 39.9% tilt=0). The support-distance rule from the earlier critic pass, now in the proto, fixes that.
- A CellularLookup graph now gives rigid stones at 36.8 ns AVX2 measured, but only sparse axis-aligned spheres with cut faces, and it has a seed+1 trap. The node wins on rotation, overlap and ease, not on cost, and its 33-55 ns is an estimate.

Family ranking: stamp-scatter and pebble-pile are the strongest, then grounded-scatter with the new chisel planes. Flow-shingle is the most striking but niche. Quad-stamp ships only for cost: a graph reproduces its depth 4 block look at 72 ns AVX2.

All node costs other than the fnlab graph benches are scalar measurements or marked estimates, because nothing here has a real SIMD port yet. Three prototype sources changed, each with a .prev2.cpp copy. Earlier verdicts are kept as critic.prev.json.
families.proto_answer: Does stamp-scatter really never pop with K-limited selection? Yes for popping, measured, with a caveat about creasing. At dense overlap (R=1, jit=1, dens=1, overlap-count image shows 1 to 5 stamps covering each point) the rank-subtract fade gives c0ratio 7.99-8.00 at K=1, 2, 3 and 4; the same scan with the fade off gives 1.06-1.26 (jumps) at every K. So K-limited selection is C0 at any K. The caveat is visual, not a discontinuity: wherever the overlap count exceeds K the subtracted m_(K+1) thins the surviving stamps. With solid dome stamps K=1 carves a Voronoi-like web of creases, K=2 leaves dark wedge voids at triple overlaps, K=3 a few, K=4 is clean. With a Perlin-patch source the thinning is barely visible at any K. Two combine-mode findings: plain sum/sqrt(sum w^2) normalisation undoes the fade and jumps at stamp edges (c0ratio 1.5), fixed by adding a background weight max(0, 1-sum w); weighted-mean (over) also jumps (1.53) and should not be offered. Only VariancePreserving-with-background, Sum and PNorm are safe. Grounded stones in vol views: proven. The 3D volume renders show stones of mixed size half buried in a Perlin heightfield rendered as one solid with the terrain, and the 2D side-view sheet is a cross-section where every stone silhouette touches the profile. The tilt option is proven with flat slabs on a steep hill: tilt=1 lays slabs flush along the slope, tilt=0 leaves horizontal slabs shelving out over the downhill side; with random rotation tilt makes no visible difference. The cost is the honest downside: 3D scalar 2756-2860 ns with tilt (27 Height evals of a 2-octave Perlin) and 1494 ns without, against perlin3 100-104 ns, so the node is only as cheap as the Height graph the user feeds it.
challenged: Grounded stones are half buried: at default sink .35 the exposed fraction is .915 over 333 stones on 3 new seeds. Half buried needs sink=1 (.504).

Grounded flagstones and the tilt option were proven: the prototyper's mean radius rest rule floated its own flagstones, 11.1% at tilt=1 and 39.9% at tilt=0. The support-distance rule from the earlier critic pass gives 0%.

Thinning wherever overlap exceeds K is the caveat of K-limited selection: this mostly comes from the rank-subtract formula. The cascade fade at the same source evals takes mass kept at K=2 from .63 to .80 at mean overlap 4.91. Only exact K+1 way ties must vanish (algebraic argument).
K=4 is clean with solid domes: true only at the prototyper's low density. RMS error to the 9 stamp reference with its fade at K=4 is .70 of std at mean overlap 4.91, though mass kept is .98.
Document K >= pi*R^2*Density: 2D only. Measured mean overlap at R=1.5 is 14.1 in 3D and 25 in 4D, so K=4 cannot meet the rule there.
Range -0.94..0.94 for stamp-scatter: Perlin source only. Stripes reach +-1.40 and craters -2.35 to .60, so a port needs a per-source scale.
Sizes within a pebble layer must stay fairly uniform: not inherent. A per-layer cell size from a golden sequence (sizej=0.3) mixes sizes with one constant per layer.
kernels: bumpMask (1-q)^3 compact mask, rot2FromHash/rotate2, Shoemake quatFromHash + 18-flop rotateQ (3D stamp rotation), superellipsoidSDF/superellipseSDF with an e=2 fast path, polynomial smin, TopK<N> insertion (Cellular-style Select chain)
3D scalar timing harness for Eval3 of all five protos vs perlin3/worley3 (perlin3 100-104 ns, worley3 146-156 ns)
Front-to-back occlusion composite out += vis*m*val; vis *= 1-m (pebble-pile, usable by flow-shingle for a C0 top-2 variant)
Confinement rule for no-window stamps: centre + radius inside the cell, superellipse corner factor 2^(1/pw-1/2), and the shadow band inside the cell (pebble-pile fixes)

families.answer:
Yes for shape: the images show forms FBm and the existing graphs do not give. Flat-floored rimmed craters that erase older ones, and separated round discs that never merge, are not reachable from Perlin/Simplex fractals or from cap-of-cellular graphs (the masked two-layer graph makes peanuts and clipped arcs; the four-layer Max makes a sponge). But only two of the five need a node, and they share one kernel. CraterField and BubblePack both are own-cell multi-scale stamps (one hash per level, feature confined to its cell), so I would ship them as one own-cell stamp node with a Shape enum, or as two small siblings. PuffyCaps is matched by FractalFBm of SignedSquareRoot(Max(CellularDistance EuclidSq, 0)) at a measured 23.9/68/218 ns; SphereFractal carve is matched by the prototyper's own 7-node graph; SphereFractal union is gravel, not cumulus. CumulusNoise is a showcase: its 3D nested-dome boulders are the only true lobes-on-a-parent result, but the 2D field is pinwheel pleats, the parents are over-even, and the port is two 3x3x3 searches plus projection chains (prototyper estimate 40 ns 3D, 120 ns 4D).

The family's three checks, by my own eye at seeds and windows the prototyper did not show: (1) Top-level lattices are real and structural in both keepers. Own-cell confinement caps the feature at one cell, so coarse features are near maximum size and at least one cell apart; BubblePack at seed 11 window 20 showed plain rows and columns (axis 36.6) because level 0 was axis aligned, and after the rot0 fix faint diagonal bands remain at seed 3 window 20 (axis 8.9). CraterField hides it better (axis 17 at seed 3 window 32, faint straight FFT streaks) but the big craters are visibly one size class evenly scattered. (2) Ordering seams: none found. CraterField c0 7.6-7.9 at every seed tried, 3D z-continuity max 0.0035; BubblePack dome 2.8 is the infinite rim slope, parabolic 7.96. (3) Over-even large features are real in CraterField and CumulusNoise and are the main artistic weakness. Density 0.6 thins the big craters without varying their size; rpow 2-3 adds a little size spread; the first critic pass's hybrid density fade (dsoft 0.25, c0 7.96) clusters them. A true few-large-many-small field would need the coarsest level to allow radius larger than a cell, which the own-cell form forbids; a 2-cell colour-fold top level is the port-time fix at 4x/8x hash cost for that one level.

Where I disagree with the prototyper: the CraterField scalar cost is 708 ns 2D (14.4x perlin2) at the stated parameters, measured twice, not 505.9 ns / 10.16x, so the AVX2 estimates of 16/18/22 ns look optimistic. The claim that graphs give only rimless dimples is too strong: a 14-node graph of existing nodes (CellularDistance bowl clamped to a flat floor, an Abs ring for the rim, gated by a thresholded CellularValue) gives sparse rimmed flat-floored craters at 23.6/65/208 ns AVX2; what it cannot do is multiple scales, erasure, and unclipped shapes (craters are bitten at Voronoi edges). NestedCracks is largely matched by Min of three F2-F1 layers; NestedCaps (dome mode) is the better discovery. The BubblePack wide-view lattice was understated. Dome/bowl Hessian figures and the AVX2 numbers of existing-node graphs are the prototyper's; I re-measured scalar speed and continuity only.
families.proto_answer:
Yes for shape, but only some of it needs a new node. FBm of Perlin cannot make these forms: its Hessian split at h=0.01 is dome 22.4% / bowl 22.5%, symmetric as expected. PuffyCaps measures 48.4 / 13.3 and CraterField 14.3 / 46.6. BubblePack measures 50.0 / 1.9 with 41.9% flat.

The convex lobes of PuffyCaps are not new, though. An existing graph, FBm of sqrt of clipped CellularDistance, measures 46.3 / 13.4 in its scalar form. Its real fnlab render looks the same in height, relief and 3D iso, at a measured 23.9 / 68 / 218 ns AVX2. So PuffyCaps is weak as a node. SphereFractal carve is also matched by a 7 node graph. SphereFractal union never reached cumulus; it reads as gravel or a raspberry crust, which is good but touchy.

What graphs could not match in my attempts:
- **CraterField:** rims, flat floors, erasure and a size power law. The best graph gave rimless dimples.
- **BubblePack:** separated discs and isolated vesicles, with overlap at 0.42% of covered area. The 4 layer graph merges into blobs and a connected sponge.
- **CumulusNoise (the reserve):** real florets nested on a parent surface, the only true cauliflower here. A graph cannot pass it the parent centre.

The family's checks:
- **Top-level lattices are real.** BubblePack at rmax 0.48 shows rows and columns (axis 182). Lowering rmax to 0.38, ramping occupancy from 0.5 to 1 and using lacunarity 1.4 removes them from the close view; only very faint rows remain in the wide view. A single CraterField level at occupancy 1 shows an obvious lattice. A size slope of 2.2 or more hides it by eye, though row shuffle leaves faint FFT streaks. Row shuffle helped CraterField and did little for BubblePack.
- **Ordering seams: none seen.** Own-cell levels cannot seam: CraterField c0ratio is 7.89, BubblePack parabolic 7.96. The BubblePack dome reads 2.86, which I attribute to its infinite rim slope. The colour fold also looked clean but cost more for less detail.
- **Over-even large features are real in two places.** CraterField at slope 2 with occupancy 1 was too even in the wide view until the slope went up. CumulusNoise parents stay too even unless a hybrid radius modulates them, and even then it is packed spheres, not a cloud silhouette.

The best surprises came from mutating PuffyCaps. Giving each cap's children their own local frame, a graph-impossible change, produced NestedCaps and hierarchical cracks. See discoveries. All AVX2 figures for proposed nodes are estimates; only the existing-node graphs were measured with fnlab bench.
challenged: CraterField scalar speed 505.9 ns 2D / 10.16x perlin: measured 708 ns and 714 ns (14.4x perlin2) at the stated 12-level parameter set with base=0.05, in two critic passes.

CraterField: 'the best graph attempt gave only rimless overlapping dimples': a one-layer existing-node graph (bowl clamped to a flat floor plus Abs ring rim, gated by thresholded CellularValue) gives sparse, rimmed, flat-floored craters at a measured 23.6/65/208 ns AVX2. It still lacks multi-scale, erasure and unclipped shapes, so the node stands, but the baseline is better than reported.

BubblePack: 'only very faint rows remain in the wide view': seed 11 window 20 showed plain rows and columns (axis 36.6) because level 0 had rotation angle 0; after adding rot0=0.5 faint diagonal bands of large discs still show at seed 3 window 20 (axis 8.9). The lattice is reduced, not removed.
CumulusNoise FFT 'axis about 24': seed 5 window 12 measures axis 40.9 with a dense even cell lattice in the wide view; the value depends strongly on seed and window.

NestedCracks 'no simple graph could nest them': Min of three scaled F2-F1 layers reproduces the hierarchical-plate height view closely; the only distinctive NestedCracks feature is the dark wedge grooves, which are also its max-slope-164 flaw.
kernels: Own-cell feature level with a fixed per-level rotation: one hash per level in any dimension, feature confined to its cell (CraterField, BubblePack)
3^D owner search returning best, second, owner centre, radius and hash by power distance (PuffyCaps, NestedCaps, NestedCracks, CumulusNoise children)

Owner-frame descent: local coordinates or surface projection from the owner, next level seeded by the owner hash and faded by smoothstep(best - second) and at the owner centre (NestedCaps, NestedCracks, CumulusNoise)
Corner lattice with margin clamp: min(q, margin) is exact and C0 when r + margin + jitter <= 1, using 2^D cells (SphereFractal, usable for any sphere-distance field)
Softened sphere profile sqrt(c + s^2) - s for a finite rim slope (PuffyCaps, NestedCaps, CumulusNoise)

families.answer:
Partly. GradedVoronoi, NestedVoronoi and CellFrame's blend work in the 3x3 / 3x3x3 window. The rest work only with tighter clamps than the prototyper stated.

Harness problem first: most of the prototyper's seam numbers could not see window seams. ContinuityProbe in lab_proto.h samples on a 0.01 grid from origin (0.37, 0.61) with steps of 1e-3 and 8e-3, so at that origin no sample pair crosses an integer lattice line. Moving the origin to (0.3795, 0.6195) gives GiniFoam press 0.3: 7.93 to 1.00; big capsule walls: 8.0 to 1.0; Planes S 0.6: 8.01 to 1.06; Hierarchy coast: 8.0 to 1.0. Graded stays 8. This probably affects c0ratio for lattice-based ideas in other families too; I only re-tested this family. I did not change lab_proto.h. The fix is to use an offset that straddles lattice lines.

I replaced it with a jump detector: bisection on every pixel edge, threshold 0.03, 6 seeds, 1536 unit^2 unless noted. A 0 means none found above threshold in that area, not a proof.

Seam results, jumps per unit^2:
- GradedVoronoi: 0 for F2-F1, Pillow, Crack and F1, and 0 on 3D slices (3 seeds, 432 unit^2).
- GradedVoronoi with the literal helpers: lab::worley3 and a square-jitter 3x3 2D window give 0 at jitter 0.9. At jitter 1 they give 0.0006 max 0.145 (2D) and 0.0004 max 0.099 (3D slice), the same class as plain F2-F1 in those windows (0.0013 max 0.151, 0.0003 max 0.065). So the handoff adds no seams of its own.
- Disc-jitter F2: wrong in 0 of 400000 2D samples and 0 of 60000 3D samples against 7x7 and 5x5x5 truth, which is why the disc-jitter window is the clean one.
- NestedVoronoi crack: 0 at aniso 1 and 3. CellFrame blend on the gentle source: 0 at jitter 0.7 and 0.9.
- Planes: 0 at S 0.06 at jitter 1, with small jumps from S 0.1 up. At jitter 1, S 0.4 gives 0.0031 max 0.132. At jitter 0.8 it is 0 up to S 0.4.
- GiniFoam: not seam free at the prototyper's press 0.3 jit 1 (0.0267, max 1.69). It needs jit 0.8 and press <= 0.1, so most of the small-bubble effect is lost.
- Hierarchy: lines need jitter 0.8; coast at default cw jumps badly (0.1128, max 1.79).
- CellularShape: distance is clean only for Rmax below about 1, walls only with small shapes at jitter 0.8.

Where I disagree with the prototyper:
- NestedVoronoi is not a keeper node. Stock graphs reproduce its look at about 2-3x an estimated node cost; that estimate is not measured. Hard-mode CellFrame over a cellular source covers the per-parent frames. If CellFrame does not ship, NestedVoronoi becomes ship.
- CellFrame is better than promising, because it is the one general new capability here.
- CellularPlanes hard mode is reproduced by 5 CellularLookup nodes at 20.75 / 68.38 / 256.22 ns AVX2, so it should be a mode, not a keeper node.
- GiniFoam should be a CellularDistance return type over F1..F4, not a node.
- The Graded k floor should be 1.4, not 1.15, and the gallery settings should be ratio 1.41 with 9 levels.

Limits of this review:
- No idea here has a real node, so every node ns figure is an estimate and only stock graph numbers are measured AVX2.
- Scalar ratios are inflated about 35% by Params std::map lookups (439 vs 593 ns on the same proto).
I re-read images until the claims kept here were checked.
- Each critic.json lists images_checked and not_viewed. Some of the prototyper's originals I overwrote without seeing as single files.
families.proto_answer: Yes, with stated limits: every idea in the family works inside the affordable 3x3 / 3x3x3 window (all prototypes use t_voronoi_common.h, a 3^D window with FastNoise's 0.437 disc jitter, no 5x5 anywhere), but each one has a parameter that must be clamped to keep the window honest, and I measured where the seams start. GradedVoronoi (the question's main target): the two-level penalty handoff is seam-free in 3x3 at jitter 1 once the blend constant k is above the largest in-window F2: the ramp test that straddles an integer level crossing (lsrc=1, out=4 raw F2-F1) measures c0ratio 0.87 at k=0.7 (visible rim jumps where incoming fine cells pop in as rings) and 8.00 at k=1.0, 1.2 and 1.5 (max slope 6.4); theory bound 1.144, default 1.5. The honest visual cost is that in the transition band incoming cells first appear as round islands that grow and only later get straight walls, so it is bubble-budding, not intermediate-size polygons. CellularPlanes: F1-relative weights are C0 (7.92-8.0) for Smoothness 0.1-1.0 but weights can pop at window edges above about 0.3-0.4, so cap Smoothness at 0.4; the sharp end is where the value is and the relief reads as tilted fault blocks. GiniFoam: the absolute Franke-Little kernel fails in 3x3 at jitter 1 (fan wedges / white blobs where no site is inside Rc); the F1-relative compact kernel fixes it (c0ratio 7.93-8.11) but multiplicative Pressure above about 0.35 lets out-of-window sites into the band and shows straight axis-aligned seams, so the Apollonius small-bubble effect is limited in a 3^D port. CellularHierarchy and NestedVoronoi are window-exact by construction (c0ratio 8.00 for wall / crack outputs); the exact-bisector wall variant jumps (1.06) and was dropped. CellularShape is exact only while primitive radius stays below about 0.4 cells: at size 0.25 x len 1.5 the wall output shows straight axis-aligned ledges (FFT axis 26 vs 11), at size 0.2 len 0.3 it is clean. CellFrame: the original two-sample blend is not a window problem but a junction singularity (564 probe pairs > 0.02 on a gentle source); a barycentric F1..F4 blend with d_K capped at 1.5 - jitter radius (the uncapped 4th distance is not window-exact and jumped at lattice crossings) brings that to 22 pairs, all at near-4-fold points with sub-pixel footprint, at the price of 3 (2D) / 4 (3D) source evals and jitter <= 0.9 / 0.7. Keepers: graded-voronoi, cellular-planes, gini-foam, nested-voronoi. Promising: cellular-hierarchy (junction wedge triangles unsolved, taper only trims them), cell-frame (residual near-4-fold spots, cost), cellular-shape (small-primitive limit, enum sprawl).
challenged: c0ratio as seam evidence: lab_proto ContinuityProbe at its default origin (0.37, 0.61) never samples across an integer lattice line. Moving the origin to (0.3795, 0.6195): GiniFoam press 0.3 7.93 to 1.00, big capsule walls 8.0 to 1.0, Planes S 0.6 8.01 to 1.06, Hierarchy coast 8.0 to 1.0. Graded and Nested stay 8.

GradedVoronoi 'floor k at ~1.15', 'practical floor 1.2', 'theory bound 1.144': crack jumps above 0.01 at k 1.0 (0.1487%, max 0.218), 1.15 (0.0070%, max 0.096) and 1.2 (0.0023%, max 0.081), none from 1.3 up, 300000 samples. The bound is the largest in-window F2 (1.390 seen). Floor at 1.4.

GradedVoronoi 'vol (out=3) gives graded spherical cavities' and 'F1 output is a graded bubble field': a penalty floor lifted F1 by up to k/2 between integer levels, and the old 3D panel is a mostly solid block with two strips of cavities. Fixed with flr=1.
GiniFoam 'clean at jit 1 for press<=0.3': 0.0267 jumps per unit^2, max 1.69, over 6 seeds. press 0 at jit 1 still gives 0.0023 max 0.29. Clean needs jit 0.8 and press <= 0.1.
CellularPlanes 'cap Smoothness at 0.4' as sufficient: at jitter 1, S 0.4 gives 0.0031 max 0.132 and S 0.15 already 0.0003 max 0.071. 0 up to S 0.4 needs jitter 0.8.
CellularShape big-capsule error 'wrong but continuous': it jumps, 0.033-0.042 per unit^2, max 1.71, c0ratio 1.00-1.16 with a straddling probe.
CellularShape 'small capsule no ledges, clean': walls at size 0.2 len 0.3 jit 1 still jump 0.0009, max 0.53. 0 at jitter 0.8.
CellularShape Dmax = 1.063 - Rmax for all shapes: not a bound for non-Euclidean SDFs. Boxes jump 0.0014 max 0.39, hexagons 0.0001 max 0.062. Per-shape bound (dfix=1) gives 0.
CellularHierarchy 'Coast 8.00': at default cw 0.8 it jumps 0.1128 per unit^2, max 1.79, 3D slice 0.0285 max 0.89. Near clean only at cw 0.25 and jitter 0.8.
t_voronoi_common.h 'jitter matches FastNoise' and the 1.5 - 0.437*Jitter cap for 3D and 4D: Cellular.inl uses 0.396144 in 3D and 0.366025 in 4D.

NestedVoronoi and CellularPlanes as keeper nodes: stock graphs reproduce the look. Nested value 39.01 / 124.51 / 424.80 ns, crack 21.31 / 66.45 / 232.55 ns, hard planes 20.75 / 68.38 / 256.22 ns AVX2. What the graphs lack is per-parent frames (Nested) and the soft S range (Planes).
kernels: 3^D window with FastNoise's 0.43701595 disc/sphere jitter (F1 exact in 3x3), stored window points (vector, d^2, hash, lattice cell), rank12 F1/F2 pass; every prototype in the family uses it

F1-relative compact weight Max(0, 1 - (d_i - d1)/S)^(2^m): used by CellularPlanes (plane weights) and GiniFoam (participation weights); window-safe because the owner always has weight 1 and S is capped at ~0.4

Window-exact distance cap 1.5 - 0.437*Jitter: any in-window distance below it is the true global one; used by CellFrame to make the K+1th distance safe and by CellularShape as Dmax = 1.063 - Rmax for the distance clamp
Per-lane reseeding from the F1 hash (NestedVoronoi child lattices, CellFrame grain sources): the Source/seed is already int32v per lane in Gen, so it ports for free

families.answer:
LOW POLY, simplex-facet vs cellular-facet-mesh. I agree with the prototyper on the 2D ranking and disagree on the packaging and on how good the PL-warped simplex looks. Cellular-facet-mesh is the best 2D low poly in the family at every seed I rendered (seed 7, window 12): large irregular triangles, crisp ridges, reads as a hand-built mesh. It is not flawless: seed 7 shows a few long slivers and a 2D axis metric of 47.7 against the prototyper's 10.9, and in 3D the Kuhn split is openly visible as an axis-aligned grid in the flat-mode XZ slice, so "nothing lines up" is seed and dimension dependent. Bare simplex-facet in 2D is a 60-degree quilt exactly as reported, while its 3D volume is the best 3D result in the family (cut crystal) at a fraction of the cost. The PL warp .5/.5 does hide the lattice, but at seed 7 the relief reads as crumpled paper with many small crinkled facets, busier than both the bare lattice and the cellular mesh; the prototyper's own number (43% more crease length) agrees. It is not a clean low poly look, so "relief reads as folded rock" oversells it. Speeds confirmed: 28.9 / 56.8 ns simplex bare / warp, 87.8 ns cellular (claims 28 / 55 / 94). Because the two share the whole output stage (Lerp, Flat, Tilted, Tent, LerpSource) and differ only in point location, I would ship ONE facet node with a Lattice enum {Simplex, JitteredGrid}, the grid option 2D/3D only and falling back to simplex in 4D, rather than two nodes. pf 0.25 vs 0.5 and jitter 0.6/0.75/0.9 sweeps found no better image; gallery unchanged.

EXCHANGE-FOAM LABEL: yes, it looks good, and it held at seeds 7 and 11 over a 64-unit wide view with koff=1: blobs of very different sizes, enclaves, any-to-any junctions, no visible lattice. With koff=0 the 4-label pinwheels at Perlin lattice vertices are visible in the field itself, so the per-field offset is mandatory. I tried the graph alternative mentally and against the real-node comparison image: Max of seeded copies gives the winner value but no node can emit the argmax label, and warped CellularValue gives convex, similar-sized cells, a visibly different shape. Speeds confirmed (Perlin K5 306.6 ns, facet 85.6, warped 852.8). Ship, with a cheap default source (facet or Value) because the cost is honestly K x source; drop Rank/Softmax; keep Gumbel weights as an advanced option at most since they need the source std.

BIOME-BLEND: the transition width is constant only against the control, not locally. I did not re-measure the cv, but the two-level render at seed 7 shows a border scalloped at cell scale and lumpy blob outlines in the wide view, consistent with the prototyper's cv 0.2 and p95/p05 ~2. Worse than the width issue, and not called out in the report, the textured render shows a honeycomb cell mosaic wherever the control hovers near a biome threshold: neighbouring jittered points pick different biomes and the kernel weights draw their cells. That is a lattice imprint even if the 3x3 window is not square. The cost is 9 control evals: 868 ns scalar for control plus weights (17.5x perlin2), 1042 ns textured, against 296 ns for DistFade (3 evals) and 124 ns for a plain Fade chain, both of which give a cleaner border on a continuous control. Drop it; DistFade is a graph recipe of existing nodes that covers the continuous case, and the categorical-control case is too narrow for a node. FoamBlend v2 (1061 ns) has the tightest width but at seed 7 its blobs have pointed cusps and the FFT rings; a curiosity, not a node.

All speed numbers above are my scalar measurements; AVX2 figures in the prototyper's report remain estimates. No prototype was changed and no gallery image was overwritten.
families.proto_answer:
LOW POLY: In 2D, cellular-facet-mesh is visibly better. Its relief reads like a hand modelled mesh, with large clean triangles and nothing lined up. Measured crease normal histogram peak/mean is 1.09, against 5.48 for the bare simplex lattice, whose creases lie in 3 directions and read as a quilt. It costs scalar 94 ns against 28 ns (AVX2 estimate 7-9 ns against about 0.8 ns).

In 3D the order flips. At equal vertex density the two look comparable, simplex has more equant facets and cellular has elongated Kuhn shards, while cellular costs 12.7x as much in scalar (342 ns against 26.9 ns). In 4D cellular does not exist. The 4D torus map used for tiling bends creases on the simplex form, so tiled output is not flat for either.

Recommendation: build SimplexFacet first as the general node, because it is cheap and works in all dimensions, and add CellularFacetMesh as a 2D-first node for when clean triangles matter.

Do not give SimplexFacet vertex jitter. The fan at J.2887 costs 81 ns and reaches only 1.78, while the cellular mesh at 94 ns reaches 1.09. A new piecewise linear warp closes most of the gap in any dimension: peak/mean 1.37 at 55 ns with facets still flat. It has 43% more creases, a softer look, and bent polygons in Flat mode, so it does not replace cellular in 2D.

EXCHANGE-FOAM LABEL: Yes, it looks good, and it is the reason to build the node. At K 3-8 over Perlin or warped sources it gives a geological map or camouflage with enclaves and any-to-any junctions. K=16 fragments and -F1 sources lose the point. Two corrections to the entry:
1. "Lattice free" is false as written. Perlin and Simplex are 0 at every lattice vertex, so at K=8 99.9% of those vertices have 4 or more labels meeting. A fixed domain offset per field takes that to 0.5% or less.
2. Exact shares and any-any adjacency are not unique. CellularValue quantised to 5 labels also measured 0.197-0.201 and 10 of 10 pairs. What is unique is the shape, plus Margin and the winner index.

Shares at K=5 measured 0.190-0.207 over 6 seeds and 4 sources. The Gumbel weights, untested until now, hit targets to within about 0.01, but only if the source std is supplied: an error of -30% or +50% moves the top label from .533 to .438 or .645. Cost is K x source: K=5 Perlin 317 ns scalar, 6.2x perlin2.

BIOME-BLEND: Its width is constant against the control but not locally. Median is 0.86-0.90 cells over control wavelengths 4 to 64, where Fade goes 0.48 to 6.84. At any one wavelength p95/p05 is 1.9-2.1 and cv 0.19-0.22. The border also sits a median 0.18 cell off the control contour and is visibly scalloped on a plain mask.

The cost is 9 control evals, about 90% of the node without sources: 895 ns scalar (17.4x perlin2), or 1141 ns with 4 sources; AVX2 estimate about 30 ns. Sources per 8 lane batch were 1.59-1.78 of 4 on coherent rows.

Two alternatives found here do better on width, using the same setup over 8 seeds:
- DistFade: cv 0.14 and p95/p05 1.42, with 3 control evals (AVX2 estimate about 13 ns) and no wobble.
- FoamBlend v2: cv 0.05 and p95/p05 1.13, with 3N field evals, no lattice, and shares of 0.247-0.251.

BiomeBlend's remaining edge is discontinuous or categorical controls, where no gradient exists.

All SIMD figures are estimates. The prototypes are scalar only.
challenged: simplex-facet: 'with PL warp .5/.5 relief reads as folded rock' - at seed 7, window 12 it reads as crumpled paper with many small crinkled facets, busier than the bare lattice and the cellular mesh; the lattice is hidden but the look is not clean low poly

cellular-facet-mesh: 'nothing lines up' - seed 7 gives a few long sliver triangles and a 2D axis metric of 47.7 (prototyper sheet 10.9); in 3D the Kuhn split is openly visible as an axis-aligned grid in the flat-mode XZ slice

biome-blend: '3x3 window shows no squareness' is true but misleading - the textured render shows a honeycomb cell mosaic wherever the control is near a biome threshold, a clear lattice imprint not mentioned in the report

biome-blend width: 'constant against the control' holds only as a median; the two-level border at seed 7 is visibly scalloped and the wide view shows lumpy outlines, so for a user the width is not constant
FoamBlend v2 discovery: presented as the clean width winner, but at seed 7 the two-level blobs have pointed cusps and the FFT shows ringing; not a drop-in replacement
kernels: Simplex location with barycentrics (no gradients): SimplexFacet, its PL warp, and foam over a facet source.
Output stage over one simplex (Lerp, Flat, Tilted, Tent, LerpSource at the vertices): the same for SimplexFacet and CellularFacetMesh; only point location differs.
Per field position offset plus seed stride for any multi-eval meta node over Perlin or Simplex: ExchangeFoam, FoamBlend, and any other node that takes an argmax of seeded copies.
Finite difference gradient with first order distance (value / |gradient|): DistFade, and FoamBlend v2 in its pairwise form.
Facet ids must come from a separate bit field or a mix, not an add on the hash; the add gave -0.48 correlation between neighbouring facets.

families.answer:
My calls: ship one node, surface-probe. Iso-distance and crest-lines become outputs of it. Contour-scarp is a graph recipe and eikonal-stripes is a showcase. The prototyper wanted two nodes with many outputs; nearly all of those outputs are Remap presets on a Signed Distance output.

Evidence notes:
- Nothing here is ported to SIMD. ns figures are real-node graphs through fnlab, AVX2; anything else is marked estimate.
- Ground-truth width means the true distance at the band edge, from an exact distance transform at 768 px over 3 seeds. Spread is p90/p10; ideal is 1.
Verdicts use only images that returned. Some listed single files I judged only from the same picture inside a family sheet: s_band5_h06, s_stripes_it0, relief_terrace, s_band3_far1e5, relief_mesa/bands/naive, crest relief, s_oct1, s_oct3_h05_c2, s_oct1_far1e5_k16. scarp_stacked_bands_relief I judged from the stacked-bands panel in probes_relief. The crest thumb I did not see separately; the sheet shows the same field.

1. Step floor at far coordinates: the need is real, but the prototyper's fix is mostly an artifact of its test.
- far_test.cpp has no Feature Scale stage. At frequency 1 I reproduce its result: at 1e5 features, h 0.02, naive error is 12.7% and exact-step 0.2%, about 60x better.
- Every real source multiplies by a frequency after the step, so rounding comes back. At the same point, exact-step vs naive is 8.8 vs 11.5% at fq 0.4, 8.5 vs 12.7% at fq 1/7, and 3.5 vs 3.5% at fq 0.01. Exact-step is cheap and worth keeping, but it does not extend the usable range from 1e4 to 1e6.
- The "2% at 1e6, floor only needs 2 ulps" claim contradicts its own file. The far test gives 1.9% with no floor and 25.8% with the k=2 floor.
- The 16 ulp Hessian floor grows linearly and passes the feature size. At fq 0.4 its gradient/Laplacian error is 14.8/14.2% at 1e5, 73.8/55.2% at 3e5 and 101/96% at 1e6 features.
- A fourth-root law, h = hw * max(1, 4 * (|x| 2^-23 / hw)^(1/4)), needs no frequency. Across 3 frequencies and 2 steps, gradient error stays at or under 8.6, 13.9 and 23.4% at those distances, and Laplacian at or under 14.7, 39.7 and 75.6%. Perlin only, 2 seeds, 2 sqrts per lane.
- At 1e5 features the 16 ulp and root-4 crest images look about equal. The gain further out is measured only, not seen.
- Above about 1e6 features no law helps much. At 3e6 and fq 0.4, gradient error is 33.8% at best and Laplacian 41.8% at best, across all laws and steps tried.
- Real nodes confirm a floor is needed: a slope graph at 1e5 features and Feature Scale 100 with a 2 unit offset shows strong diagonal moire, 5 units faint, 10 units clean in gray with some grain in the hillshade.
- Labels are off: the "1e5 features" images use far=100000 world units at fq 0.4, which is 4e4 features.

2. Does iso-distance give constant width from a 5 octave FBm? No, but it is better than abs(f).
- Spread with first order at h 0.06: 1 octave 1.07, 3 octaves 1.89, 5 octaves 3.28, 7 octaves 3.29. Naive abs band: 2.86, 4.77, 4.77, 4.81.
- It depends on width at 5 octaves: w 0.03 gives 2.40 vs naive 5.43, w 0.2 gives 4.02 vs 4.20, almost no gain.
- At 5 octaves the clearest gain is continuity: 2.6% of the core is missed against 11.8%.
- The step does change width: median true distance at the band edge is 0.082 at h 0.03 and 0.068 at h 0.06.
- It is not a new capability. I built the band from real nodes: it looks the same, check gives 0 FAIL, and it costs 44.49 ns at 5 octaves against an estimated 32 ns for a node.
- The Gradient Floor is broken at normal scales. It is absolute 0.1, and at Feature Scale 100 it gives median width 2.94 w and 34% false band, a fat mush.

3. Is contour-scarp an output of iso-distance? I disagree with merging it as an output.
- It needs no kernel and barely needs distance. On seed 42 the prototype's distance mesa and profile-on-value mesa are nearly the same picture.
- A real value-only mesa costs 13.34 ns, stacked bands from Modulus + Remap 19.40 ns, and the full cliff + talus Remap chain on a signed distance graph 53.06 ns, all 0 FAIL.
- The stacked preset spans -2.04 to 1.15 and needs a Remap. The value and distance versions do not match in look, so these presets share the character, not the exact shapes.

4. Is crest-lines stable or noisy? Stable against the step at 1 to 2 octaves, noisy above that, and fragmented at every octave count.
- Mask overlap (IoU) between step h and 1.5h: 0.995, 0.982, 0.956 and 0.659 at 1, 2, 3 and 5 octaves.
- Only 24.4% and 13.0% of line area at 1 and 2 octaves sits in pieces longer than 3 units.
- As specified it renders blank at Feature Scale 100 (std 0), because its thresholds are absolute. My scale-free version fixes that, at the cost of sparser lines that I did not tune further.
- The bad 3D result is mostly the power iteration. A closed-form solve drops z-continuity max from 0.50 to 0.031 and gives a connected membrane, which looks like neither Abs nor F2-F1.
- A thin warped masked F2-F1 graph gets close in 2D at 8.38 ns, though its lines are straighter. What no small graph gives is lines on the ridges of your own source.

Not tested: 4D, and tiling through a real 4-axis stencil. Crest has no closed form in 4D, so it will not tile. Real Simplex in 3D/4D has radius 0.6 kernels, so a finite-difference slope on it shows jumps (worst ratio 1.23, against 4.02 on SuperSimplex); the prototype tested only the r2 0.5 version. Prefer SuperSimplex or Perlin as probe sources in 3D.
families.proto_answer:
This was a resumed run: the earlier pass had already written all four result.json files, so I verified its images and code, re-measured iso-distance, and ran two extra experiments (step size vs specks on a 5-octave source, step and regularisation for crest-lines at 3 octaves). Answers to the family question, from what the images and numbers show:

1. surface-probe step floor at far coordinates: settled numerically. A naive finite difference breaks past about 1e4 features (7-20% gradient error at 4e4 for h<=0.01, 45% at 1e5). A k-ulp floor alone only helps at k about 4 and k=32 ruins 1e5 with 52% truncation error. The fix is to divide by the step the floats actually took, hx = (x+h)-(x-h): gradient error 0.2% at 1e5 and 2% at 1e6 with h 0.05, after which the floor only needs 2 ulps to stop x+h == x. Second differences (Hessian, Laplacian) need about 16 ulps: at 1e5 features the crest-lines Hessian at h 0.03 (2.5 ulp) is a hash of noise and a 16-ulp floor (h 0.19) restores clean but thicker lines. Beyond about 1e6 features the source noise itself is quantized and nothing helps. The jet (D+1 tap) stencil carries an O(h) bias of about 1.3h relative, central is 1% at h 0.05. The shared kernel lives.

2. iso-distance on a 5-octave FBm: yes, the band width is visibly constant along the whole coastline where the naive abs(f)<w band in the same frame has fat blobs at saddles and hairlines on steep flanks (the grid octave sweep 1/3/5/7). The cost is specks at fine zero crossings and critical points: at h 0.03 the 5-octave band has scattered specks (c0ratio 3.3), 3 octaves is nearly clean (c0ratio 5.0), 7 octaves is fuzzy. Doubling the step to h 0.06 (about 1/10 of the finest octave wavelength) removes most 5-octave specks with no width change (c0ratio 5.5), so Sample Distance should track the finest source detail. Newton refinement on the band adds specks (c0ratio 1.0), so first order is the default. Eikonal stripes work as a Period/Stripes output but only with 3 Newton steps: at it=0 the stripes collapse into compressed interference away from the zero set; with it=3 they are the fingerprint labyrinth with a ring FFT and knots on the medial axis, best on 1-octave sources. Terrace, canyon and a 3D constant-thickness shell (vol) all work. Measured scalar: 6.7x perlin on 1 octave, 28.3x on the 5-octave simplex FBm, stripes it=3 18.2x.

3. contour-scarp: yes, it is an output of iso-distance. It is Profile(d) on the same taps, floor and Level/Period handling plus a smooth max against the source. Relief shows flat-topped mesas with constant-width near-vertical walls and a constant-width talus apron, and stacked bands give stepped cuesta hills. The naive profile-on-value version is only subtly worse at this source (walls broaden on gentle slopes, thin on steep). Cliffs widen or vanish at saddles and summits where the gradient floor takes over. Status merged into iso-distance, either as a Scarp output or as a small ScarpProfile modifier fed by the Signed output. Not a look that justifies a separate kernel.

4. crest-lines: stable, not noisy, on 1-2 octave sources: thin even-width crest and valley lines with free ends and Y-branches, nothing like Ridged or F2-F1 (c0ratio 7.9 / 6.7). At 3 octaves with the default h 0.03 it fragments into dashes (c0ratio 2.1); h 0.08 alone barely helps (2.4, still dashed); h 0.05 with regularise c=2 and width 0.08 reconnects most lines into a continuous branching net (3.6) but never as clean as 1-2 octaves. It also hits the Hessian far-coordinate limit (about 1e4 features at the default h) and 3D gives fragmented plates with eigenvector flips (z-continuity max 0.97). Promising, with the recommendation to feed it low octaves only.

Overall: surface-probe (keeper, prerequisite kernel) and iso-distance (keeper, the world-unit width primitive with Band, Contours, Stripes, Terrace, Canyon, Scarp outputs) are the nodes worth building; contour-scarp merges into iso-distance; crest-lines is promising but limited to smooth sources and near coordinates.
challenged: Exact-step divisor gives 0.2% at 1e5 and moves the usable range from 1e4 to 1e6 features: true only at frequency 1, since far_test.cpp has no Feature Scale stage. At 1e5 features, h 0.02, exact vs naive is 8.8 vs 11.5% at fq 0.4, 8.5 vs 12.7% at fq 1/7, 3.5 vs 3.5% at fq 0.01. At fq 0.4 the Laplacian is not helped at all: 2.72 vs 2.39 relative error.
2% at 1e6 with h 0.05, floor then needs only 2 ulps: its own far test shows 1.9% with no floor (neighbouring smaller h values are NaN) and 25.8% with the k=2 floor.

Second differences need about 16 ulps: this floor grows past the feature size, giving Laplacian error 55.2% at 3e5 and 96% at 1e6 features (fq 0.4). A root-4 law at C=4 gives 15.8 to 33.6% and 20.6 to 75.6% at the same points (h 0.05 and 0.02).
'At 1e5 features' on the iso and crest far images: far=100000 is world units at fq 0.4, so about 4e4 features.

3-tap jet Laplacian shows a hexagonal null pattern and central does not: false. Central on Simplex shows the same six nulls, including the prototyper's own image. Jet on Perlin shows an axis cross. It belongs to the Simplex kernel, not the stencil.

'All are masks a graph cannot make today': false. Slope built from real nodes renders the same mask, check 0 FAIL, 26.62 ns AVX2 at 5 octaves. Band from real nodes: same look, 0 FAIL, 44.49 ns. Hillshade is close to a 2 node emboss.

Band width visibly constant along the whole coastline on 5 octaves: ground truth spread p90/p10 is 3.28 (3.81 at h 0.03), naive 4.77, and at w 0.2 it is 4.02 vs 4.20. Near constant only at 1 octave (1.07), decent at 3 (1.89).
Doubling the step to 0.06 changes no width: median true distance at the band edge goes from 0.082 to 0.068, band area from 23.5 to 21.3%. At h 0.1 it is 0.062 and missed core is 6.0%.

Gradient Floor 0.1 as a working default: absolute units. At Feature Scale 100 it gives median width 2.94 w, 34% false band, 57.5% area instead of 19%. The prototype was only ever tested at feature size about 2.5.
Crest-lines works with a=0.5, b=3, c=1: output is blank at Feature Scale 100 (min -1, max -1, std 0). The thresholds are absolute on Hessian values, which scale as frequency squared.

Terrace output improves on the value terrace: on seeds 42 and 7 at 3 octaves the plain value terrace looks crisper with flatter treads and the distance risers look smeared. That is my eye; I did not measure riser width.
Canyon cuts an incision of constant width with sheer walls: at 1 octave it reads as blue flats with thin crease lines, at 3 octaves as blobby noise, at 5 octaves pillars.
Crest-lines is 'nothing like Ridged or F2-F1': a thin warped masked F2-F1 reads as a similar crack network at 8.38 ns, though with straighter lines and 120 degree joints.
Crest 3D is fragmented plates, not useful: mostly the 4 step power iteration. A closed-form solve drops z-continuity max from 0.50 to 0.031 and 1.02 to 0.080, and gives a connected membrane.
Crest c0 6.74 is seed dependent: 4.8 on seed 42 for the same 'both' output.
Contour-scarp c0 4.94: 4.31 with the stated params; the sheet was made with default params.
Surface-probe scalar 5.82x with stencil=1: that figure is about the jet (5.71x). Central is 6.88x at 1 octave and 30.37x at 5.
3D continuity is measured on simplex3g (r2 0.5), not the real 3D Simplex (r2 0.6). A real-node slope on Simplex has 3D worst ratio 1.23 against 4.02 on SuperSimplex.

The exact-step divisor 'keeps the band identical' at far coordinates as if it were the cause: the naive divisor gives the same band there, mean difference 0.84 to 0.95 of 255, no pixel off by more than 12.
kernels: probe_common.h Probe2/Probe3 stencil: simplex jet (D+1 taps, O(h) bias ~1.3h) and per-axis central with exact-step divisors hx=(x+h)-(x-h) (2D taps, 0.2% at 1e5 features)
StepFloor(h, |pos|, k): h >= k * |pos| * 2^-23 with k=2 for gradients (exact-step) and k=16 for Hessian/Laplacian outputs
wrapP(r, P): signed offset to the nearest contour of the family Level + kP, shared by Contours, Stripes, Terrace and stacked Scarp bands
Fixed-count Newton walk toward the level set with a Min on the step scale (needed for the Stripes/eikonal output, harmful on the Band output)

families.answer:
Partly, and less than the prototyper reported. Defaults: the StrataTerrace caprock default does look like mesas, cliffs and plain slopes straight away, and it held on every seed I tried (1337, 7, 99, 555, 2024 at window 16). But the ablation tjit=0,tpow=1 gives a relief I cannot tell from the default, which means the two things the node adds over a staircase (hashed layer thickness, talus apron) are invisible at the default. Worse for the node: the alternating hard/soft caprock profile is algebraically Max( s, Terrace( s, 2T ) ), and the stock graph Add( Max( S, Terrace( S, Step Count 1.8, Smoothness 0.05 ) ), Plane ) with S = Subtract( FBm, Gradient plane ) reproduces flat caps, cliffs and plain slopes in one stack on seeds 1337 and 7 (13 ns AVX2 2D with the FBm evaluated twice). The prototyper tried Terrace alone and two-Terrace Fades but never Max, so the central claim 'Terrace cannot do this' fails. Tilt is a Gradient added and subtracted, folds the same with a Perlin. So mesas and cuestas: graph recipe, not a node. For 3D, density + PingPong(Gradient along the strata axis) gives corrugated ledges and some overhangs from stock nodes; the proto's hoodoos with clean mushroom caps are nicer but leave floating fragments, so that is a showcase image at most.

Wood: the Timber profile reads as sawn wood on stretched Perlin and on GrowthAge, agreed. But the claim that the node with jitter and contrast off reads as zebra stripes did not reproduce; jit=0,ajit=0,lat=0 still reads as wood and is close to the default. A stock PowInt(3) of a smoothed sawtooth (S - Terrace(S)) on the same stretched FBm reads as harder engraved stripes, wood-ish but worse, so the soft latewood drop and per-ring contrast are a real but mild refinement. Knots and cathedral arches only come from GrowthAge, which no graph reaches; that is the one genuinely new thing in the family, and it is a niche material texture with a non-stationary trunk, thin rings that alias (c0ratio 1.71, max slope 651 at the default remap) and a 3D isosurface that is splintery sheets, not the timber block claimed.

Agate 'from any field': the agate profile on single Perlin is the best texture image in the family and neither stock lookup matches it: the 1D Value lookup is soft, and a 1D CellularValue lookup (AddDimension over DomainAxisScale 0,0) gives flat poster-like bands with hashed widths, striking but cartoony and 49 ns AVX2 because it runs two 3D cellular searches. So the band kernel earns a place, but everything in StrataBands and StrataTerrace is a 1D profile of the source on a jittered band lattice, which is what Terrace already is with a staircase profile. My call: give Terrace a Thickness Jitter and a Profile enum (Step | Caprock | Agate | Timber) plus an optional Lateral source, about 1 ns over the source, instead of a new Strata node. Glacial troughs look good at the default on new seeds too, but the troughs are smooth canals, tributaries do not branch, closed loops remain in the wide view, and the prototyper's own stock F2-F1 carve graph is about as strong; graph recipe, as they half conceded.

Where I disagree most: the prototyper scored the caprock stack as the family's keeper; it is the easiest one to replace with four stock nodes. The only true keeper-grade novelty is GrowthAge's knots, and that is a showcase, not a building block.
families.proto_answer:
Mostly yes. The modest look came from the layer profile, not just the parameter values, and a new profile fixes it.

MESAS AND CUESTAS: yes, with a qualification. The old profile gave every layer a bench and read as paddy terraces. In the new one, hard layers are a short cliff then a flat cap. Soft layers keep the source slope and steepen into a talus apron under a hard layer. Plain alternation of hard and soft layers (k & 1) held on all 4 seeds I rendered. Seed-rolled hardness gave seeds 1337 and 7 mostly hills. Default relief now shows flat-capped mesas, cliff bands and smooth slopes straight away. dipx=0.8 gives parallel hogbacks, and a fold source gives curved cliff bands.

The claim that Terrace and graphs cannot do this is only partly true:
- A graph can tilt Terrace, and tilted Terrace reaches parallel cuestas with equal rhythm.
- FN Terrace with a very large step makes mesas on a plain (seen on one seed).
- A real stock density graph with a two-Terrace sawtooth gives crisp, unevenly spaced 3D ledges, so that 3D gain is smaller than the earlier run reported.
- What stock Terrace and the two-Terrace graphs did not give is flat caps, cliffs and plain slopes in one stack. A real Terrace at matching cliff spacing is an even staircase, and a real two-Terrace Fade goes bumpy.
- Overhanging caps in 3D are also new, but they leave small floating fragments.

WOOD: yes, and this is the clearest win. A new Timber profile (mostly light, thin dark latewood building on one side, hashed ring width and contrast) reads as sawn wood on stretched Perlin and on GrowthAge. Its rivals read as stripes or stone: a real equal-sawtooth graph and the node with jitter and contrast off both look like zebra stripes, and the 1D lookup (scalar copy of the stock graph) on GrowthAge looks like banded stone. Knots and cathedral arches need GrowthAge; I could not get them from warping noise.

AGATE: yes from one setting (bands 8, weak laminae, seams 0.6). It reads as polished agate on single Perlin, malachite on Worley and sediment on a gradient. FBm and warped fields give ragged banded stone, and ridged is the weakest. However, the real stock 1D lookup graph is a genuine rival: soft and pretty, without seams. The node is richer, not a different league.

"Any field" holds for agate. Timber needs a field with long iso-lines; on FBm and Worley it gives engraved contour lines, not wood.

GLACIAL: the look is good after I let walls scale the source and stretched the valley source, especially with a fjord floor. But the tributary system does not read as branching, hanging valleys are barely visible and some closed loops remain. A real stock F2-F1 graph gives fjord blocks about as strong, so only gradient-normalised width is earned, and iso-distance already has that.

STRUCTURE: build one Strata node with a Profile enum (Caprock, Agate, Timber, Sawtooth, Layer Value) plus GrowthAge as a field. Treat glacial troughs as an IsoDistance output or a saved graph at most.

All timings are scalar prototype figures inflated by parameter map lookups. AVX2 numbers are estimates, apart from the stock graph benches.
challenged: StrataTerrace: 'what stock Terrace and the two-Terrace graphs did not give is flat caps, cliffs and plain slopes in one stack'. Add(Max(S, Terrace(S)), Plane) in stock nodes gives exactly that on seeds 1337 and 7; the alternating caprock profile is Max( s, Terrace( s, 2T ) ).
StrataTerrace: hashed thickness jitter and the talus power are part of the look. Relief with tjit=0,tpow=1 is visually indistinguishable from the default.
StrataBands: 'the node with jitter and contrast off reads as zebra stripes at matched density'. The proto with jit=0,ajit=0,lat=0 on stretched Perlin still reads as wood and is close to the default.
GrowthAge: 'Vol at iso 0.58 is a timber block whose grain grooves agree across faces, with a knot on top'. At iso 0.58 with the default params the isosurface is a stack of thin splintery sheets.

GrowthAge: c0ratio 3.14 with max slope 351 through Timber at 10 rings. The default check measures c0ratio 1.71 and max slope 651 per unit (the thinnest jittered ring), so the rings alias harder than reported.
StrataTerrace 3D: overhanging caps are new. density + PingPong(Gradient along the strata axis) in stock nodes also undercuts ledges, though the proto's mushroom caps are cleaner.
kernels: Jittered 1D band lattice: floor(s), hashed boundaries, two Select fix-ups, returns k, u, lo, hi. Used by the StrataTerrace layers, StrataBands agate and timber, and the GrowthAge remap.
Zero-at-band-ends envelope: per-band contrast and lateral slices can change at a boundary with no seam.
Slow 1D value noise over the band coordinate for tone drift, 2 hashes and continuous.
Gradient-normalised distance |n| / max(|grad n|, floor) with 1 + dim evals, the same kernel as iso-distance, used by the glacial tiers.

families.answer:
ONE-SIDED FRONTS: real, but the prototyper's account is wrong in several places.

Uniqueness: "No existing node or graph" is only partly true. Nested self DomainOffset gives only blobs and rings. A stock Modulus graph, Add(Multiply(Modulus(Add(Gradient, Multiply(Perlin, .9)), 1.5), .5), Multiply(Perlin, .6)), does give one-sided ramps and cliffs, convincing in relief, at a measured 4.59/7.75/12.60 ns AVX2. Its cliffs are one height and run as long unbroken level sets. Node shocks start from nothing, grow, hook and merge, and any source works. That is the real uniqueness.

Pinholes: the prototyper's bisection and K21 counts reproduce exactly on seed 1337, but the counter misleads because it only sees islands up to 40 px.
- Against a converged reference (locked K65, within 0.05-0.06% of unlocked K33 N6 at t=1.5), bisection has 3.71% of pixels on the wrong root with 42 thick islands. Entropy K13 N4 has 0.84% with 16.
- Entropy K13 is not "nearly pinhole free". By the prototyper's own counter it is worse than bisection in all 4 cases I ran, in islands/px: 25/43 vs 12/28, 134/842 vs 33/287, 172/382 vs 73/177, 34/134 vs 10/76. Sliding taps fray the shock edges.
- K21 does not remove them either: 6/52 on seed 90210 against bisection's 10/76, and 49/163 at t=3.
- My fix is taps locked to a world lattice along d, with an exact Hopf-Lax minimum over segments. K13 pol2 gives 2/2 on seed 1337 and 18/49 at oct 5. Seed 90210 still counts 6/45, though those panels look clean, and at t=3 K13 pol2 counts 4/45.
- K13 at t=3 looks clean but has 6.8% of pixels wrong, which I read as misplaced shocks, so use K about 3+6t. K21 pol1 gets 0.85% and 4/38.
- Cost: 15 evals for K13 pol2 is still 3x bisection in evals. Scalar is 18.4x vs 10.2x perlin2. No spectral peak at the tap period.

Contraction bound, max compressive slope over 3 seeds, 800^2 samples, window 32:
- Gain .5: .366-.368 oct 1, .273-.304 oct 3 (the prototyper's .32 is high), .230-.240 oct 5, .181-.188 oct 8. The oct 8 value is limited by the finite difference step (h 2e-3), so the true time may be lower.
- Gain .35 saturates: .303-.313 oct 5, .300-.319 oct 8. Gain x lacunarity below 1 is the rule that keeps a usable bound.
- Below the bound, bisection N5 is exact to under 0.02 (rms .0002-.0007). Fixed point is worse at equal evals: N5 rms .001-.003, N2 .010-.026. Above it, it gives no fronts.

High octave FBm: at gain .5 torn shingles appear in every solver, so this is not a root problem. Gain .35 fixes most of it and reads as rocky cuestas, but 5 octaves cost 86.5x perlin2 scalar. The prototyper's recommended graph (steepen octave 1, add detail raw) costs 23.5x, but in relief the fronts largely drown. It is the cheap option, not the better look.

FAULT-LINES: yes, it needs structure, but the strata source is not special. CellularValue through DomainAxisScale with a Perlin fold gives it from stock nodes. True cross-cutting is real and holds on 5 seeds.

Cross-cutting does not need a new node for the look. Six stock chains of DomainRotate, DomainOffset, Multiply, Terrace, DomainAxisScale and Value reproduce it in kind, busier at the settings I ran, at 9.36/14.62/18.34 ns AVX2 over Perlin. I still say ship, because of what the graph cannot do: it needs 36 nodes, has no shared Slip, only slip -1/0/+1, curled stock tips, dip needs inverse rotations, and DomainRotate has no 4D form, so GenTileable2D renders plain stripes.

Zone is not drag: the fault trace vanishes and the layers just fold. My tip and zres parameters make faults end and make layers bend then break, and both clearly improve the look.

CLOSED-LOOP SHEAR FAULTS: no. There are no straight traces, clean offsets or cross-cutting at any setting I tried, on any seed. I partly disagree with the stated reason. The tangential flip explains the serration, but a rigid Y offset across closed Perlin loops is clean and still reads as lenses. Closed curved traces fail on their own, and straightness is what sells a fault. Self mode is not the same as a stock warp (it has hairline creases), but it is untectonic and shear-flow covers that ground. Drop.

COLE-HOPF: I disagree that banding rules it out. Banding came from sliding point-sampled taps. An exact integral over locked taps gives c0ratio 7.97-7.99 and no ripples, the only continuous form of the one-sided profile. Keep it as a Root option on BurgersSteepen.

LIMITS: no real SIMD node was built, so every per-node ns figure is an estimate. 4D and GenTileable2D were not tested on any prototype; only the stock fault graph was rendered tileable. Sheet, thumb, relief and vol were overwritten for burgers and fault-lines; earlier renders remain in the proto folders.

ASIDE, outside this family: in base.dll, CellularValue benches AVX2 10.45 ns against SSE41 6.51 ns in 2D, which seems worth a look.
families.proto_answer:
One-sided fronts: real. BurgersSteepen (v = S(p - t v d), bracketed root) gives smooth windward ramps ending in razor leeward cliffs; the relief is an asymmetric sawtooth that no existing node or graph produces (confirmed on the sheet, relief, and 3D XZ slice). Pinholes: the idea's 5-eval bisection does pick inconsistent roots; measured with a connected-region counter on 256px thumbs: 12 islands / 28 px at t=1.5, 33 / 287 px at t=3, 73 / 177 px on 5-octave FBm; in relief they are isolated pillars. The entropy root (K-tap trapezoid Hopf-Lax scan of the true potential, then 4 bisections in the bracket around the min tap) removes them: K21 leaves 2 px at t=1.5 and turns t=3 into clean merged N-wave sawtooth; K13 leaves 43 px; K9/K7 are no better than bisection. Cost is the catch: K13+N4 is 17 source evals (measured 21.5x perlin2 scalar, estimate ~19/37/73 ns AVX2 on Perlin) versus 5 evals for bisection (10.4x scalar). Contraction bound: breaking time measured from source max slope is t = 0.37 for 1-octave Perlin, 0.32 for 3, 0.23 for 5 octaves (gain .5, lac 2); below it the field is C1 and the fixed point converges, above it every octave shocks at about the same t, so high-octave FBm at t=1.5 becomes torn shingles with many tiny shocks in every root mode. Steepening only the coarse octave(s) and adding fine detail raw keeps the shocked silhouette with intact detail; that should be documented as the intended graph. Cole-Hopf (cole-hopf-dunes) was tested as a mode: with the source as potential (the idea's formulation, K=7) it gives blobby derivative-like cells, not dunes; with the true integrated potential (viscous, K=9..15) it shows tap-spacing banding ripples. Rejected as a separate node; it stays a note under burgers-steepen. Status: promising, the unsolved flaw being that the clean root costs 3-4x the cheap one.

True cross-cutting offsets: real, from FaultLines. Sequential hashed-slab families with the position updated per family give long straight traces where later families visibly offset earlier traces; the strata source reads as a geological cross-section, Density 0.6 (not every slab slips) looks more geological, Zone 0.15-0.35 turns scarps into drag folds, Throw adds a height step per slip so the relief shows fault-block terrain with straight scarps. It needs a structured source: on isotropic 3-octave FBm the faults are barely visible, on Worley F1 they show as cut cells. Residual flaw: a faint per-family parallel lattice in wide views at window 40 even with jitter 0.6 and pre-warp 0.6. 3D form (dipping planes, strike/dip slip) rendered as a volume of stacked offset slabs. Cheap (one dot, floor, 2-3 hashes per family). Status: keeper.

Do closed-loop shear faults read as tectonic? No. FractalShearCascade self mode is a swirly sheared FBm, in kind an eddy warp; with a strata source the octave zero loops at slip 0.1-0.35 serrate the layer edges into wavy saw-tooth bands, larger slip shreds them into curls, and the ridged open-fault variant (|v| = thr) tested this pass at gentle settings gives the same jagged edges. No straight traces, no clean offsets, no cross-cutting at any setting tried. Status: weak. A tangential sign-flipping displacement across a closed loop reads as rotation of the inside against the outside, not slip.

PlateDrift is the family's other keeper: rigid rotated and shifted polygonal plates with real wedge gaps (plate outlines move, unlike F2-F1), 3x3 window audited against 5x5 (0-10 px of 65536 differ for drift 0.15-0.5), TiltedHeight relief is a striking tilted-slab field, full-3D volume is polyhedral rubble; the prototype's extruded 3D ignores z, which a port must fix by passing z to the Lookup source.
challenged: 'mode=5,K=13,N=4 is nearly pinhole free': failed. On the prototyper's own counter it is worse than bisection in all 4 cases run: 25/43 vs 12/28, 134/842 vs 33/287, 172/382 vs 73/177, 34/134 vs 10/76 (islands/px). It is better only on wrong-root area, 0.84% vs 3.71% at t=1.5 on seed 1337.
'The entropy root removes pinholes (K21 leaves 2 px)': true only on seed 1337 at t=1.5. Seed 90210 gives 6 islands/52 px against bisection's 10/76, and t=3 gives 49/163.

The pinhole counts understate bisection. The counter only sees islands of 40 px or less, so 28 px of pinholes sit alongside 3.71% of pixels on the wrong root and 42 thick islands against a converged reference.

'Asymmetric sawtooth that no existing node or graph produces': partly false. A stock Modulus of a tilted plane plus Perlin, added to Perlin, gives one-sided ramps and cliffs at 4.59/7.75/12.60 ns AVX2. What it cannot do is make shocks that start, end, merge and vary in height.

'Breaking time 0.32 for 3 octaves': measured .273-.304 over 3 seeds. The 1 and 5 octave figures hold. The prototyper's list also stops at 5 octaves: it keeps falling to .181-.188 at oct 8 for gain .5, and only saturates below gain x lacunarity 1, for example gain .35 at about .30-.32.

'Steepen the coarse octave and add fine detail raw is the intended graph': it keeps some silhouette, but in relief the fronts largely drown under detail. Gain .35 with all octaves steepened looks clearly better, at 86.5x vs 23.5x perlin2 scalar.
'Banding argues against even a viscous option': failed. Banding came from sliding point-sampled taps. An exact segment integral over locked taps gives c0ratio 7.97-7.99 and no ripples.
'Zone .15-.35 turns scarps into drag folds': the image shows the fault trace gone and the layers simply folding. Real drag needs a residual jump, which is what the new zres parameter adds.
'Throw gives fault-block terrain with tilted blocks': the code adds only a height step per slab, with no per-block tilt, and the image reads as rugged hills with thin scarps.
'Faint per-family parallel lattice in wide views': not reproduced. I could not see it or in my own window 32 renders. The visible limit is 6 orientations.

The idea's claim that graphs cannot make slip discontinuities or cross-cutting offsets: false. A stock DomainRotate, DomainOffset, Terrace chain does both. The node's case rests on usability, dip, tips and 4D, not on the look.

'3x3 window audited: 0-10 px': seed flattering. Seed 90210 gives 13 of 65536 at default settings and 63 at drift .3 rot .8 gap .15, with max diff .85. These are tiny clipped pieces, so the window is still fine with drift clamped.
'Unlike F2-F1 the gap width varies': a stock F2-F1 with a per plate threshold also gives uneven gaps and a close mask silhouette. The real difference is rotation, per-plate texture and tilted slabs.
'Full 3D plate cost ~80-100 ns': scalar measured 10.4x worley3 implies about 125 ns against the 12 ns handbook figure. This is an estimate, not a SIMD measurement.

'A tangential flip across a closed loop reads as rotation' as the reason shear faults fail: incomplete. A rigid offset across closed loops has no rotation, stays clean, and still reads as lenses. Closed curved traces fail on their own.

'Self mode is in kind the same as DomainWarpGradient or a curl warp': the DomainWarpGradient, Progressive and Independent graphs I rendered have no such hairline creases. It is still not worth a node, because shear-flow covers that ground.
kernels: Strata source: random-brightness layers of a folded depth coordinate (Strata(h) = lerp(rnd11(hash(i)), rnd11(hash(i+1)), smoothstep edge) with h = y + fold*perlin), used by fault-lines and shear-cascade as the structured test source; worth a tiny built-in or documented graph since both offset nodes need it to show.
1D line search over a source along a direction (S(s) = Source(p - s d)): burgers bisection, Hopf-Lax entropy scan and Cole-Hopf all share it, dimension agnostic.
Polygonal gauge in a candidate frame (g_i = max_j 2 (p_i - c_i).(c_j - c_i)/|c_j - c_i|^2, from rel_gauge) used by plate-drift; dot products only in the inner loop.
Sequential hashed-slab displacement (dot, floor, hash of (slab, family), position update per family) used by fault-lines; could also drive a Throw-only height-step mode.

families.answer: The family holds up better than most, with one disagreement on node shape. TileDomain is the real find: nothing in the catalogue gives brick, hex, herringbone or fan paving, every pattern reads as the material, and I reproduced the continuity claim myself (all 9 patterns with Bevel 0.1, Smooth profile, Random rotation and Mortar 0.05: c0ratio 7.93-7.98, range -1..1, no z jump in 3D; the Round profile is a rim at 3.0-3.4, as stated). The resolved speed table also reproduced (grid 5.5 ns to fan 60.9 ns). Ship it, with the caveat that it is a very large node (about 25 params, 4 enums) and the headline 3.06x Perlin is the parquet only; the fan cobbles recipe with its source reads 12.8x in the speed command. Textile ships for the weave half: plain, twill, satin and wire mesh are immediately cloth, continuity and speed re-measure as claimed (twill prof=1 7.97; 1.45x Perlin resolved, 7.3x via the speed command). The knit half is weaker than reported: at seed 5 window 16 it reads as twisted-rope columns and vertical ribbing, not stockinette. LevelSetWeave is correctly merged: the Textile weave on two Worley F1 fields reproduces it (c0ratio 8.05 with prof=1) and the woven rings are the best image, so Textile should take optional A/B coordinate sources. FiberNoise: the fur holds at a fresh seed and nothing else gives line features with free ends, but the fur recipe costs 26x Perlin in the speed command and the streak path shows a plain K-arm star in the FFT and reads as pick-up-sticks at a wide window; ship with the Layers path as the cheap default and treat K=6 capsule fur as showcase. StreakScatter is the Layers mode, agreed. HEIGHT-BLEND VS FADE: the look claim is true and the graph claim is true. On the same two sources Fade is a double exposure while HeightBlend keeps both materials crisp with the border following the features; and the Fade(A, B, Fade=Add(Subtract(HB,HA), 2*Control)) graph is identical by eye (my pair-3 re-render at seed 3 with a noise control). The new fact is cost measured on real nodes: fnlab AVX2 bench, two 4-octave fractals, plain Fade 10.0 / 23.0 / 38.2 ns (2D/3D/4D), the HeightBlend graph 21.4 / 48.7 / 68.6 ns, and the graph with GeneratorCache on every source 21.9 / 51.1 / 72.2 ns, so the cache does not rescue it and a native version would be about 2x cheaper. That earns the feature, but it is Fade with a height-aware weight, so I disagree with a separate node: add optional Height A / Height B hybrids and a Depth to Fade (ship-as-mode of Fade). TileSplit was not prototyped here and I did not score it. 4D was not run by either of us; I did not view two of the prototyper's discovery images (combed hair, hook wisps), so those are unverified by me.
families.proto_answer:
The family gives four real material tools: TileDomain, Textile, FiberNoise and HeightBlend. HeightBlend is a keeper for cost and ease only, because a graph reaches nearly the same look. LevelSetWeave merges into Textile and StreakScatter becomes FiberNoise's cheap path. TileSplit was not prototyped here. Its cracks-family entry stands, and I suggest its KD splits become an option on TileDomain's box patterns.

TILE-DOMAIN ENUM CONTINUITY (table)
- Method: jumps were found by bisecting any sampled difference down to float resolution, with a jump threshold of 0.02.
- Patterns: all 9 enums were tested (Grid, RunningBond, Basket, Herringbone, Hex, Chevron, Courses, Scales, Fan), 15 configs in all, including N=2/3/5 and maximum jitter.
- EdgeDistance: no jump on any pattern.
- Value outputs without Bevel: Lookup, TileValue, TiltedHeight, LocalU and LocalV jump by 1.0 to 2.0 at tile edges. That is by design for a tiling.
- Value outputs with Bevel 0.1: no jump on any pattern or output.
- Rotation None, Quarter and Random, with Bevel 0.1 and Mortar 0.05: no jump on any pattern.
- Mortar without Bevel: jumps 1.9 to 2.0, by design.
- 3D with Z Length, along z: no jump.
- Bevel Profile enum, c0ratio from the check command: Round 2.26 to 2.78 (infinite rim slope, not a jump, since the bisection finds none), Smooth 7.93 to 7.98, Linear 8.00.
- Edge distance is exact. Over 30000 points per config, Lipschitz is 1.000 to 1.005, there are no id collisions, and a move of 1.15e always found the tile edge. A move of 0.95e changed tile on at most 2 points per config, all at tiny e, which I attribute to float or angle-polynomial noise.
- Period closes on all tested configs: worst error 0.001, Fan 0.010, at P=24. Herringbone N=5 was left out because 24 is not a multiple of 2N.
- Only Fan failed at first: 201 inside failures, Lipschitz 1.246, and residual jumps of 0.075 and 0.132 on a 0.1 bevel. Three fixes cleared it: an atan polynomial whose octants meet at 45 degrees, an edge of rho*sin instead of arc length, and a rigid frame. A per-ring and per-fan phase then removed straight horizontal seam lines.

HEIGHT-BLEND VS FADE
- On the same two sources, Fade is a double exposure: ghost pebbles fogged over sand, and rock fading into soil.
- HeightBlend keeps full contrast on both sides, and the boundary follows the features. Pebbles stay whole, sand fills the gaps first, and moss fills mortar before it climbs the bricks.
- Fade on Control plus noise is also crisp, but it slices pebbles in half.
- The caveat from the earlier run: a graph Fade(A, B, Fade = Add(Subtract(HB, HA), Multiply(2, Control)), FadeMin = 1 - Depth, FadeMax = 1 + Depth) reproduces the look, with max difference 0.118 and std about 0.016 on all 4 pairs.
- So the node's value is 1.64x to 1.71x less scalar cost (sources not re-evaluated), clearer parameters and a composite height output, not an impossible look. I re-ran its check on the earlier binary and it reproduces c0ratio 6.62 and range -0.592..0.986.

THE OTHER NODES
- Textile: plain, twill and satin read immediately as cloth, and thin threads make a convincing wire mesh. The polyline-table knit reads as stockinette, slightly rope-like up close, at 1.81x Perlin scalar against the catalogue's 17x. 3D gives real interlocking tubes.
- LevelSetWeave: the Textile weave on the same A and B fields gives nearly the same plain-weave image and adds twill and satin, so it should be two optional Textile sources.
- FiberNoise: capsules on a field Angle make excellent fur, but K=6 costs 17.73x Perlin scalar. The streak path gives the same long fibres at 5.55x against 17.23x for a 5x5 capsule window, measured. Its cost is an orientation star in the FFT, which jitter spreads but does not remove.

The nodes also compose: brushed plates, patchwork and thatch all work as TileDomain with a family node as Source.

Not done: 4D was not run for any idea in this pass, and no real SIMD node was built, so every AVX2 figure is an estimate. The speed command figures include Params map lookups, so for tile-domain, textile and fiber-noise I also give scalar timings with the config resolved once.
challenged: TileDomain 'the speed command reads 2.98x-5.13x': the fan cobbles recipe with its fbm source reads 12.79x Perlin in the speed command (fan alone with out=EdgeDistance reads 5.12x); the 3.06x headline is the parquet config only.

Textile knit 'reads as chunky stockinette': at seed 5, window 16, it reads as twisted-rope columns and vertical ribbing, and the wide view is plain vertical stripes; thinner yarn turns it into chain-link, not knit.

FiberNoise fur cost is understated in the summary: the fur recipe (path=0, K=6, field angle) measures 26.1x Perlin in the speed command; the report quotes only the resolved 17.7x and a 14.5x speed figure for K=2.
LevelSetWeave headline c0ratio 7.96 does not belong to its recipe params: src=4,k=1.2,cell=0.3,mode=1 measures 2.99 (round-profile rim); 7.96-8.05 is reached only with prof=1 or the Textile mode.

HeightBlend '1.64x to 1.71x less cost': with real nodes in fnlab AVX2 the saving is larger, about 2.1x in 2D (21.4 vs 10.0 ns) and 1.8-2.1x in 3D/4D; and the GeneratorCache remark, which the prototyper only read from code, is now measured: wrapping every source in GeneratorCache gives 21.9 ns vs 21.4 ns, no saving.
kernels: Tile lookup: one small window-free function per pattern returning (id, u, v, e, hu, hv), with common post-processing for bevel, mortar, rotation and outputs. TileSplit's KD split could operate on any box pattern's result.
Continuous polynomial atan (FanAtan in tile_core.h): the lab atan polynomial scaled by 1.00025877 so the 45 degree octants meet, needed when an angle drives an edge distance.
Thread height rule: profile(u)*(0.5+0.5*A*z) with Max, which is C0 without occlusion logic. It is the Textile weave and the knit, and the same idea as the level-set-weave formula.
Tapered capsule stamp: width and amplitude both taper to 0 at the tips, so reach is L rather than L+W and the result is C0. Used by both FiberNoise paths and in 2D and 3D.
Layered stretched lattice with a per-stamp lateral budget: the 2x2 window stays exact because jitter and bend are clamped from the remaining reach.

families.answer:
No. Plains with rough peaks at FBm cost is real, but the premise that a graph cannot make it is false. I do not think FractalMultifractal should ship.

**Why the graph claim fails.** FractalFBm's Gain and Weighted Strength are hybrid inputs, and the prototyper did not test either at the settings that matter. Its only existing-node baseline was WS 0.8 at gain 0.5, the weak end of that node.

Roughness in the top height quintile divided by the bottom quintile (same noise, seeds 1337, 7, 42, 99, window 5):

| Field | Top/bottom | Correlation to Hetero |
|---|---|---|
| FBm | 1.0 | 0.951 |
| FBm WS.8 g.5 (prototyper baseline) | 2.5 | 0.987 |
| FBm g.84 WS1 | 8.8 | 0.987 |
| Hybrid g.84 | 10.7 | 0.956 |
| FBm g1 WS1 | 12.4 | 0.969 |
| Hetero | 14.1 | 1.000 |
| Hetero via PowFloat(e, FBm) graph | 15.4 | 0.994 |
| FBm Gain=Remap(same-seed Simplex) | 19.5 | 0.991 |

The PowFloat graph tracks Hetero's roughness at every height, within about 8%. Same-seed reliefs at 99 and 2024 read the same.

**Real AVX2 cost, ns 2D/3D/4D, single runs:**
- FBm: 7.23 / 12.73 / 18.64
- FBm g.84 WS1: 7.28 / 12.67 / 18.67, the same cost with no graph
- FBm Gain=Remap: 8.56 / 15.54 / 29.56, about +18% in 2D. The 4D figure looks noisy.
- Same plus MaxSmooth floor: 9.33 / 16.38 / 30.21
- Exact Hetero graph: 10.84 / 20.38 / 25.34

Real `check` on the MaxSmooth recipe: 0 FAIL, 3 WARN (range target, plus the 3D and 4D continuity jumps the handbook flags for Simplex). It has no parity, tiling or far-coordinate problem.

**The best plains image comes from real nodes.** Hetero's lowlands are smooth bowls, not plains. FBm Gain=Remap plus MaxSmooth gives actual flats with isolated rough peaks, and looks better than Hetero.

**Range table.**
- The 2D numbers reproduce exactly at the prototyper's seed.
- Other seeds exceed them, so they are not bounds. At seed 5, p-model inter 1.5 reaches 6.77 against 6.31, and Hetero 6 octaves reaches 5.45.
- "No analytic range" is wrong for Hetero. The bound (1+off)*Prod(1+a_i(1+off)) gives 4.48 / 6.01 / 6.59 / 14.08 against measured 4.31 / 5.27 / 5.42 / 10.77.
- The table does not carry to 3D. With off .7 on the lab simplex3g (range -0.70..0.70, std 0.274), Hetero 5 octaves has 0.00% of samples below zero, min about 0, max 3.35-3.48, so the prototype has no smooth floor regime in 3D. Real 3D Simplex was not measured for this.

**Other claims.**
- "Flat voids of all sizes" is false at gain .5. Inter 1.5 cuts voids only in octave 0 (14.2% of area). Inter 2.5 cuts in octave 0 (28.3%) and octave 1 (6.9%), and all other octaves are exactly 0%.
- Real multi-scale voids need gain about .7, and that costs clean continuity: c0ratio 3.5-4.4.
- RidgedMulti is fine to drop, since FractalRidged g.7 WS1 is close. The prototyper's image compared it to FBm Weighted rather than FractalRidged, so I rendered the real comparison.

**Root vein.** New defaults that hold up: `bf=0.5,bfreq=3,w=0.07,bw=0.6,reach=0.5,rough=0.5,oct=3,octdrop=1,tiers=3,floor=0.3,side=0.2,gap=0.3,gapf=1,tipw=0.3`.

| Px per vein spacing | Old speck % | New speck % |
|---|---|---|
| 128 | 5.74 | 1.91 |
| 64 | 11.28 | 4.86 |
| 32 | 21.45 | 11.16 |

Speck is the share of bright pixels with at most one bright neighbour, seed 1337; seed 42 gives similar new values. c0ratio rose from 3.67 to 7.28, and max slope fell from 502 to 141. At 32 px it reads as short dashes, not fine strands, and it is still not good there.

Calls: multifractal graph-recipe, percolation graph-recipe, root-vein showcase.
families.proto_answer: Yes: Musgrave's Heterogeneous mode gives plains with rough peaks at exactly FBm cost, and a graph cannot build it. Evidence: (1) same-seed reliefs at seeds 1337 and 7 show Hetero with a glassy flat lowland floor and busy sharp summits, while plain FBm is uniformly rough and the existing FBm Weighted Strength 0.8 only mildly smooths its lows; Hybrid at Musgrave H=0.25 (gain 0.84) gives dense jagged spires on smooth flats. (2) Cost measured in one binary, 6 octaves of simplex2: FBm 558.1 ns, Hetero 560.6, Hybrid 558.4, Multiplicative 561.1 (11.2x perlin2 for all), so the modes are free relative to FractalFBm. (3) Range table measured (8 seeds, 256^2, window 16): Hetero off .7 gain .5 min -0.299 (= off-1 exactly) max 4.31/5.27/5.42 at 3/5/8 octaves mean 1.27, gain .65 max 10.8; Hybrid gain .5 -0.6..2.85 and unchanged past 3 octaves (weights collapse, so gain .84 is the right default: -1.63..5.99); p-model inter 1: 0..3.85 mean 1.00, inter 1.5: 0..6.3; lognormal sigma 1: 0.09..2.9.
