All modes are heavy-tailed, so the node needs VariableRange with these as defaults (a linear remap puts the mean near -0.4) or a knee output v/(v+1) for the product modes. c0ratio 7.9 (6.4 at 8 octaves from steepness, not jumps). The multiplicative-cascade test: the p-model is the same formula as Musgrave's multiplicative mode with an intermittency scale and a Max(0) floor, and at inter 1.5-2.5 it gives exact flat voids of all sizes; the lognormal cascade is exp(FBm), graphable with PowFloat, so it should not be a mode. Percolation-fractal turned out to be the same cascade with step weights (its mask next to the p-model shows the same hard voids) and its mask aliases to static at any normal feature scale, so it merges into the multifractal as a Weight {Linear, Step} option. Root-vein defaults that do not turn to static: bf 0.5 (one primary vein per 2 units), bfreq 3, w 0.05, reach 0.5, rough 0.5, bw 0.5; measured good at 64-128 px per primary vein spacing (window 8 and 16), static at 32 px (window 32), and bf 2 at window 8 is static; rough 0 gives smooth tendrils with hair roots, rough 2 is fuzz. It is promising, not a keeper: 11.5-13x perlin, c0ratio 3.7 from the finest lines, and the branchlets cross the parent vein rather than sprout from it.
challenged: 'A graph cannot build it' is false. FractalFBm with Gain=Remap(same-seed Simplex) gives top/bottom roughness 19.5 against Hetero's 14.1, correlation 0.991, at 8.56 ns against 7.23 AVX2 2D. FBm g.84 WS1 gives 8.8 at 7.28 ns with no graph. Hetero via PowFloat(e, FBm) gives correlation 0.994 and a nearly matching roughness curve.
'FBm Weighted only mildly smooths its lows' holds only at gain .5 WS .8 (ratio 2.5), which was the only setting compared. The same node at gain 1 WS 1 reaches 12.4.

'Glassy flat lowland floor' overstates it. Hetero's lowlands are smooth bowls of the first octave. Actual flats need a floor such as MaxSmooth, and the real-node recipe with a floor looks better than Hetero.
'No analytic range' is false for Hetero. The bound gives 4.48 / 6.01 / 6.59 / 14.08 against measured 4.31 / 5.27 / 5.42 / 10.77.
Range-table defaults are not bounds. At seed 5, p-model inter 1.5 reaches 6.77 against 6.31, Hetero 6 octaves reaches 5.45, and Hybrid g.84 spans -1.46..6.05 against -1.63..5.99.

The range table is 2D only. With off .7 on the lab simplex3g, Hetero has 0.00% of samples below zero and max about 3.4 in 3D, so the prototype's defaults do not carry over. Real 3D Simplex was not measured.
'Flat voids of all sizes' is false at gain .5. Measured area with a zero factor: inter 1.5 only octave 0 (14.2%); inter 2.5 octave 0 (28.3%) and octave 1 (6.9%); all others 0%.

Cascade-mesas as a look 'neither FBm, ridged nor the other modes give' is not a reason for a node. A real graph of clamped Remap, PowFloat and Divide reads as the same genre at seed 99, though it costs 22.55 ns AVX2 2D with the subtree duplicated.
'Merge percolation into a Weight option' is unnecessary. The Mask is three clamped Remaps in two Multiply nodes at 5.62 ns AVX2 2D.
The RidgedMulti comparison image pits it against FBm Weighted (mode 6), not FractalRidged, so it does not show what was claimed. The conclusion survives: real FractalRidged g.7 WS1 is close.

Root-vein 'needs about 100 px or more per primary spacing' applied to the old defaults. With the new defaults speck at 64 px is 4.86% against 11.28%, and it stays readable. Branches crossing the parent and the closed web were treated as inherent, but both are fixable with side and gap.

Scalar ratios are weak cost evidence in these prototypes. Root-vein going from 10 to 7 evals only moved 644 to 516 ns, so 560 vs 558 ns says little by itself. The real-node bench is what supports the cost statements.
kernels: Fixed-octave cascade loop over Source with per-octave precomputed amplitudes (Fractal.inl shape) shared by multifractal Hetero/Hybrid/Multiplicative and the percolation step-weight product
Knee density output v/(v+knee) for unit-mean product fields
Perlin value+gradient kernel (perlin2 derivative / perlin3g) for root-vein, shared with fractal-derivative

families.answer:
STEERABLE PERLIN (#159): build it, as its own node. The flow-aligned grain is real and not a cherry-pick: at seed 7 and a 24 unit window it is the same even combed grain with no lattice, the threshold is feathered flames, the FFT is radial. I reproduced the checks (c0ratio 7.99, scalar 7.1x perlin2 at 4 octaves, aspect 3.04-3.15 flat across angles with the prototyper's measurement tool). I also rendered the obvious existing-node rival with fnlab, DomainRotate + DomainAxisScale(.33) + FractalFBm 4 Perlin, and it matches the constant-angle steerable sheet almost exactly, so at a constant direction this is a graph recipe. The node's value is entirely the per-lane direction hybrid, which no existing node or graph can do (a spatially varying DomainRotate is a warp, not a local anisotropy). Where I go further than the prototyper: the lattice envelope is the main quality flaw (cellVarMax/Min 21x at one octave, 5.3x at four), and dividing each octave by its own expected std, computed from the same per-corner terms, cuts that to 2.1x and 1.6x with the aspect unchanged, at one FMA per corner plus one rsqrt per octave; it sharpens the grain (max slope 15 to 37) and flattens the histogram, so it should be an option, not the default. Agreed limits: aspect caps near 3 with the 2x2 window, 3D fibres are a sponge while sheets are torn slabs (re-checked at seed 7), octaves must be internal because a FractalFBm parent would sample the direction hybrid at scaled positions. AVX2 cost claims were not re-measured here; the scalar ratios reproduced.

WAVE NOISE COST: both figures are right for different configurations, as the prototyper says, but I disagree about which configuration counts. The N=8 default that gives the 5-8x figure is not clean: at a 24-32 unit window the blobs line up in straight chains along the 8 wave directions, in 2D and in the XZ slice; N=12 is fainter and N=16 reads isotropic. So the honest cost of a usable Real output is N=16 sliced, 12.5-15 ns in the prototyper's own AVX2 table, about 9-11x real Perlin in 2D (falling to about 3x in 4D because the cost is flat across dimensions). That is nearer the 13x claim than the 4-6x one. The 4-6x figure holds only for plain unsliced N=16 sincos, which has a dot-ring FFT and visible long-lag correlation. Harmonics (M=3) cost 25-32 ns and look like fish scales, so the 13x figure is also not the worst case. I did not re-run the AVX2 harness; the scalar ratios (2.36x at N=8) match.

Family verdicts: steerable-perlin ship. wave-noise-sliced showcase: Wired needles and the labyrinth-to-stripes dial are striking and new, but Real is Perlin with a narrower band and Ridged is the same net and the same 3D membrane foam as FractalRidged(Octaves=1, Source=Simplex) at iso .5, which I rendered. wave-noise drop (merged, nothing earns a mode). cyclic-noise showcase: the relief is the second best image of the family, but the final form has a global diagonal shear bias that every seed and every decorS setting shares, so it is a preset-grade look, not a general node.
families.proto_answer:
STEERABLE PERLIN (#159): yes, build it. The flow-aligned grain is real. Measured grain aspect (correlation length along / across): Perlin control 1.02, metric in the projection only 1.93, adding the paper's second weight 2.88, and 3.0-3.3 at 4 octaves. It stays flat across 7 angles (std .275-.281), so the grain does not depend on the angle relative to the lattice. Estimated cost from hand-written AVX2 kernels, not a node: 1.40 / 2.89 / 7.05 ns per octave, 2.0x / 2.4x Perlin in the same harness (2D/3D; 4D has no same-harness Perlin to compare).

It has real limits:
- The 2x2 window caps aspect near 3, and going below k=.5 barely helps (3.6) while lattice imprint rises from 21-31x to as much as 105x.
- At a constant direction it is close to DomainAxisScale. Its value is in a spatially varying direction.
- Octaves must be internal. Emulating a FractalFBm parent destroyed the flow.
- 3D fibres are weak (aspect 2.1, reads as an ordinary sponge). 3D sheets are better (3.3, torn laminated slabs).
- 4D was only timed, never run as a function.
- Strong warps of stretched FBm make longer lines, but with varying width, moire and no choice of direction. It is a different look, not a strictly better one.

Licence: the code follows Algorithm 1 and section 3.1 of the paper (DOI 10.1145/3721239.3734101), checked line by line, and I did not fetch the unlicensed repo. It is not a clean room, though: I read the catalogue entry and protos/dem_steer, both derived from that shader, before the paper. I also did not read the paper's supplemental, so the closed-form metric and octave loop are not from the paper. Write the port fresh from the paper and supplemental.

WAVE NOISE COST: both claims are right, for different configurations. Single-thread hand-written AVX2 kernels, ns/sample 2D/3D/4D:
- N=16 plain sincos: 7.00 / 7.37 / 8.35
- N=16 phase-only slices: 13.31 / 13.68 / 15.32
- N=16 tilted slices: sincos 20.66 / 21.33 / 22.06, parabola 15.38 / 15.58 / 15.68
- N=16 M=3 harmonics, phase slices: 31.99 / 32.47 / 33.23
- N=8 tilted parabola (chosen default): 7.75 / 7.88 / 8.04

Real Perlin AVX2 measured 0.90-1.51 / 2.10-2.22 / 4.11-4.26 over 6 runs, so 2D ratios carry a wide error. That puts plain N=16 at 4.6-7.8x (the 4-6x claim), N=16 phase slices at 8.8-14.8x and N=16 tilted parabola at 10-17x (the 13x claim), and N=16 M=3 at 21-36x, worse than either claim. These are estimates of a node. My harness Perlin reads .70, faster than the real node, so a port will cost somewhat more. The default is 5.1-8.6x Perlin in 2D but only about 3.6x in 3D and 1.9x in 4D, because the cost is flat across dimensions (+3.7 percent 2D to 4D), and it is below FBm 6 octaves in 3D (13.24) and 4D (25.30).

I found no derivation of the 13x figure beyond the queue line. The deck's own table, slide 29, is a GPU figure comparing against FRACTAL Perlin with octaves, units and hardware not shown, so it is not comparable: 50 directions run about 2x its fractal Perlin. Its precomputed profile does not transfer to AVX2, where 16 complex gathers cost 26.68 ns against 7.00 for sincos. I read the talk deck, not the TOG paper.

Verdict on the family: steerable-perlin keeper. wave-noise-sliced keeper for narrow-band outputs only (Wired needles, Ridged foam, order dial), not as a general spectral noise, since broad band needs about N=32 (about 30 ns) and harmonics do not beat FBm on look. wave-noise merged. cyclic-noise promising.

Evidence note: only the newest few images and PDFs stay visible to me, and older results show as removed. Looks I describe were logged straight after viewing, but most cannot be re-inspected now. The later CORRECTION TO THE CORRECTIONS line supersedes them. All 4 result.json files list images that exist.
challenged: wave-noise-sliced: 'Real N=8 ... no lattice in the wide view' and 'N=8 tilt .5 is the new default'. At seed 7, window 24-32, N=8 shows the blobs lined up in straight chains along the 8 wave directions in both 2D and the XZ slice; N=16 is needed, which moves the cost to 12.5-15 ns by the prototyper's own table.

wave-noise-sliced: 'Ridged ... 3D thin membrane foam, the best 3D result of the family'. FractalRidged(Octaves=1, Source=Simplex) at iso .5 rendered with fnlab gives the same membrane foam and the same 2D closed-loop net. It is an existing graph.

wave-noise-sliced: the Wired wide panel 'one faint horizontal line' is wave 0 being exactly axis aligned (angle -90 degrees); at seed 7 window 32 it is a long bright row across the whole field. A half-step offset of the direction table removes it.
wave-noise cost answer: 'the default is 5.1-8.6x Perlin in 2D'. That default is the N=8 configuration with visible direction chains; the clean configuration is about 9-11x.

cyclic-noise: 'the final form ... removes the rows (r .072)'. The rows are gone, but at seed 7 window 32 the whole field is sheared along one diagonal at decorS 6, 9 and 14 alike, so seeds still share a fabric direction fixed by the slice axes.

cyclic-noise: 'reads as different from warp graphs'. Different from the two graphs the prototyper rendered, but the existing Warp Fractal Progressive panel on the existing-nodes sheet is the same wispy-marbling family without the shear bias; the gap is smaller than reported.
kernels: Parabola sincos in cycles: one reduction per output, used by wave and cyclic, saving about 25 percent in tilted wave form and about 40 percent in cyclic, at the price of a faint harmonic at 3f
slice1: 2 hashes and a quintic lerp, a 1D value noise along an oblique axis; decorrelates any periodic field, used by wave global warp and cyclic
Closed-form uniaxial metric G v = e1 v + (e0-e1)(d.v) d with v'Gv reused, dimension agnostic, for steerable-perlin
Compact crest (1 - k(1-v))^4 instead of repeated squaring, which avoids a measured 2.5x denormal penalty
Direction lattice: K nearest of Nv fixed wave vectors, weighted by a smooth bump in angle, for per-lane steering of plane waves

families.answer:
Light cone CA: confirmed as a real pointwise CA, and tested harder than asked. My own brute force used a separately written hash, hand-listed B/S sets, new seeds, origins up to 40000 and -123456, and fractional positions. It covered gens 0-14 in 2D and gens 1-3 in 3D: 98896 cells, 0 mismatches. Pyramid mode, which the prototyper never tested, is also exact: 81920 cells, 0 mismatches. My branch-free AVX2 port matches the scalar version exactly, 0 of 16000 samples differ.

I disagree on what that is worth. The port measures 29.6 ns at gens=4, 33x AVX2 Perlin, so the quoted 3x scalar ratio misleads (scalar perlin2 spends ~50 ns on cos/sin). The prototyper compared against 3-octave FBm. Against one octave of SuperSimplex x20 clamped (2.79 ns, passes fnlab check), the blobs are nearly the same. 3D is no better than a SuperSimplex isosurface at 3.9 ns. I tried 8 more rules and an age output and none rescued it. Call: graph-recipe, not a node.

Spanning-maze: connectivity holds. Union-find found 0 cycles everywhere in 2D, 3D and 4D, with exactly 1 component in block-aligned 2D and 3D windows. Flood fill on rendered thresholds found 0 enclosed pieces in both phases over new seeds, windows straddling 0, far coords and thresholds +-0.6. 3D at 128^3 has the wall phase as 1 piece and 0 enclosed corridor pieces. Measured AVX2 is 9.9 ns as prototyped (mean of two runs, port matches scalar on 0 of 80000 differing) and 5.4 ns with one hash per edge (a different maze, also 0 enclosed over 3 seeds).

I disagree on three points:
- "Hidden by any warp" is false. Warp 0.3 at f0.5 still shows row banding at window 24 (FFT axis 52).
- The guarantee survives only near-injective warps. Warp 0.6 at f0.5 gives 34 corridor and 62 wall enclosed pieces, warp 0.3 at f1.0 gives 25 corridor.
- The 4D form gives no usable tile. On the GenTileable2D torus it is window-pane fragments, 161 enclosed corridor pieces, largest 1.6%.

A low-frequency two-scale warp plus capped distances fixes the first two: axis 14, 0 enclosed, no junction spikes. No existing-node graph I built matched the look or the topology. Still the keeper: ship, with native tiling unsolved.

Hilbert: the prototyper is right (4 enclosed, largest 11%). Drop.

Barchan-field: it does sell a desert, more than the prototyper said. The fin look was largely the terrain ramp: the same params under a sand ramp and side sun read as barchans. The dead-flat plain was a real fault. Faded spatial supply, wind variation, swell and interdune ripple fix it, and swarms with bare corridors now look right from the air and in oblique relief. Dunes are still stamped copies, dense areas overlap rather than form true barchanoid ridges, and the 3D form is only a crossfade.

Two of its numbers do not hold. AVX2 is 20-22 ns measured against the 6-8 ns estimate. A hybrid Sand Supply as prototyped seams (c0ratio 1.02) until each dune fades instead of switching on (8.06). Call: showcase.

Prototypes changed only by adding params whose defaults keep the old behaviour; originals saved as *.prev.cpp.
families.proto_answer: Light cone CA is a real pointwise cellular automaton: a brute-force grid CA run from the same hashed initial state (verify.exe) matched the pointwise light-cone evaluation in every cell over 8 configurations (2D gens 3-8 with cave/maze/coral/life rules, 3D gens 1-2 with 26-neighbour thresholds), 0 mismatches of ~78k cells. Judged on the look afterwards, the cave rule gives clean rounded blobs that differ only modestly from a soft-thresholded FBm; the pyramid mode gives a distinctive chunky fractal coast but costs ~31x Perlin scalar; the maze rule does not converge within an affordable window. Promising, not keeper. Spanning-maze connectivity was checked by flood fill on rendered thresholds: 1200 px over 96 units, 3 seeds, kd and quadtree rules, warp 0 and 0.3: 0 enclosed pieces in both phases (only 0-6 sub-6px rasterisation specks when warped); block-aligned 32x32-cell windows: the corridor phase is exactly 1 piece in 6/6 cases; 3D 8^3 block: corridor 1 piece in 2/2, and 160^3 voxel windows have the wall phase as 1 piece and 0 enclosed corridor pieces. The Hilbert comparison looks almost the same after a warp but has no branches, dead-ends at block borders and 4 enclosed corridor pieces, so it is not worth a mode. Spanning-maze is the keeper of the family (3.6x Perlin scalar, 2D and 3D from one dimension-generic rule, 3D isosurface is a tree of square pipes). Barchan-field partly sells a desert: from above the aligned crescents with sharp brinks, trailing horns and slip faces read as barchans immediately; in the relief view they read as crescent fins on a dead-flat plain, and the dense Max composition stacks crescents like scales rather than merging them into barchanoid ridges. Promising; the 3D form is a time crossfade, not migration. No discoveries were saved: nothing accidental was striking enough to claim.
challenged: spanning-maze: 'hidden by any warp'. The shown warp 0.3 f0.5 leaves plain row and column banding at window 24 (FFT axis 52).

spanning-maze: the topology guarantee is only safe for near-injective warps. Warp 0.6 f0.5 gives 34 corridor and 62 wall enclosed pieces, warp 1.0 gives 864 and 497, warp 0.3 f1.0 gives 25 corridor. The prototyper tested only warp 0 and 0.3 at f0.5, where its numbers do hold.

spanning-maze: '4D is the same code path' holds for the rule (0 cycles in 4D) but gives no tile. The GenTileable2D torus slice is window-pane fragments with 161 enclosed corridor pieces, largest 1.6%. Any 2D slice of the 3D form has the same problem.
barchan-field: est_avx2 6-8 ns. Measured 20-22 ns with ripple, 16.3 ns without, using an AVX2 port that agrees with scalar (worst difference 0.00005).
barchan-field: Sand Supply as a hybrid with binary existence seams, c0ratio 1.02 and max slope 614. Fading each dune by sat((supply-rnd)/w) restores c0ratio 8.06.
barchan-field: 'crescent fins' is largely the terrain colour ramp. The same params in a sand ramp with a side sun read as barchans. The flat plain complaint was correct.
light-cone-ca: scalar_vs_perlin 3.06 misleads. AVX2 gens=4 is 29.6 ns measured, 33x AVX2 Perlin at 0.90 ns.
light-cone-ca: 'real but modest difference' came from a 3-octave FBm baseline. One octave of SuperSimplex x20 clamped (2.79 ns) nearly erases it.
light-cone-ca: pyramid est 60-100 ns looks 2-3x low. My estimate is ~205 ns, scalar 1577 ns divided by the measured 7.7 scalar/AVX2 ratio.
light-cone-ca: 'no specks after 3-4 gens'. Faint gray single-cell dots remain at gens 4. Minor.
kernels: Hashed-lattice 3^D window loop with per-cell Select masks (spanning-maze edges, barchan dunes); same shape as Cellular.inl
Axis-aligned segment / face distance in D dims (spanning-maze dPath/dWall, Hilbert corridor)
Bit-sliced neighbour counting over int32 rows (light-cone-ca 2D and 3D); reusable for any lattice boolean rule
Faded polynomial smooth max that stays 0 at ground: smax = max + h^2 k/4 * sat(min(a,b)/k) (barchan; applies to any kernel-splat Max composition)
Flood-fill connectivity harnesses (2D render + 3D voxel, block-aligned mode) and verify.cpp (brute-force CA agreement)

families.answer:
Prove or kill, on look alone: knot-field is proved on look and killed as a noise node; coral-noise is proved on its showpiece (growth) and is a bake or hero object, not a building block; newton-basins is neither striking enough nor clean enough and I would drop it. I disagree with the prototyper on the overall framing of three keepers: only two deserve to be kept, and both as showcases.

knot-field: the vol view decides in its favour as an image. The fibre bundle (mode 8) is the best picture in the family, the trefoil and cinquefoil tubes are clean constant-radius knots, and a seed 7 bundle looks like seed 0, so it was not cherry-picked. The P=2,Q=2 Hopf-link and P=5,Q=2 bundles also render well. But it is one centred object: my vol at window 10 is a small pom-pom in an empty cube, the 2D whirl at window 16 is one spiral whose scales grow to screen size away from the centre, and the check with the hero tube params returns -1 everywhere (c0ratio 0.00, std 0), because the field is a constant except at one spot. The bundle wire discontinuity is real (c0ratio 1.53, max slope 514). AVX2 sketch numbers reproduce (tube 1.8 ns, Hopf lift 0.4 ns). A technical artist would model a knot in a DCC; this is a demo scene, so showcase.

coral-noise: growth in the extra dimension works exactly as claimed, the strips show stumps, trunks, branches, twigs, thickening, with nothing popping, and seed 7 matches seed 0. Re-measured scalar 3180 ns forest (64x perlin2) and 7155 ns staghorn (121x); AVX2 sketch reproduced at 55 to 358 ns unique and 88 to 203 ns template; the idea's 45 ns was indeed 6x too low. What the images also show: capsule-union silhouettes with one equal-size tree per cell (2D wide view is a lattice of equal glyphs, axis 8.06), a one-template forest that visibly repeats at window 4 (the prototyper did not look close), and no template speed-up at all in the scalar prototype. Nothing in existing nodes can make branching objects, so unique is high, but at 100 to 360 ns a sample and a 130-segment fixed-count loop it is a showcase or bake node. Adding ageJit and density jitter gives mixed sizes and helps a little.

newton-basins: the hero sheet is a favourable seed. At seed 3 the fronds shrink to a few small zones and most of the frame is a flat mosaic; at seed 11 window 16 it is a speckled mosaic, and axis stays 14 to 19 so a mild lattice alignment survives the offsets. I rendered the real existing-node graph with fnlab (DomainWarpFractalProgressive over CellularValue): it gives flat patches with marbled borders and no fronds, so the prototyper is right that the lace cannot be had from a graph, but the lace is a minority of the area and the rest is what the graph already does. out=5 gives a cleaner mesa relief than the default relief, and Terrace on a warped noise gives comparable plateaus. Hard jumps, wedge aliasing, static and a rubble 3D make it a drop.

All numbers above were measured; nothing is estimated except where the prototyper's own estimates are quoted.
families.proto_answer:
All three are proved on look; none is killed. They are expensive or specialised, so treat them as hero or bake nodes, not everyday building blocks. Ranking by how much they deliver: coral-noise, knot-field, newton-basins.

knot-field: the vol view decides in its favour. Tube mode renders literal, clean torus knots (trefoil, cinquefoil, 8_19, a 3-ring link). The Gauss-Newton distance gives constant radius, where the raw |f| tube from the idea visibly pinches. The new fibre bundle mode looks like hundreds of field lines or combed hair wrapped around a lobed core, and it is the best image in the family. The idea's claim that 2D is dull is wrong for Hopf: slices are a whirlpool of scales. The real limit is that it is one centred object that fades to a constant far away. Fold makes it stationary, but the result is an obvious mirrored carpet. Per-cell scatter reads as macaroni and the tumbleweed cells as a grid of fuzzy balls, so I dropped both. Measured cost is low: tube 1.7 ns and Hopf lift 0.4 ns in an AVX2 sketch.

coral-noise: growth is the showpiece and it works. In the growth strips stumps become trunks, branches appear where the parent has passed the attach point, then twigs, then thickening. Age continuity scales about 8x from da=1e-3 to da=8e-3 (0.016 to 0.133 at age 0.3), so nothing pops. The look only landed after I changed the layout: roots on a plane with a 3x3 window gives staghorn coral, sea fans and a bare winter forest. The idea's 3D lattice gives floating sticks and is weak. Cost is the catch: 160 ns unique or 90 ns with template trees for 117 capsules in the AVX2 sketch, and 278 ns for the 189-capsule lattice the idea priced at 45 ns.

newton-basins: real fronds and lobed borders on flat patches, which a warped CellularValue graph did not produce in the side-by-side. The earlier judged look was partly an artifact. Perlin vanishes on the integer lattice, so the noise pair shared a root at every lattice point and the basins were a square grid. Offsetting the noises dropped the FFT axis ratio from 50.92 to 7.66 and removed the grid in the wide view. N=4 with a det floor of 0.5 looks at least as good as N=12 with less static, at 16.9 ns in the sketch. Fronds cover only part of a view, the far view is an ordinary mosaic, jumps are inherent (c0ratio 1.00), and the 3D vol view is rubble rather than lace.

The AVX2 sketch numbers are cost only: its output was never compared with the scalar prototypes, and the same sketch ran about 1.4x leaner than the handbook's real nodes on its calibration kernels.
challenged: Template forest 'looked much the same as unique trees': at window 4 the one-template forest repeats visibly (same silhouette rotated in several cells). The 1.79x speed-up reproduces only in the AVX2 sketch (156.9 to 87.8 ns); the scalar prototype shows none (3189 vs 3180 ns).

Newton 'real fronds and lobed borders': seed dependent. Seed 3 at the same params has fronds in only a few small zones and seed 11 at window 16 is a speckled mosaic; sheet axis stays 14 to 19 after the offsets, so a mild lattice alignment remains.

Knot tube 'c0ratio 8.11': with the hero params the check returns a constant -1 field (c0ratio 0.00, std 0, seed sensitivity 0); the continuity figure comes from other params and the checks are not meaningful for a single centred object.
Knot '2D is a whirlpool of scales': true at the centre only. At window 16 it is one spiral whose scales grow to screen size away from the centre; it is not a texture.
Coral 2D twig mode 'useful as a mask': one equal-size tree per cell shows as a lattice of glyphs in the wide view (axis 8.06).
Family answer 'all three are proved on look; none is killed': newton-basins does not survive a different seed or the wide view, and its only non-graph content (lace) is a minority of the area.
kernels: Gauss-Newton distance to a zero set, sqrt( f^T (J J^T)^-1 f ) with a scale-invariant floor: knot tube and bundle; the same formula the tube-noise and iso-distance ideas describe (not tested on them here)
Tapered capsule SDF with growth clamp: coral-noise; possibly reusable by fiber-noise, not tested
Perlin with analytic gradient, with a non-integer offset per channel whenever several noises are solved together: newton-basins, and any multi-noise zero-set node
Per-node template tables with per-cell rotation and scale, as a cheaper alternative to per-segment hashing

families.answer:
Family question, answered by my own tests: both wild cards are proven. Only chiral-wallpaper deserves a node.

FISK: omega loops and oxbows are real. Over 36000 bends on 3 seeds at the prototyper's params, 45.1% of bends double back, 22.7% are classic omegas with both limbs leaning inward (one per 4.4 bends), and oxbows come once per 13.8 bends. I saw them on seeds 7, 42, 99 and 2024, not only 1337. A strong warped-gradient graph makes a coastline with pinched width, so the look is unique.

I disagree with the prototyper's "promising as a node":
- Own AVX2 port, parity worst 0.00115: 73-77 ns at one generation and 220-230 ns at three, against the 20-28 and 55-80 ns estimates. Channel-only at one generation is 46-51 ns, about 12x CellularDistance 2D (3.83 ns).
- "G1 everywhere" is false at the defaults: breakpoint kinks p50 9.9, p90 23.2, max 62 deg.
- Chutes have corners of p50 120 deg and read as canals. This was not reported as an artifact.
- Necks are fat: no doubling-back bend has a loop over 2x its neck.
- warp=0.4 does not break the belts.

My tuned params fix most of the look and it now reads as a meander belt, but chutes remain slightly angular at zoom. Verdict: showcase.

CHIRAL: all 17 groups pass a black-box test with no group tables. It searches every rotation and mirror, refines by direct evaluation, requires residual under 2e-3 out to +-40 units, then classifies. Results: 17/17 at chi .15 (seed 1337), chi .5 (seed 99), modes 2 (seed 7), and the final params (seed 7); chain=1 at k=.25 (seed 7) also 17/17. Continuity is tested source-free at the prototyper's recommended rounds=2: the coordinate map's Lipschitz bound stays fixed as the step shrinks, 0.59-1.34 at chi .15 and 0.96-4.34 at chi .5, so F is continuous for any continuous source.

Three caveats the prototyper missed:
- chi=0 collapses 14 of 17 enum values onto pmm, p4m or p6m.
- modes=1 gives pg->pm and pgg->pmg at seed 21, so Modes must be 2-4.
- The per-seed output range is narrow and seed dependent, for example -0.18..0.15 at seed 99, so "passes the source range" is false and users need a Remap.

The cost is better than claimed. After merging, the warp has 4 wave vectors (rect and square) or 6 (hex) regardless of group order. Measured AVX2 map cost is 2.0 ns for rect and square and 4.7 ns for hex including p6m, against the 12-24 ns estimate. Post-fold crease softening removes the seam lines and keeps the group (17/17). Verdict: ship, merged with domain-kaleidoscope's 2D groups, since chi=0 is exactly those groups.

Bubble-invert: the claims held. Map Lipschitz equals 1/eps^iter at both steps at eps .2, so steep but no jumps; AVX2 1.13-1.26 ns per first iteration. With a cellular source, 3D gives nested sphere clusters, better than the stripe volume shown. Niche, so showcase.

Domain-kifs: agree with the prototyper. Drop it; stacking wallpaper nodes gives better nested ornament with an exact group.
families.proto_answer:
Wild cards: two proven, one narrow, the reserve killed.

fisk-meanders PROVEN as a look, promising as a node. The sheet shows exactly what was asked for: tangent-continuous rivers with real omega loops (goosenecks with narrow necks), oxbow lakes (the cut loop stays as a shallower crescent while the live channel takes the straight neck chute) and concentric scroll bars on the inner banks. Getting there needed a change from the idea: single arcs with a constant per-strip sweep gave a uniform wave train, so every bend is now an equal-chord biarc with a hashed tangent angle at each breakpoint, which is G1 everywhere and gives bends from near-straight to full loops in one river. Measured: c0ratio 7.98 after three extra continuity fades in the scroll bars (the idea's sector fades were not continuous; c0 was 1.9-4.8 until fixed), scalar 2632 ns = 50.6x perlin2 for 3 generations (1055 ns for one), window 3 strips x 4 bends x 2 arcs (NA=4 vs 5 differed by exactly 0; NA=3 had seams). Flaws: cost (estimate 55-80 ns AVX2 2D at 3 generations, mark estimate), the parallel belts need an upstream warp (built-in warp=0.4 shown), the plain is dead flat, the 3D form is only crossfaded stacked layers, and the scroll bars stay subtle next to the channel depth.

chiral-wallpaper KEEPER. All 17 wallpaper groups were tested by program (t_chiral_wallpaper_test.exe): for each group, invariance under every coset representative and both lattice translations is ~1e-5 (float noise), c0ratio 7.4-8.3, and every Coxeter-parent mirror or rotation not in the group is broken (mean difference 0.1-0.3) while those in the group give exactly 0, so each enum entry is exactly its group. Two corrections to the idea: the equivariant field must be RMS-normalised per group (Reynolds averaging shrinks it by a group-dependent factor) and must use diagonal trig modes as well as axis-aligned ones (with 2 axis modes pmg accidentally kept its parent mirror). The p6m fold needs 2 rounds, not 12 (0 of 200000 points outside the triangle). Look: p6 gives interlocking pinwheel blades with no mirror lines, chi sweeps from snowflake kaleidoscope to spiral vortices while staying exactly symmetric, worley sources give crisp Escher mosaics; the rectangular groups are distinct but less striking. Cost: fold ~1 ns AVX2 estimate; the chiral warp is |G/T| x modes sinusoids, so p6m at 4 modes is a few Perlins (estimate), the rectangular groups are cheap. 3D done only as a prism.

bubble-invert PROMISING but narrow. Works exactly as described (identity on the rim, no seam, c0ratio 8.0 at one iteration, ~1-2 ns per iteration estimate, 3D spheres render). Clean looks need a structured low-frequency source: stripe dipoles, checker dust, and an unplanned frogspawn/compound-eye nested-cell look with a cellular source (saved as a discovery). With fbm the cores alias into speckle and the relief is spiky; 2-3 iterations add dust. Not a terrain node.

domain-kifs (reserve) WEAK: continuous and cheap, but the look is a CG kaleidoscope with concentric fan bands around every tile centre and hard mirror-tile seams; chiral-wallpaper covers the symmetric-tiling need better.

Shared: fisk and chiral both rely on branch-free fold/reflect with masked ops, and the lab now has a reusable jump-map debug trick (out=4 renders |f(p+h)-f(p)| > thr) that found every discontinuity quickly.
challenged: fisk: est AVX2 20-28 ns (G=1) and 55-80 ns (G=3) is about 3x low. Measured 73-77 and 220-230 ns with a port at parity (worst 0.00115). The borrowed 47x scalar ratio is about 14x for this code.
fisk: G1 everywhere is false at defaults. Breakpoint kinks p50 9.9, p90 23.2, p99 36.6, max 62.2 deg, caused by jv=0.15. jv=0 gives exactly 0.
fisk: tangent-continuous rivers is false at oxbows. Chute corners p50 120, min 100, max 154 deg; they read as straight canal segments on seeds 7, 42, 2024 and were not listed as an artifact.
fisk: goosenecks with narrow necks overstates it. 0.0% of doubling-back bends have a loop over 2x the neck; median neck gap 0.57 Lc against channel half width 0.11.
fisk: warp=0.4 does not break the parallel belts. It takes warp 2.5 at frequency 0.05 plus per-river bend length.
fisk: dead flat trench relief was partly the view. hscale 90 on a -1..0.3 range; hscale 18-22 with a low relief Add reads as a floodplain.
chiral: warp cost |G/T| x modes sinusoids is wrong. After merging, 4 or 6 wave vectors for every group. Measured p6m 4.7 ns against 12-24, p3 and p6 4.7 against 6-12, p4 2.06 against 4-8.
chiral: fold about 1 ns is true only for hex (0.98). Rect and square measure 0.15-0.18 ns.
chiral: each enum entry is exactly its group fails at chi=0 (14 of 17 collapse) and at modes=1 (pg->pm, pgg->pmg at seed 21). The proposed Modes 1-4 range must be 2-4.
chiral: passes the source range through is false. Per-seed range is narrow and seed dependent, e.g. -0.18..0.15 at seed 99 k=1 and -0.67..0.42 at seed 7 k=1. Auto-ranged images hide this.
chiral: the prototyper's group test ran at rounds=4 and tested mirrors only about the origin. It holds when retested at rounds=2 with a full search, so the result stands but that test was weak.
bubble: the 3D vol shown (stripe slabs) undersells it; a cellular source gives nested sphere clusters. Other bubble claims held.
kernels: Branch-free Coxeter folds (triU, triU+sort, hex lattice reduce + 2 rounds of masked reflections) shared by chiral-wallpaper and domain-kifs, and reusable by domain-kaleidoscope
Circular-arc SDF with sector test by dot products (no atan2) and signed ray distances for continuous sector fades, from fisk-meanders; useful for any arc/biarc curve node
Equal-chord biarc construction from per-breakpoint tangent angles (joint at angle (a0+a1)/4, half-sweeps (3a0-a1)/4 and (3a1-a0)/4), G1 curves from hashed angles
Reynolds-averaged equivariant trig field as a precomputed sinusoid table (wave vector, phase, amplitude vector), the general way to make any symmetric warp exact
Jump-map debug output (|f(p+h)-f(p)| > thr rendered as an image) for locating discontinuities; it found every bar-field jump in fisk-meanders

data.plan_changes: 1. Time default is 150 in world units, not 1.5 in feature units. Like Warp Amplitude and Sample Distance. 150 is 1.5 x the default Perlin Feature Scale. 2. Breaking time: measured on the real source, 0.34 x Feature Scale on 1 octave Perlin (seams clean at 0.34, jumps at 0.40), 0.14 x at 3 octaves, 0.10 x at 5 (clean at 0.10, jumps at 0.15), 0.135 x on Simplex. The plan's 0.37 and 0.23 came from the prototype's own FBm, normalised differently. 3. Solver works in v space, G = v - S( time * v ), not the prototype's s / t. That needs no division by Time, Time 0 is exact on Locked and Fast (worst 7.45e-08 including Polish 0) and negative Time works. 4. Viscosity is unit free, in v space: 0.02 is the prototype's 0.03 at t = 1.5. By arithmetic the prototype's form spreads the weight over the whole window as Time falls and has no source passthrough short of its own t == 0 test; not measured. Default changed from 0.03 to 0.02. Viscous Time 0 against the source, worst and rms: Viscosity 0.03 4.69e-03, 5.13e-05; 0.02 1.49e-03, 3.90e-04; 0.01 8.52e-03, 6.00e-03; 0.005 2.51e-02, 1.74e-02. 5. Viscous estimator: mean of ( v + S ) / 2 over taps with one Exp each, not the prototype's exact segment integral with two. Scalar test on one line (t 1.5, nu 0.03, K 13, against 8193 taps): rms 0.0211 against 0.0323, slope error 0.107 against 0.186. Viscous end taps fade with the phase, so no seam at any Viscosity. Scalar test only, the 2 point Gauss form was slightly better at twice the Exps. 6. Mixins: added VariableRange, the plan had none. 7. Considered and removed Max Time, which the critic asked for. Measured against Taps 65 with Time 0 to 300 on Perlin 100, before the member was removed: per sample spacing off by more than 0.2 on 0.44% and Max Time on 3.81% at Taps 13, 0.07% and 0.52% at Taps 21. Small islands on a 256 px thumb, per sample against Max Time, at Taps 13 at offsets 0 and 20000: Time 0 to 150 at Feature Scale 400, 1 and 1 against 8 and 8. Time 0 to 300 at Feature Scale 100, 19 and 13 against 10 and 4. Time 50 to 250 at Feature Scale 30, faster than the source, 35 and 21 against 8 and 15. At Taps 21 all are 1 to 4 either way. So a fast Time field does fray more without it, which is on the Time member text, but it loses far more placement than it saves. The critic's no seams test at tvar 3 tmax 1.5 was not a test of the alternative. 8. Taps minimum 5, not 3, which divided by zero in the prototype's Locked. Max 65. Polish 0 to 8, Iterations 1 to 16. 9. Locked skips the energy update for a whole batch with FS::AnyMask when no lane crosses: 20.91 to 18.18 ns 2D AVX2. 10. gMetadataVectorSize left alone. Reviewer: 11. Bound capped at 1e6, also the metadata maximum. 12. Fast takes the source as flat across the last interval when a bracket end was never sampled, so Time 0 is exact at any Bound and Iterations. 13. Non finite Time is no travel and non finite output is 0.

data.notes: Status ok-with-notes: fnlab seams exits 1 on Locked and Fast above breaking time, by design and as the plan expects, and Locked is the default. The reviewer found and fixed 4 defects in 265cb30, see below; everything else the author measured reproduced. Fixed: 1. NaN on huge Bound (Viscous from 1e20, Locked and Fast at 3e38) and on Bound 1e-45, from overflowing tap energies and bracket width: Bound capped at 1e6, output masked. 2. NaN on AVX2 2D only when Time or Source was NaN or Inf, including stock Divide( 1, 0 ) which returns NaN: non finite Time is now no travel, and output is masked. fast-math made this one depend on feature set and dimension. 3. Fast assumed f = +-Bound at a bracket end it never sampled: at Time 0, Bound 0.5 worst 2.94e-02 on 15.5% of samples by more than 1e-2, Iterations 1 worst 4.49e-01, and it compressed the top of the range at any Time. Now worst 1.19e-07. 4. Direction squares overflowed or flushed in float, so Direction X=Y=1e20 or 1e-30 silently meant no travel: normalised in double. Descriptions corrected: Time 0 is the source clamped to Bound, stepped sources stair on Taps, Viscous grain on a connected Time. Limits, measured: Terrace stairs at low Taps as in seams; Taps 21 leaves Simplex off by more than 0.2 on 4.13% at Time / Feature Scale 3; with a connected Time, Viscous gets noisier away from the origin since the tap phase churns with distance, second difference medians at Viscosity 0.02 7.01e-04, 1.18e-03, 1.46e-03 and at 0.01 3.26e-03, 8.94e-03, 9.10e-03 at offsets 0, 2e4, 1e5; Locked does not grow (0.045%, 0.030%, 0.030% off by more than 0.2 at spreads 200, 2000, 20000). Viscosity scales with source amplitude squared. A NaN source gives finite output that differs per feature set. The critic's Max Time would have helped the Viscous grain; I left it out as the author did, it is not a defect at the default Viscosity. MSVC 14.51 compiles the AVX2 unit at /Od with the node instantiated, clang-cl builds the rest; GCC and ARM not tried. Code read: no per lane branches, no hash, no int conversion, Floor guarded at 2^23, division by zero masked or impossible, all members used, metadata defaults match the header, registration last, plan members all present, no test node committed. Author's context, still true: 15 source evaluations by default, jumps alias and are poor warp or slope inputs, fine octaves tear with every root, Taps rule measured on 1 octave Perlin. Also rendered and liked by the author: Patchy cliffs, Rocky cuestas, Feathers, DSL.

data.check: 0 FAIL, 0 WARN on CausticWeb, all 4 Field x Lens Dims forms at Feature Scale 40 and at the default 100, and all 5 presets. Default at Feature Scale 40: SSE2 max diff 5.41e-05 / 5.82e-05 / 4.13e-05, SSE41 5.43e-05 / 5.85e-05 / 4.13e-05, AVX512 2.62e-06 / 3.58e-07 / 3.58e-07, 0.0000% of samples off by more than 1e-2, entry parity 2.57e-05, continuity ratio 7.83 / 7.96 / 7.81. Field=Free: SSE2 and SSE41 4.10e-04 / 4.34e-04 / 8.94e-04, AVX512 3.58e-07, 0.0000%. Battery of 56 runs over Steps 0-16, Gamma 0.05-4, Line Softness 1e-4 to 4, Depth 0, 0.3, -1.1, 3, 8, 64, 1e9, hybrid Depth, Seed Offset, inverted output, seeds 7 and 2024, scales 0.37 and 3, Feature Scale 1000, FractalFBm and DomainWarpGradient over the node: 0 NaN/Inf anywhere. Only FAIL lines, both by design at Depth 0 where the lens is flat and the output constant: 'FAIL  non-constant: std 0.00000'. WARNs: continuity ratio below 4 at Depth 3 and above (for example 'WARN  continuity 4D: worst step ratio 3.19 on axis 2 (8 = Lipschitz, ~1 = jumps), max slope 208.151 per feature' on Free with a hybrid Depth up to 2.4), at Steps 8 (Free) and 16, and at Line Softness 1e-4; 'WARN  tileable: seam 0.1260 interior 0.0420 (ratio 3.00), std 0.394' on Free at seed 7; FBm's own unnormalised sum on the range line for FractalFBm(Octaves=3). Degenerate scale: Feature Scale 0.001 gives 'FAIL simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 1.02e+00 3D 1.11e+00 4D 9.87e-01, samples off by >1e-2: 2.7303%', the same for SSE41, and 'FAIL entry parity 2D: grid vs positions 7.45e-01, grid vs single 7.45e-01'; stock Perlin fails the same three there (1.32e-02, 0.2482%, 5.46e-03), this is float position precision at 1000 features per pixel, far worse here because of the steep lines. Independent check: a numpy version of the maths using np.linalg.det agrees with fnlab raw on all 30 combinations of Field, 2D/3D/4D, Lens Dims and Steps 0, 2, 3: Gradient max diff 2.8e-04, Free 7.1e-03 and p99.9 2.0e-03 (float rounding on the steep lines). That covers the 3x3 and 4x4 determinants, the packed Hessian indices, the scale constants and the floor.

Steps 2: SSE41 12.27 / 21.58 / 41.66, AVX2 5.69 / 10.15 / 16.35, AVX512 3.84 / 7.64 / 12.01. Steps 0: AVX2 2.49 / 4.69 / 7.63. Free Steps 2: AVX2 9.96 / 24.85 / 50.06. Free XYOnly: AVX2 12.98 / 21.89 / 32.99. Gamma 1 (the Log2 and Exp2 path): AVX2 7.61 / 13.27 / 21.08. Hybrid Depth from Simplex: AVX2 8.11 / 15.58 / 23.28. data.seams: This gate does not read clean at every setting, and the reason is slope, not jumps. CausticWeb() at its default Feature Scale 100: 'SEAMS: none found', worst 0.0077 / 0.0080 / 0.0104 over 0.000977. Presets: Pool floor, Cobblestones, Cell foam, Two scale net 'none found'; Silk filaments 'jumps above 0.02: 1 of 4000' in 3D at 0.0242, 2D and 4D clean. Flagged by the scan: Feature Scale 40 default, 2D 0.0194 / 0 of 4000, 3D 0.0242 / 1, 4D 0.0212 / 1; seed 2024 2D 0.0213 / 1, 3D 0.0285 / 1, 4D 0.0214 / 1. XYOnly at 40: 0.0369 / 3 and 0.0567 / 4 in 3D and 4D. Free at 40: 0.0395 / 44, 0.0535 / 45, 0.0799 / 56. Free at the default 100: 0.0197 / 0, 0.0251 / 2, 0.0327 / 4. Also flagged at higher Depth, Steps 4 and up, Gamma 1 and up, and small Line Softness, which all steepen the lines. Evidence that these are steep continuous lines: the worst step shrinks as the window shrinks relative to a feature, a jump would not. Default 2D at Feature Scale 40, 160, 640, 2560: 0.0194, 0.0054, 0.0006, 0.0001. Free 4D: 0.0799, 0.0186, 0.0091, 0.0003. Depth 3 2D, the steepest case that was tried: 0.3273, 0.0655, 0.0080, 0.0008. All the code is continuous per lane and the r^2 = 0.5 kernel has a continuous Hessian. Seam scan at Feature Scale 40 before the line core was rounded read 0.0317 / 0.0312 / 0.0290 on the default, so the round core removed 22% to 39% of the reading.
data.range: Native range is a floor to 1. The line value is ( softness^2 / ( det^2 + softness^2 ) )^( Gamma / 2 ), which is 1 at det 0 by construction. The floor is computed in the setters from Line Softness, Gamma and a measured peak |det| of 10, 24, 70 for 2D, 3D, 4D. Measured with the floor disabled over 4 seeds of 490000 samples per form at Feature Scale 40, peak |det| by form: Gradient Full 6.1 / 8.8 / 21.7, Gradient XYOnly 7.3 / 9.7 (3D, 4D), Free Full 9.9 / 23.4 / 69.9, Free XYOnly 12.6 / 14.5 (3D, 4D). Output range from check: default -0.946..1.000, XYOnly -0.944..1.000, Free -0.997..1.000, Free XYOnly -0.996..1.000, mean -0.63 on Gradient and -0.66 on Free, std 0.37. Line values below the floor are clamped to Output Min, which happens at Depth above the default: Depth 1.6 and up measures -1.00. Below the default Depth the output does not reach Output Min and at Depth 0.3 the bright end does not reach 1 either (-0.754..0.241), because the determinant never gets to 0.
data.far: fnlab check far coordinates ok on every form. Through DomainOffset at Feature Scale 40: no NaN to 1e9 world units. Std, mean step and max step are flat through 1e7 world units, which is 2.5e5 features. Equal neighbouring samples: 2.0% at 3e6, 23.5% at 1e7, 74.8% at 3e7 for Gradient; stock Perlin 0.0%, 0.0%, 59.9%, so quantisation shows about 3x earlier than Perlin. Free 2.6%, 11.7%, 66.2%. Gradient collapses to one value at 1e9 like Perlin, Free to 18 values. No limit in normal use, so none is in the description.
data.tile: Real 4D form, so GenTileable2D wraps by construction, at the 4D cost. fnlab tile seam ratio 0.72 on the default at Feature Scale 40 and 0.66 on Free; check ratios 0.38 to 2.19 on all presets and forms. One WARN at ratio 3.00, Free seed 7: against every interior row and column of its PNG the seam's mean step sits at percentile 12 and 97 and its peak step is 0.776 against 0.945 inside, so one row against sparse bright lines reads high; that is suggestive, not a proof. It does not keep the 2D look: the image, viewed, shows no seam, but rounder dark cells, foggy grey patches and a few small ring shapes, because a torus in 4D is curved and the 4D Simplex is more intermittent. XYOnly on the torus looks closer to a net, with the same fog. Stated in the node description.
data.versus_proto: The image, viewed, prototype and node at seed 1337 at matching zoom (Feature Scale 84 in fnlab thumb). Web: same closed net of curved polygons around dark bowls with fainter internal folds and bright junctions, no visible lattice. Silk: same open filaments with hooks, tapered ends and cells left open. Not the same field: K1's gradient table differs from the prototype's random unit vectors, so line positions differ. Lines are softer and wider at the same Line Softness on purpose, because the core is round rather than a crease, 1.7x wider at half height by the formula. Free uses Simplex per channel as the prototype's silk does, not Perlin. Slices viewed for 3D and 4D: XYOnly keeps the 2D net, Full 3D is similar with thicker fog, Full 4D has rounder cells, and Free Full gets busier and more tangled with dimension. Not re-run: correlation against the ray histogram, which the plan says is not a quality judge. The volume with Line Softness 0.3 and iso -0.2 reads as a clean open cell foam; Inverted, reads as cobblestones. Viewed: in XYOnly the lines drift and relink smoothly along Z, correlation against the first slice 0.859, 0.701, 0.390, 0.048 at 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4 features; Full 0.774, 0.547, 0.220, -0.156. That is the plan's missing z strip; it was judged from stills, not played as motion.
data.plan_changes: Line core is softness / sqrt( det^2 + softness^2 ) rather than softness / ( |det| + softness ): same tail, no crease, max slope on the check grid 30.5 to 14.9 per feature in 2D, for one extra sqrt. Cost: lines 1.7x wider at half height at the same Line Softness, by the formula. Depth is capped at +-6: at 8 the entry parity check starts to fail (1.42e-03) and only dots are left. Negative Depth is allowed and is the same picture with the height flipped. Setters clamp Steps 0..16, Line Softness 1e-4..16, Gamma 0.05..16. Gamma other than 0.5 uses Log2 and Exp2 rather than FS::Pow, following the note in PolyMath.inl that FS::Log jumps; I did not measure FS::Pow myself. Plan note changed: the plan said lines alias below about 30 px per unit. Measured with one sample per pixel against 16 there is no threshold: the error relative to contrast is 57% at Feature Scale 10, 29% at 30, 14% at 84, 10% at 120; Line Softness 0.5 gives 31%, 12%, 4%, 3%; stock Perlin 5.3% at 10. Depth units in the 4D and XY forms are normalised by the measured RMS Laplacian per form, 29.62 in 2D, 27.16 and 21.59 for Full 3D and 4D, 20.02 and 12.46 for XYOnly 3D and 4D, because the prototype's constants were for its own kernels. Free's Depth 1.1 is scaled to the prototype's silk at A 0.8, using RMS gradient length 3.675, 3.04, 2.205 and 2.482, 1.559. Free uses Simplex per channel with fixed position offsets between channels, since without them all channels are zero on the same lattice vertices. Feature Scale is lattice units as in stock Simplex, the prototype's fq 0.8 and 0.7 are gone because the map is scale free in lattice coordinates, so Feature Scale 84 in fnlab thumb matches the prototype's image. Real 4D exists now on the K1 kernel, not only the 16-wave height.

Log2/Exp2 path: Gamma 1 worst step 0.0118 / 0.0029 / 0.0004 at Feature Scale 100 / 400 / 1600 in 2D, Free Gamma 2 0.0509 / 0.0127 / 0.0058, shrinking with the window, so no jumps from FS::Log2. Depth 6 and -6 flag 480 to 530 of 4000 at 0.35 to 0.82 in 2D/3D (steep dots at the cap, 4 WARN in check, continuity ratio low), Gamma 16 flags 279 of 4000 at 0.066, Line Softness clamped to 1e-4 flags 177 at 0.61.

review.versus_proto: Viewed: prototype thumb beside the node at Feature Scale 84 seed 1337. Same closed net of curved polygons with bright junctions and faint folds inside cells; node lines a little softer and wider; different line positions (different gradient table). Free at Softness 0.12 is open silk filaments with hooks. Steps 0 is closed loops and blobs. Viewed: Depth -1.1 a clean net, Depth 3 a thinner net, Depth 6 mostly dots and short dashes, Gamma 2 thin crisp lines. After the fix, a test of every member at 0, -1, +-1e20, +-3e38, +-inf and NaN and Feature Scale at 10 odd values, through SSE2, SSE41, AVX2 and AVX512, 2D, 3D and 4D, five sources, with NaN, inf and 1e30 in the positions: 0 non-finite samples, no crash. All 75 registered nodes as Source at 4 settings on fnlab check: 0 non-finite, no crash except the 2 fractal warps fed a plain Perlin in the battery, which crash bare too; with a real warp source they pass. Huge members still 'FAIL  non-constant: std 0.00000', below float resolution. Parity decays with the stretch, as stock does: Source Scale 1e4 fails simd parity on seed -5 at max diff 3.07e-02, Source Scale 1e5 on every seed, Aniso 1e6 at 43.1%; stock DomainScale(Scaling=1e6) fails at 8.4%. Entry parity is under the 1e-3 limit at Feature Scale 2000 over a source at 5 on seed 4242; at 5000 over 5 it fails on seeds 777 and 4242 at 5.60e-03 and 2.73e-03. It also fails from Aniso 1e4 and from Source Scale 1e3 on some seeds. A NaN Blend Width set through the C API gives output 0.
data.seams: fnlab seams on the final build. Default tree, seeds 1337, -5, 777, 1, 4242: 'SEAMS: none found', worst after bisection .0034 / .0059 / .0039 over .000977. Fibre block on seed -5: 'jumps above 0.02: 1 of 4000', worst .0208 at 351.796, -105.117, none on 777, 1, 4242, and none in the 2D scan of seeds 11 to 22. It is a steep ramp, not a jump: the step there scales with spacing, .0726 at .004, .0063 at .00025, and --scale .1 finds none. Over about .15 world the output goes .24 to -.21. Cause: 4 sites nearly tie and K = 3 cannot hold them, the same pinch as Grid Jitter 0 at cell corners, but at any Grid Jitter. Measured over a gentle source (Aniso 1, Source Scale .25, Scale Jitter 0, Feature Scale 64, 1024 px, 4 seeds): pixel step above .2 in 94.7 spots per 1000 cells, above .4 in 3.9, worst .624. 3D planes 5.8, worst .278; 4D planes 0, worst .142. Now in the description. Side by side with K = D + 2 I could not tell them apart on fibres, and saw only small differences in hillshade on the gentle source and ridges. K = D + 2 takes the spots above .2 to 0 at that setting, worst .163, at +21% AVX2 2D, +6% 3D, +25% 4D, with a worst case of 4, 5 and 6 source evals. Not applied, the plan says D + 1. Shards: jumps 3867 / 3755 / 3647 of 4000, by design. Aniso 1000, Source Scale 1000 and Feature Scale 1 report jumps at --scale 1 and none at --scale .01, so slope. Window borders: 8M 2D, 3M 3D and 1M 4D pairs one float either side of n + .5, at 5 Grid Jitter and Blend Width settings, 40 seeds: 0 above .02, worst .00019, so no grain is lost at a border. Frames measured from each grain's lattice point plus a random offset of up to 47.3 cells, not the world origin: no position growth from the stretch, and no FS::InvSqrt difference in source positions. 4. Top K slots start at the cap, and a batch skips a site no lane needs and a grain no lane weighs: output is unchanged, 4D kernel 837 to 139 ns on AVX2. data.versus_proto: The author wrote never prototyped, but the catalogue names prototypes. Review render at Grid Jitter 1: cl_kens node 3 k=12 against Smooth Value Smoothness 0.08, the same soft polygon mosaic; node 4 k=6 against Smooth F1 Smoothness 0.167, the same merged peanut wells; dcc_lens mode 0 against Alligator Smoothness 0.05, where the prototype's darker domes with wide dead zones become brighter, broader plates with thin creases, which the author disclosed. The prototype panels show about twice the feature size in that sheet, so compare the look and not the scale. Presets on seed 24601 show no artifacts. Worth shipping.
data.plan_changes: Output has SmoothF1, SmoothValue and Alligator; the plan's data called the second Voronoise. Smoothness and Grid Jitter are hybrids where the plan's data had floats, which is a superset. The catalogue's Bevel was built and rendered, then dropped: it reads as a soft F2-F1 and CellularEdge already covers walls. Also dropped: power mode, distance function, kernel reach and a separate value smoothness, so Smoothness drives everything, as in the plan's member list. Kernel: exp(-d / S) minus its tangent at the window's reach of 1.5 - jitter, instead of iq's 5x5 window or a plain exponential. Alligator departs from the HDK form with an outer Sqrt, which moved the mean from -0.64 to -0.28 and turned thin peaks into broad plates, and Smoothness blunts the crease from a cusp to a V. Smooth Value gain changed in review to 1 + S^3 / 2. Measured costs beat the plan's on a grid, on AVX2 Alligator is 1.04x CellularDistance in 2D and 0.79x in 4D, not 1.4x, but scattered lanes cost 1.45x and 1.28x there. Review: nothing else left out silently.

At Chirality=0 exactly 3 of 17 keep their name, the 9 rect groups read pmm, the 3 square read p4m, the 5 hex read p6m, as the plan says. Fold reach with 2 rounds: worst outside the fundamental triangle 1.49e-08 over 2e6 samples at spans 3, 50 and 3000. Lipschitz of the coordinate map, two step sizes, all 17 groups: 1.26 to 3.45 and stable between h=4e-4 and 1e-4, so no jump for any continuous Source. 3D slices and 4D planes keep the symmetry: worst |F(g p) - F(p)| for p6 60 degrees 2.61e-04 3D, 1.24e-05 4D XY, 1.34e-05 4D ZW; p4, p2 and p3 smaller or similar. A Chirality node breaks it by design, 1.18 on the same test. REVIEW (523350c): rebuilt and re-ran. Presets 5 of 5: 0 FAIL, seams none. 17 groups at Modes=3, Chirality=-0.7, Crease Softness=0.2, Cell Size=333, seed 12345: 0 FAIL, seams none. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: an out of range Group (fnSetVariableIntEnum with -1, 17, 100, INT_MAX, or a bad encoded tree) matched no switch case, left the field empty and chirality / Sqrt( 0 ) made every sample NaN; now clamped in SetGroup and the switch has a default. 0 non finite after the fix. data.versus_proto: Prototype g=16,chi=0.2,cell=0.5,modes=4,rounds=2,src=0,k=1,soft=0.04 against the real node at Cell Size=200 and the same window: same hex lattice spacing, white 6 fold eyes and pinwheel arms. The arms differ: thicker and darker in the prototype, thinner and paler in the real node, because the field now comes from a fixed table with seed weights in place of the prototype's per seed hash. I did not compare group by group against the prototype's g1..g17 images; the identifier covers the group identity and I looked at the real 17 group sheet, each group reads as named. REVIEW (proto the thumbnail against real p6 Cell Size=200 fBm4 Perlin 100): same hex lattice of 6 fold eyes and the same handedness of pinwheel, the real node's arms are thinner, longer and streakier, the prototype's shorter and fatter with dots inside the triangles; agrees with the author. All 17 groups read as named.
data.plan_changes: 1. Cell Size is world units and means the repeat distance in every family, default 400. A direct conversion of the prototype's 0.5 would be 200 at Feature Scale 100, and rect groups would repeat at twice the hex distance. Now rect fold units are Cell Size / 2, so rect groups at 400 are the prototype's geometry and hex at 200 is. Default 400 because at 200 an fBm Perlin source lost one sign on some seeds (over 8 seeds max as low as -0.125, min as high as 0.012); at 400 every seed spans 0. 2. The prototype built its field per seed, which a node cannot do at set time. The table of amplitudes and phases is now fixed, built at set time, and the seed per lane scales each orbit of merged waves by a signed weight of magnitude 0.5 to 1, renormalised to unit RMS. Multiplying a whole orbit keeps the field equivariant. Less seed variety than the prototype: hex at Modes 4 has 2 orbits, and at Modes 2 or 3 only 1 or 2. Measured warp response between seeds, p6: 27 world units on most pairs, 4 between seeds with the same sign pattern. 3. The field runs on lattice coordinates reduced to one cell. Not in the plan, it fixes far parity (1.29e-02 at 1e6 before, 6.08e-03 after). 4. 4D is the plan's two folds, written, same weights and same Chirality value on both planes. 5. rounds is fixed at 2 as the critic recommended, and tested. 6. Table build sits in the dispatch class, called from its constructor and through a virtual from the setters, so no inline function compiled with AVX flags is merged across feature sets.

data.versus_proto: Reviewer: prototype at the plan's params against the real warped default, both seed 4242, looked. Trunks the same width with the same soft halo, real twigs a little shorter, coverage above mid gray .208 prototype, .182 real. Warp differs: prototype .14 cell with 2 octaves, preset .19 cell with 1. Reliefs against the prototype: canyon walls comparable, the real one has wider plateaus, and the prototype's relief has its own fine detail term. Older prototype thumbnail has thin trunks since it predates wmode=1, as the author says. Vol: same rod radius and about the same amount of rod at this seed. The prototype shows a star hub the real one lacks, since its 3D has no stochastic descent. I do not see the fewer rods the author could not explain. The comparison image is the author's and predates the level reseed, so its twigs differ in detail from the node now. Author's measures for that image: mean .191/.173, .210/.176, .199/.208; largest connected piece 73%/34%, 52%/51%, 38%/36%.
data.plan_changes: 1) Control cost in the plan was wrong: it is evals per sample, not per level, since only level 0 reads the control: 25 for Mask, 49 for Proximity and Carve, 1 more at the sample for Carve, 125 in 3D. 2) Proximity also uses the 5x5 level 0 and 7x7 control the plan gave only to Carve: at the 3x3 reach of .2 cells it is just a thick mask. 3) Epsilon is rounded to 1/256ths and stops at 1/256 and .9. Point positions are hash bits times Epsilon, so exact, and all decisions are made on differences of them, so no decision depends on where the window sits; a regular grid has exact geometric ties that rounding settled differently per SIMD level. 4) Parent search: the prototype indexes per lane, a port cannot. Per axis a child's pair is fixed except for child 0, so 4 lookups suffice once 16 parent entries have been picked per lane with 80 Selects a level. Lowest cell first, see seams. 5) Link limit is min( 1.1, .9 + ( 1 - Epsilon ) / 2 ), since a fixed 1.1 gives a negative reach above Epsilon .8; below Epsilon .6 it is the prototype's 1.1. 6) Hash control scaled by .5 so its bounds are -.85 to 1.05, noise .02 hash only and .04 on a source. Hermite in the value noise instead of quintic. 3D uses one 3D value noise at .2. 7) Prototype params that became fixed constants since the plan has no member for them: link 1.1, taper .45, Carve width 4x, depth .4, floor keep .9, level amplitude .6 for Carve and .8 for Proximity. The prototype's warp and Carve detail are left to the graph. 8) Valley Profile applies to Mask and Carve, not Proximity, whose radius is about a cell wide so that U and Box flatten it (reviewer change; the author had it on every Output). V is the prototype's bump, U has a floor to .4 of the radius, Box a wall over the outer .3: basin-tree's per segment size term is not ported. 9) 3D width is 4x Width capped at ( 1 - Epsilon ) / 2, so at defaults the rods are constant width and Proximity equals Mask in 3D. 10) Stochastic Descent uses one mixed hash per point rather than a separate one. Fern-fold stays out of v1 as the plan says. 11) Reviewer added level seeds to the seed instead of xoring them; that was reverted as 4f13232, so they are xored as the author wrote them. Its Valley Profile row could say 'not used by Proximity'.

data.notes:
As merged: the reseed 6ce33e9 was reverted as 4f13232, so level seeds are xored. Text and numbers marked 'at 6ce33e9' below were measured with the reseed, which changes the values levels 1 to 3 draw and not the code they run. Rechecked on the merged integ.dll: check on the default 0 FAIL, 2 WARN, the same two; bench AVX2 101.60 / 296.20 and AVX512 75.96 / 218.39 ns/sample 2D / 3D. The presets were rechecked on clang: 0 FAIL, seams none.

Usable as a hero or bake node, not a building block: 112x Perlin on AVX2, over the 5x guideline, as the plan expected. Known limits, all in the description: no 4D so no tiled tree, 3D is straight rods, segments are straight until warped, width is a proxy, hubs and crossings remain, fine lines go jagged far from the origin. Stack frame by counting, not measured: about 120 KB per Gen in 3D on AVX512 and 60 KB on AVX2, about 100 KB and 50 KB in 2D Carve; a target with a small stack (the plan's wasm editor) should check that, I did not run wasm. The number on Control has no effect, which is a slightly odd hybrid. Not done: no ARM, no MSVC, no wasm build.

REVIEW. Fixed, both: 1bb15c4 Proximity ignores Valley Profile, since Proximity + Box failed check as constant and Proximity + U was 92% flat; descriptions now say what Proximity ignores, the 4x width of Carve and 3D, and that 3D Proximity equals Mask at the default Width. 6ce33e9 level seeds added instead of xored, reverted afterwards as 4f13232. Measured stack at last, hard reservation in a child process: 2D Mask under 64 KB on AVX2 and 64 to 96 KB on AVX512, 2D Carve 64 to 96 KB, 3D Mask 64 to 96 KB on AVX2 and 128 to 160 KB on AVX512. Left alone: 3D height noise bits 20 to 25 overlap the eligibility bits, an effect of about .001 in height, not visible. NaN member values are not rejected. Disagreements: the author's 'every gate passes at usable settings' did not hold for Proximity + Box. '0.0000%' in check hides the rare SSE flips, about 4e-6 of samples. Not done: no ARM, wasm or GCC build, no full library MSVC build after the last commit, cross not re-run after the reseed.

Independent clang-cl re-measure at 6ce33e9 from a private DLL copy: agrees with the numbers above. Added here: far renders looked. Trees intact at 15600 and 31250 cells, twigs breaking up at 62500, no lattice artifact, so the description's 30000 cells is fair by eye, though fnlab seams already reports stair steps of .43 at 15600 cells. Hash fields, 2M cells with the repo primes: jitter, height noise and 2D eligibility bits all at or below .0013, under the 4 sigma null of .0028; level 0 against level 1 jitter under .0005 for xor and add alike; the only correlation is the known 3D overlap, eligibility bits 23, 24 and 25 with height noise at .007, .014 and .026. Wasm stack: build_editor uses -sSTACK_SIZE=1MB and proto builds 2MB, far above the measured need; The WASM build script sets none in the lines searched, not investigated further.

data.check: Final build ea18fb0. Default on a cellular source, DomainInvert(Feature Scale=213, Source=CellularDistance(Feature Scale=91)), seed 1337: check passed: 0 FAIL, 0 WARN. SSE2 and SSE41 vs AVX2 max diff 1.16e-06, AVX512 vs AVX2 5.54e-05, 0.0000% of samples off by >1e-2, grid vs positions 5.36e-07, continuity ratio 7.91 / 7.97 / 7.98. Five presets on seeds 1337, 42, -7 and on 9001, -424242 and 9001 at --scale 8, plus 5 setups the author did not show: 0 FAIL. Sweep of 19 configs: 0 FAIL. Odd values, 38 configs with 0, negative and huge values of every member: 0 FAIL, no crash, no NaN; before the fix 8 failed with NaN at Feature Scale 0, -0, 1e-42, 1e38, 1e39, -1e39, and 3 more on parity at Feature Scale 1e9 and 1e20. The WARNs come from the sources. Stock CellularDistance with Distance Function=Euclidean reads continuity ratio 0.97 to 2.45 alone over seeds 1337, 42, -7, 9001, -424242 and 1.09 to 4.62 under the node, and seams finds no jumps. FBm of Simplex: 'WARN  continuity 3D: worst step ratio 1.23 on axis 1' as the author reported. Checker dust: 'WARN  continuity 2D: worst step ratio 1.00 on axis 0' and on some seeds 'WARN  tileable: seam 0.0000 interior 0.0000 (ratio 0.00), std 0.000', and Checkerboard alone gives the same tile WARN. A scalar model written from the maths and hash scheme reads the same positions through a Gradient source over 66 cases: worst 0.044 world units at Eps 0.2, worst of all 1.25 at Feature Scale 37, Eps 0.05, Iterations 3. Hash fields over 1e6 cells: worst correlation between density, radius and jitter 0.0022, none with neighbour cells above 0.01.
data.seams: Default and every continuous preset on 3 seeds: none, 0 of 4000 above 0.02 in 2D, 3D, 4D, worst 0.0004. Same on the setups, including --scale 8 on seed 9001, which covers about 30 x 30 cells rather than 4 x 4: worst 0.0087. Low Eps on a cellular source is flagged in 2D: Eps=0.05 Iterations=3 6 and 10 of 4000, Eps=0.02 Iterations=3 21 and 35, Eps=0.01 Iterations=3 30 and 54 (1 in 3D), Eps=0.01 Iterations=2 12 and 11; Eps=0.01 Iterations=1 is clean. At Eps=0.05 the step falls 0.511, 0.519, 0.277, 0.066 as spacing falls 0.064, 0.016, 0.004, 0.001, so a slope. At Eps=0.02 and 0.01 with Iterations=3 the slope is up to 1 / Eps^3 and the step can still be 0.41 to 0.62 at spacing 0.001, near float resolution at these positions, so those settings are noise in the core as the description says. The Checker dust preset reports 4000 of 4000 at step 2.0, which is its Checkerboard source.
data.far: DomainOffset at 0 to 1e8 world units, 4 graphs: no NaN. Default on a cellular source: std 0.238 to 0.306, p99 neighbour step 0.066 to 0.091 up to 1e7, 0.188 at 3e7, 0.223 at 1e8. Source alone measured this time at spacing of about one float step, Euclidean cellular: p99 step 0.019 to 0.040 up to 1e7, 0.109 at 3e7, 0.433 at 1e8, node 0.086 to 0.137, 0.434, 0.949, so the rise from 3e7 is position rounding in both and the node multiplies it. To 1e30: the node is finite wherever the source is. CellularDistance alone leaves its range from about 1e12 and gives NaN at 1e30, with or without the node. Nothing to write into the description.
data.tile: Real 4D form, seamless. A tile is a torus of radius width / 6.28, so the author's fnlab tile runs at Feature Scale 213 (width 256, radius 41) never reached a bubble on the first build: 0.0% of samples differed from the bare source on seeds 1337, 42, 9001, -7, and those seam ratios were the source's. On the final build the share of a tile that moves is, for Feature Scale 213: width 256 24.8%, 0.0%, 71.3%, 0.0%; width 512 3.9%, 0.5%, 13.6%, 3.1%; width 1024 7.6%, 4.9%, 7.8%, 5.1%; width 2048 10.2%, 10.7%, 8.4%, 6.2%. Feature Scale 40: 9.8% to 13.5% at every width from 256. The description says so. Wrap tested where bubbles reach it, by Gen through the C API: Feature Scale 213 width 1024 Iterations 3 seed 9001, 74% of the wrap row moved, mean step over rows beside and across the wrap 0.0170, 0.0188, 0.0193, 0.0195, 0.0188, 0.0192, third value the wrap; four other setups the same. No seam. Author's script on the final build, seeds 1337, 42, 7: default 0.88, 0.98, 0.84; Iterations=3 0.84, 0.98, 0.84; low Perlin 1.20, 1.00, 0.78; Feature Scale 40 0.96, 1.07, 1.57.
data.range: Inherits the source's range, with no ScaleOutput and no VariableRange: gate 4's measured constant does not apply, because the node returns the source's value unchanged. Density 0 and Feature Scale 0 differ from the bare source by exactly 0. Samples moved in 2D at the defaults 35 to 43% over seeds, 76 to 78% at Iterations=3. Share of space by dimension at the defaults 38.6%, 20.7%, 10.1% against 38.9%, 20.9%, 10.1% from the geometry. A bubble shows other parts of the source, so a finite window's range can shift: seed 42 Perlin -0.699 to 0.866 alone, -0.771 to 0.866 with the node.
data.bench: fnlab bench on the final build, ns/sample, 2D / 3D / 4D, best of two runs. Constant source, so the node's own cost. Iterations=1: SSE41 2.23 / 2.62 / 3.48, AVX2 1.01 / 1.31 / 1.64, AVX512 0.75 / 0.88 / 1.04. Iterations=2: SSE41 4.49 / 5.19 / 6.61, AVX2 1.98 / 2.43 / 2.90, AVX512 1.41 / 1.60 / 1.89. Iterations=3: SSE41 6.73 / 7.49 / 9.59, AVX2 2.91 / 3.39 / 4.13, AVX512 2.04 / 2.32 / 2.63. Constant alone: AVX2 0.20 / 0.24 / 0.29. On Perlin: AVX2 1.98 / 3.26 / 5.48, Perlin alone 0.92 / 2.20 / 4.16. Frogspawn preset: AVX2 4.80 / 13.60 / 43.04, its source alone 4.10 / 12.53 / 41.58. fnlab bench has no SSE2 row. Against the author's numbers the cells differ by at most 7%, up or down, and AVX2 2D shows occasional outliers, up to 3.44 on the first run of a pair, on the author's build too. The plan still carries the author's numbers.
data.versus_proto: Reviewer's render beside the prototype (before the first lattice shift, and the image after it): same look, cell clusters inside bubbles at the same size and density, FFT radially symmetric, sphere clusters of the same character in 3D. Differences: layout, as the hash bits differ and the first lattice is turned 17 degrees and shifted where the prototype's is on the axes at the origin. 3D layers are turned in x y where the prototype only shifts them. Cell tone needs a source remap (Distance Function=Euclidean, Output Min=1, Output Max=-2.6) because stock defaults to Euclidean squared. The real volume at this framing shows smaller spheres and more cut faces than the saved prototype volume, whose framing was not recorded. The prototype's first layer sits on the origin too, so it would have the z = 0 hole the first build had; its images come from other slices.
data.plan_changes: Author's, reviewed and kept: 1) Cell Size removed. The prototype's cell is a lattice frequency, and with the source on its own Feature Scale it only repeated this node's Feature Scale. 2) Every layer is turned by 0.3, 0.85, 1.35 radians in x y in all dimensions; not benched on its own. 3) The move is added in world units, so outside bubbles the source sees the exact input position. 4) One division rather than a reciprocal. Reviewer's: 6) The first layer is shifted too, by the same per axis shift as the others, which the plan and prototype did not do, because z = 0 and w = 0 lay on lattice planes. 7) Feature Scale is limited inside the node to frequency 1e6 and move scale 1e6. 8) Eps is stored as 1 / Eps. The plan's bench numbers and the note of 4 of 4000 at Eps=0.05 Iterations=3, now 6, are the author's.

data.versus_proto: The Sphere, Cylinder and Torus part was never prototyped, as the catalogue says. The merged DomainPolar has a look test the author missed: lm_lens mode 19 show 1. Reviewer rendered it beside Log Polar on FBm: features grow from the centre the same way. The prototype is a 6 fold kaleidoscope with visible mirror creases from atan2; the node has no creases and no symmetry, since Symmetry and Mirror were left out. Rendered and looked at: Cylinder repeats along x with no line; Torus repeats 2 x 2 under a Terrace with no line; a globe resampled from the 2:1 Sphere output in numpy shows no pinch or seam at the poles or the wrap; Polar gives tree rings at small Period X and sun spokes at large; Log Polar gives infinite zoom cells and an Escher style checker. Matches the catalogue's look text, except that the catalogue's cube sphere and symmetric planets were not built.
data.plan_changes: 1) Scale replaced by Period X and Period Y in world units, the catalogue's names. One number cannot make non square tiles or a 2:1 map, and with radius = Period X / 2 pi features keep the source's world size. 2) Min Radius default 1, not 0.01, since it is now in world units beside Period X = 1024, and it goes under the root instead of clamping, which keeps the centre smooth. 3) Polar mode added beside Log Polar, the catalogue's Linear radial mode; one line of code and a look Log Polar does not have. 4) Left out to keep it small: CubeSphere, Stereographic, OctaFold, Twist, Symmetry, Mirror. A cube sphere caller already has 3D positions and can use GenPositionArray. 5) 3D Torus, which the catalogue calls unsupported, drifts the tile along a fixed 4D direction, which gives evolving tiles at no cost. In 3D, z passes on as the fourth axis in Cylinder, Polar and Log Polar, and Sphere uses z as height. 4D input is identity, as the catalogue says. Also not mentioned by the author: DomainPolar's spherical 3D mode was left out, and the mapping's z is cylindrical only.
