data.check: 14 graphs on seeds 1337, 42, -7: every Axis, Falloff, connected Rate and Swirl, --scale 8, all presets: 0 FAIL. Worst feature set difference from AVX2 5.2e-05 (SSE2, SSE41) and 1.3e-05 (AVX512), 0% of samples off by more than 1e-2; grid, positions and single agree to 9.3e-06. WARNs are the source's: 'WARN  range: observed [-1.194, 1.206]' on 3 octave FBm alone, and on Screw sheets 'WARN  seed sensitivity' and 'WARN  continuity 4D: worst step ratio 0.00 on axis 3', because that stripe source ignores seed and w. Odd members (Rate and Swirl 1e30 and -1e30, Falloff -50, 1e-30, 1e-10, 1e30, Axis W): 0 FAIL, no NaN. Exact identities, largest difference: Axis Z or W with Swirl 0 in 2D against the bare source 0; Axis Y with Rate 0 in 2D against the source in 3D at z = 0, 0; past Falloff 0 over 191447 samples; distance from the axis kept to 2.4e-07 under Swirl 3 and Rate 0.05. REVIEW: rebuilt and rerun by the reviewer. 49 graphs across the four nodes, 78 check runs, presets on seed 9001 and new graphs on 9001 and 0, including nested twists, hybrid Rate and Swirl and negative values: 0 FAIL for this node. One seam flag, 3 of 4000 in 3D with Swirl and Rate from Simplex, where Simplex has its own 3D jumps. After the turn guard the AVX512 figure above is 5.1e-06, and on the author's 14 graphs total FAIL is still 0. 3936 renders of odd values across the lane, each float and hybrid at 0, -1, +-1e-30, 1e-10, +-1e6, 1e18, 1e19, +-1e30, +-1e38, near the origin, at the exact centre for Stamp, and at scale 1e6: no NaN, no crash. Odd values the author did not show do fail one gate: Swirl 1e6 fails fnlab check with 72% of SSE2 and SSE41 samples off by more than 1e-2, and 98% at 1e8, because the limit is the turn and not the position. Swirl 1e5 and Rate 1000 pass. At Rate 0.01, 1 and 100 alike parity holds to a turn of 1e5 and breaks at 1e6: 28 to 39% off, by up to 0.09. The description now says so. Falloff below 1e-19 made the inverse inf, so inf * 0 on the axis, and Rate 1e38 with Falloff or with Swirl -1e38 made a NaN angle. x86 Min and Max clear those inside SinCos, but FastSIMD uses vmaxq_f32 and wasm_f32x4_max on ARM and WASM, which keep a NaN. Now the inverse is floored and a turn past 1e9 or NaN is no turn. Read from source, not run on ARM or WASM.
data.seams: fnlab seams on the 14 graphs: 0 of 4000 above 0.02 in 2D, 3D and 4D, worst 0.0147 over 0.001.
data.far: DomainOffset on Perlin(Feature Scale=70), Rate 0.01, Axis Y. Finite and std 0.25 to 0.29 at every distance from 0 to 1e8. Along the axis, p99 step along y 0.035 to 0.058 up to 1e7 with the source alone 0.027 to 0.037, then 0.247 at 1e8 with the source 0.162, which is position rounding. Off the axis it is the first check of the plan: p99 step along y 0.037 at 0, 0.073 at 100, 0.251 at 1000, 0.905 at 1e4 and 0.88 to 0.95 past that, so a Feature Scale 70 source is noise from about 7000 = Feature Scale / Rate. With Falloff 300 the same offsets read 0.019 to 0.022, like the source. Feature sets: AVX512 matched AVX2 exactly in these far runs. SSE2 and SSE41 against AVX2: off the axis 2.1e-04 at 1e5, 1.8e-03 at 1e6, 0.026 on 1.8% of samples at 1e7, 0.26 on 8.8% at 1e8; along the axis 2e-06 up to 1e7, 0.088 on 38.5% at 1e8. The source alone stays at 1e-06. Both limits are in the description. REVIEW: spot checks agree: off the axis p99 step along y 0.037, 0.073, 0.251, 0.905 at 0, 100, 1000, 1e4 and 0.019 to 0.022 with Falloff 300. The non-FMA limit along the axis is a limit on the turn: Rate 1 and Rate 100 break at 1e6 and 1e4 world units, not 1e8.
data.tile: Real 4D form. fnlab tile ratio 0.65 to 1.66 over the 14 graphs at --scale 1, and the seam line ranks in the middle of all lines over 10 seeds, mean rank 0.28 of 1, so no seam. The tile does not look like a twist: on the torus the turn acts as a shear between the circles of the image, so Axis Y gives wavy chevrons. The description says so.
data.range: Inherits the source's value, with no ScaleOutput and no VariableRange: gate 4's constant does not apply, since the node only moves positions. With Axis X or Y in 2D the range is that of the source in 3D, since it is sampled there.
data.bench: fnlab bench, ns/sample, 2D / 3D / 4D, smaller of 2 runs. Constant alone: AVX2 0.19 / 0.23 / 0.29. Node on Constant: SSE41 1.32 / 1.56 / 1.75, AVX2 0.70 / 0.81 / 0.87, AVX512 0.46 / 0.63 / 0.69. With Falloff: AVX2 0.77 / 0.93 / 0.98. Axis Y on Perlin: AVX2 2.70 / 2.86 / 4.86, where 2D costs a 3D source. So about 0.5 ns of its own on AVX2 against the queue's 0.3. fnlab bench has no SSE2 row. The first draft indexed the plane at run time and took AVX2 1.29 / 1.65 / 1.11 and SSE41 3.98 / 3.61 / 1.97 on Constant, so the axes are now compile time. Presets, AVX2 2D / 3D / 4D: Whirlpool 4.07 / 7.70 / 14.95, Spiral bands 2.59 / 4.17 / 6.18, Helical ribs 2.89 / 3.21 / 5.17, Vortex column 7.40 / 7.72 / 13.42, Screw sheets 1.83 / 2.18 / 2.52. REVIEW, fnlab bench, smaller of 2 runs, same list on b2a1f6f and then with the turn guard. Author's numbers reproduced within noise. Node on Constant AVX2 0.68 / 0.79 / 0.85 before, 0.72 / 0.85 / 0.92 after; with Falloff 0.76 / 0.92 / 0.97 before, 0.80 / 0.95 / 0.99 after; SSE41 1.38 / 1.64 / 1.79, AVX512 0.49 / 0.68 / 0.75. Axis Z on Perlin AVX2 1.44 / 2.83 / 4.78 before, 1.44 / 2.93 / 4.89 after, with Perlin alone moving 0.91 / 2.13 / 4.14 to 0.93 / 2.22 / 4.24 between those runs, so the guard costs about 0.03 ns. Whirlpool in 3D on AVX2 is noisy, 7.74 to 10.67 between runs.
data.versus_proto: Never prototyped, so there is no image to compare. Judged by eye on gray and vol sheets: worth shipping. The 2D whirlpool (Axis Z, Swirl, Falloff) is the best look and a graph cannot make it. In 3D the twist reads on Vortex column and Helical ribs and only moderately on Screw sheets. The default in 2D (Axis Y) shows a shear, not a swirl, because a 2D slice through a Y twist is not a vortex, and the preview is the first thing a user sees. Presets use Axis Z for that reason. REVIEW: the plan names no prototype image for tier 3 and the prototypes have none for this node. Looked and at Whirlpool and Vortex column: the swirl and the column read as described.
data.plan_changes: 1) Swirl added as a hybrid, from the catalogue's Swirl and Angle merged: without it the node has no effect at all in 2D with Axis Z and no vortex column. 2) Axis W added, it turns x y by w. 3) Falloff is a compact radius with ( 1 - r^2 / F^2 )^3 and not the catalogue's Exp: cheaper, and past the radius the source sees the exact input position. 4) No Center members, a DomainOffset above the node moves the axis. 5) 2D with Axis X or Y evaluates the source in 3D at z = 0, as DomainRotate does, so it is a true slice. 6) Cost in the plan replaced by bench numbers, about 0.5 ns against 0.3.
data.notes: No real problem left. Without Falloff the node is only useful within Feature Scale / Rate of the axis, by what a twist is.

data.versus_proto: Same world sizes, looked. Marble: same hooks and eyes on bands once amplitude was corrected, first render at equal A was stronger than the prototype. Plates: same flat plates, the real node has dotted aliasing on a few edges at the thumb size and the relief still draws comb at the cliffs as the critic reported for the prototype. Plates show stripes above a step of about 0.25 features, as the critic reported. Jet bands: same rollups along band edges, but real bands are straight and periodic because the preset leaves out the prototype jm bend, and it reads grayer since Source is a plain sine. Storms: the graph gives a large hook on seed 555 but a less clean spiral than the prototype image, ovals come from cellular bumps rather than its hash discs. Path Average: same swirled streaks, prototype has more contrast and fine grain from its finer source. 3D: same folds in all directions, both show small patches of aliased grain. Lattice imprint from Perlin (T shapes in the marble) is unchanged, a connected SuperSimplex gives softer hooks without it, matching the critic.
data.plan_changes: 1. Warp Amplitude scale: Warp Amplitude = 0.75 x prototype A x Feature Scale, since the prototype rms speed is 0.75, not the 1 its comment says (mean displacement 0.693 against 0.92 here). Flow prototype L maps to 1.6 x L x Feature Scale. 2. Gradient mode descends at positive amplitude, so A=-3.33 is +2.5 x Feature Scale. 3. Guidance is on total path length, not per step length: at a fixed amplitude more steps make folds sharper, not cleaner, since 12 steps at 1.2 x is flagged in 3D where 4 steps at 2 x barely is. L <= 1 per feature still holds as the clean range. 4. Clamps: Steps 1 to 64, Step Decay 0 to 1, connected gradient to +-16 after scaling, which never reached on smooth potentials (5 octave SuperSimplex peaks at 12). No per step length clamp: not tried, a per axis clamp would push tangled flow towards diagonals rather than untangle it, and the limit that matters is total path length. 5. Step lengths are normalised to sum to 1, unlike the prototype, so Step Decay does not change Warp Amplitude. Path Average weights samples by step length. Kept per plan though the critic asked to remove Step Decay; descent at 0.21 features per step is clean without it. 6. Added a constant seed offset for the potential, not in the plan: psi is conserved along its own curl, so Perlin at the same seed and Feature Scale as Source does not warp at all. 7. 3D Curl differs by path: built in uses grad phi x grad psi from two channels of one lattice visit via GradientNoise::Internal::PerlinKernel, K1 is unchanged. Connected uses one potential per step with a cycling axis, as in prototype ax3, so 2 steps or fewer stay anisotropic and it does not vanish on a seed insensitive potential. 8. The base Warp Amplitude member description, which says maximum, is overridden for this node. 9. K2 Step (fourth root law) is not used, as its own comment advises when no Laplacian is needed. Tap distance fixed at 0.02 x Feature Scale, Jet stencil. gMetadataVectorSize left alone.

All are in the member text. Under a Domain Warp Fractal the noise position advances at the base frequency, since Warp gets no octave frequency, so higher octaves advect less than a true multi octave flow. 2 octave Progressive passes check, 3 octaves weighted flags 46 of 4000 in 3D. Not mine, but it affects these merged nodes: compiling FastNoiseCpp11Include.cpp at /std:c++14 finds std::clamp errors in ExchangeFoam.h 1, Scatter.h 8, SpanningMaze.h 2, SteerablePerlin.h 4, TileDomain.h 4, TubeNoise.h 1, Wallpaper.h 2. That test target is C++11 and FASTNOISE2_TESTS is off in lab builds, so it has not shown up. DomainWarpFlow.h has none. Storms recipe, left out of the presets at 632 ns 2D AVX2. Read 4 of the 6 allowed images.

data.versus_proto: Same world sizes, looked. Thumb: same combed fibres and veins with even detail and no plateaus, only the layout differs since the hash and seed rotation differ. Relief: same layered mesas and wind sheared slopes. Vol: curved folded sheets where the prototype has flat lamellae, which is the 2D noise per shear the plan asked for. Steps sweep agrees with the critic: 1 straight bands, 2 crosshatch, clean at 3. Periodic 3 at 9 steps: curling smoke on seeds 1337 and 7. Marbled paper, strain 1.5, has dotted aliasing on its thinnest lines at thumb size. Parabola on a regular source was not rendered here, the textile warning in its member text is the prototype critic's. Reviewer: the thumbnail beside a fresh Marble thumb on seed 99, read both: same combed fibres, dark veins and hillshade bands with blue basins, no plateaus, layout differs. The gallery images are from 733d7d8, the fix moves positions by rounding only on presets.
data.plan_changes: 1. Warp Amplitude is the distance of the first step, Warp Amplitude / Feature Scale is the prototype amp, and the prototype's unit is 64 world units at fnlab's thumb and vol sizes, so per=2,amp=0.6,freq=0.3 is Feature Scale 213, Warp Amplitude 128, Source Feature Scale 64. The default 50 over 100 is strain 0.5, so the node looks right unset. The base class text says maximum, the member text is replaced with the measured numbers. 2. Seed rotation does not turn the table: the position turns into the table's frame once per lane, by D - 1 rational rotations from one hash, and the travel turns back at the end. The prototype's per lane table offset in 3D and 4D would need a gather. 3. Tables: the prototype's Fibonacci sphere and random frames are replaced by one constexpr walk of orthonormal frames, turned by the golden angle in the next coordinate plane each frame, 2D is still the golden angle sequence. An additive recurrence I tried first gave linearly dependent frames. 4. 2D noise per shear is also used in 4D, not only in 3D: 4D cost rises from 6.82 to 10.81 at 6 steps AVX2, and the rosettes in the tile are gone. Periodic 3 stays on 1D noise in 3D and 4D as in the prototype, and cycles 4 axes in 4D. 5. 1D noise uses GetValueCoord, since one multiply over one lattice axis is a Weyl sequence at seed 0. 6. Clamps: Steps 1 to 32, Lacunarity 1 to 4, below 1 each step moves further than the last and it failed, Gain 0 to 2. Periodic 3 ignores Lacunarity and Gain. 7. Amplitude Scaling applies to the final move only, the chain itself runs at Warp Amplitude. 8. Parabola scale is 0.331 cycles per unit and 0.8 amplitude, from the prototype's freq 0.625 and amp 1, so it reads the same strain at the same settings and moves about twice as far. 9. The plan's aliasing at 21 Periodic steps did not reproduce on seed 7 here: 0 of 4000, worst 0.0063, 0 FAIL. Left as guidance in words only. Reviewer: 10. Moves that overflow leave the position alone, and Warp returns at most 1 for Weighted Strength, see check. 11. The plan note on 21 Periodic steps is seed specific, see seams, the member text now says steep lines past about 20. 12. Under a Domain Warp Fractal the chain runs at Warp Amplitude x the node's own frequency while the octave samples at the fractal's frequency, as Warp receives no octave frequency. That is part of why area is lost there, which the description already says. Left as is.

data.plan_changes: 1. Slope Reference default 0.6 became 0.09 and is now source height per gully cell, not per proto unit: proto 0.6 at s0=0.15 is 0.09, and a whole graph now scales cleanly. 2. Jet plus the centre is 4 taps where the proto's forward differences use 3, which costs one more source evaluation, 3.1 ns on the test FBm in 2D. 4. No ScaleOutput or VariableRange, see range. 5. Mask stays in Output as planned, though the critic suggested dropping it. 6. The 4D form pairs (x, z) and (y, w) to match GenTileable2D, not the scalar proof's (x, y) and (z, w), and its taps rotate along the circles. 7. Feature Scale default 10 needs a const_cast on the mixin's metadata entry and a constructor SetScale; the C API reports 10.0. 8. K1 analytic base not taken, so any source works.

Parity vs AVX2 on SSE2, SSE41 and AVX512: 0.0000% of samples off by more than 1e-2 for every Perlin, Value and warp graph, also at K=8 with Feature Scale 6 where walls are dense. Worst seen is CellularDistance source at Feature Scale 8: 0.0102% on AVX512, below the 0.2% limit, and only on that stock source. WARN lines: Label 'continuity ... worst step ratio 1.00' in 2D, 3D, 4D on every source, by design. Single seed tile WARNs at the default seed: 'WARN tileable: seam 0.0664 interior 0.0218 (ratio 3.05)' on Margin Feature Scale 60, gone at seeds 42, 7 and -5, also Phases=2 ratio 5.00, Seed Stride 2147483647 ratio 6.00, CellularDistance ratio 4.67, node driven Margin Gain ratio 2.69, and 'WARN tileable: seam 0.0000 interior 0.0000 (ratio 0.00), std 0.000' on Value Feature Scale 90 where one label covers the small check tile. The check reads 2 lines of a tile holding few features; see the tile field for the 64 seed numbers on these settings. Only a nonsense setting fails: Margin Gain=-3 gives 'FAIL non-constant', the output is a constant Output Min, and the member description says so. Reviewer: rebuilt from source and re-ran check and seams on all 5 presets, 0 FAIL, same WARN lines. The default Label on Perlin Feature Scale 128 gives 'WARN tileable: seam 0.0332 interior 0.0010 (ratio 34.00)' at the check's seed; an independent GenTileable2D test at the check's own size (128, step 2) over 32 seeds gives ratio 1.10, and 1.05 at 256^2, so that WARN is the check's tiny interior on a one-or-two-region tile, not a seam. Odd values, none crash or give NaN: Phase Offset 0, -1000, 1e9 pass; Phase Offset 3e38 gives 'FAIL simd parity 99.8%' (the source is sampled at 2e38, where float to int conversion differs between feature sets, as any DomainOffset of that size would) and 1e39 (inf) gives a constant Output Min; Margin Gain 0 and 1e9 and 1e39 give constants (Output Min, Output Max, Output Max), Margin on a Constant source with gain 1e39 gives Output Min, no NaN; Seed Stride 0 and -2147483648 pass; Phases 1 and 100 clamp to 2 and 16; Output Min=Max gives a constant; Output Min > Max inverts. Margin on White() fails parity 7% and entry parity, but White() alone fails the same lines at 19.6%, so that is the source.

data.versus_proto: Looked at proto K=5,koff=1,src=0 and out=2,gain=5 beside the real node at Feature Scale 128, seed 7 in the sheet stats and default seed in the thumbs. Same look: curved blobs of mixed size, enclaves, any-to-any junctions, tablelands with gullies between them. Field differs because the node runs the stock Perlin and its hash. Stats close: Label std 0.705 vs 0.705, skew 0.10 vs 0.10, kurt 1.79 vs 1.68, beta 2.91 vs 2.95. Margin mean 0.379 vs 0.397, std 0.691 vs 0.683, beta 5.08 vs 5.15. The `axis` stat is 19.1 vs 13.1 on Label and 10.5 vs 8.2 on Margin, not chased: it is large on both and I saw no axis alignment in the renders. The prototype's thumbnail is more angular than plain Perlin, the warped camouflage preset is the nearer match to it. No facet source exists among real nodes yet, so that proto variant was not compared. Gumbel, Rank, Softmax and facet shade outputs are left out as planned. Reviewer looked at the node, the plan's image (warped Perlin source) and the camouflage preset: same family of shapes; the proto thumb has larger, rounder plates and the Camouflage preset has more stringy regions from the warp amplitude, which is a parameter difference, not a port difference.
data.plan_changes: Added a `Phase Offset` float member, default 1000 world units. The plan calls the offset mandatory but lists no member, and the proto offset was in lattice units, which a modifier cannot do because it does not know the source's Feature Scale. Without it (Phase Offset=0) K=8 Perlin has 99.8% of lattice vertices with 4 or more labels within r=.03 cell, 0.0 to 0.1% with it at any Feature Scale from 10 to 10000. Usable range measured: ties return at 0.033x Feature Scale (21.5% at r=.1) and 0.01x (96.1%); position quantisation shows at Feature Scale 0.01 with K=16 (54% of neighbour steps exactly 0). Also: no default source is possible, since FastNoise nodes have none, so the Source description asks for a cheap one instead; `gMetadataVectorSize` not bumped, it is reservation only. Reviewer confirmed the Phase Offset claim: Perlin128 K8, circle r=4 px around phase-0 lattice vertices, Phase Offset 0 gives 100% of vertices with 4 or more labels, 1000 gives 0% (random centres 0%).

data.name: FaultLines
data.check: Reviewed build 04f5b79. fnlab check: 0 FAIL on the author's 32 edge settings and Feature Scale 1 and 1000, on the default and all 5 presets at seeds 1337, 7, 90210, -5, on 7 new setups, and on a real multi seed run through CellularLookup. SSE2, SSE41 and AVX512 against AVX2: 0.0000% of samples off by more than 1e-2 on the default and presets, worst 0.0020% (Offset strata seed -5, AVX512; Tip 0.1). Default on Perlin has 3 WARNs, the jumps the node exists to make: 'WARN  continuity 2D: worst step ratio 1.00 on axis 0 (8 = Lipschitz, ~1 = jumps), max slope 418.155 per feature', 3D 1.36, 4D 1.57. Zone Resist 0, Slip 0, Density 0 and Fault Count 0 give 0 WARN. NaN and Inf: 0 on 81 odd trees in 4 feature sets, 2D and 3D, and 0 in the 80 check runs of 0, negative and huge members. The author's build gave NaN at Feature Scale 0, 1e-40, 1e38, Spacing 1e38, Slip +-1e38, Tip 1e-40 and Dip 1e20 and up; fixed. FAIL lines that remain only at absurd values and are stated: parity at Feature Scale 1e6, Spacing 1e6, Slip 1e3 and 1e6, for example 'FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 1.63e+00 3D 1.22e+00 4D 1.11e+00, samples off by >1e-2: 71.2931%' at Slip 1e3; parity at Throw 1e6 and up, where the difference is rounding of values that size; 'FAIL  non-constant: std 0.00000' at Spacing 1e20, where the source is read at about 1e21 and stock DomainOffset does the same at 1e38. Limits inside plausible settings, measured on 3 to 4 seeds and now in the description: Slip 3 is clean, Slip 5 is marginal with grid against positions 1.06e-03 on 1 of 4 seeds, Slip 30 fails parity at 1.74%; Slip 0.5 with Tip 0.1 and Slip 1 with Tip 0.2 fail only entry parity at 2e-03 to 1e-02; Spacing 50 is clean, Spacing 100 fails parity at 0.31% on 1 of 3 seeds. That is Slip * Spacing / Tip above about 5. Fault Count 16 is clean to Slip 2 and fails at Slip 5.
data.seams: GATE FAILS AS WRITTEN, BY DESIGN: fnlab seams exits 1 at the defaults and on 4 of 5 presets at seeds 1337 and 90210, because a hard break along each trace is what the node is for. Default on Perlin: 2D 3187 of 4000 worst 1.3333, 3D 2976 of 4000 worst 0.9799, 4D 2584 of 4000 worst 1.0471. To show there are no other jumps the break was turned off: Zone Resist 0 is clean on 2D, 3D and 4D, worst 0.0002 at the default, on the author's list apart from Tip 0.2, and on 5 setups they did not run plus the default (Spacing 0.37 with Fault Count 11, Jitter 0.33 with Zone 0.67, Jitter 0 with Zone 1, Dip 3 with Dip Slip 0.2, Simplex source) at seeds 7, -424242 and 2147483647, worst 0.0067 on Simplex 3D and 0.0007 otherwise. Drag folds uses Zone Resist 0 and exits 0. A real limit on short Tip at Zone Resist 0 and 6 families, compounding stretch rather than a lattice jump: Tip 0.1 flags 2D 1788 of 4000 worst 1.2765, 3D 28, 4D 488; Tip 0.2 flags 2D 237, 4D 9; Tip 0.3 flags 2D 29 worst 0.0871; Tip 0.5 and 1 are clean, worst 0.0135 and 0.0013. Tip 0.2 is clean at Fault Count 1 and 2 and flags 14 at 3. The Tip description says so.
data.far: fnlab check's own far coordinate test passes ('far coordinates: std 0.305 vs near 0.313' at the default). Wrapped in DomainOffset on X and Y at Feature Scale 64, over seeds 1337, 7, 90210, -5, SSE2 and SSE41 against AVX2: 2e5 and 5e5 pass, worst 0.0732%; 1e6 fails on 1 of 4 seeds at 0.3642%; 2e6 fails on all 4 at 1.16 to 2.55%; 5e6 at 5.8 to 10.8%; 1e7 at 9.74%. AVX512 is 0.0000% everywhere. For scale, DomainRotate(Yaw=30) on Perlin at 1e7 is 17.5% and bare Perlin passes. Cause: the build uses /fp:fast and FMA, so the dot with a family normal rounds differently with and without FMA and samples flip across a trace. Past about 1e9 the grid step is below float resolution and the output is constant, as for any node. The description says about 500000 world units. Each feature set stays deterministic on its own and the output stays finite to 1e38 in all 4 sets.
data.tile: Real 4D form, so GenTileable2D closes by construction. check seam ratio at seed 1337: default 0.95, Offset strata 1.23, Drag folds 0.75, Fault block terrain 0.38, Broken agate 1.40, Faulted layers 0.60. Those compare the seam to one interior line, so on a field with sharp features one image says little: Drag folds reaches 4.45 at seed 90210. Ranked among every column and row step over 8 seeds the seam is at percentile 57 default, 35, 61, 50, 50, 57 on the presets, an ordinary step. I looked at the 2x2 tile: no visible seam. Limits: traces are curves in a tile, since a 4D plane cuts the torus that way (in the description), and a tile holds few faults at a large Feature Scale, so a tile looks like a few curved lenses rather than the long straight traces of the plane.
data.range: No ScaleOutput and no VariableRange: this is a domain modifier and without Throw the output is a Source value at a moved position. Throw 1, Slip 0 on Constant 0: 1 family -0.943..0.947 std 0.381, 3 families -1.733..1.563 std 0.521, 6 families -2.661..3.107 std 0.833, 16 families -5.555..4.502 std 1.371. Limit is +-Fault Count * Throw and the node does not clamp, the description of Throw says so. Fault block terrain measures -1.558..1.567 in check.

Zone Width 0 AVX2 9.02 / 10.59 / 12.66. Slip as a Perlin node AVX2 14.93 / 17.57 / 21.94. The review fixes cost about 0.5 ns over the author's AVX2 13.57 / 14.75 / 18.39, which I reproduced on 723cc58 as 13.52 / 14.71 / 17.39.
data.versus_proto: Reviewer's look, one contact sheet: prototype thumb and fault_drag_tips beside real Offset strata, Drag folds, Broken agate and default, prototype relief and vol beside real. Same read as the prototype's thumb: stacked bands cut by long straight traces, wedges between crossing faults, offsets that die out at tips. Differences: the prototype's strata source is built in with thin smooth edges, and stock nodes give hard band edges. With Grid Jitter 0.25 the Offset strata band edges are close to the prototype, some zigzag remains where a cell row steps. The prototype's default pre-warps by 0.3, not in the plan, so its traces bend slightly and the node's are straight; a DomainWarp above the node gets that back. Drag folds is softer and more folded than the prototype's drag image, which keeps breaks; it is the Zone Resist 0 end of the same range. Relief: Fault block terrain has longer, clearer scarps and fewer of them than the prototype's relief, which is busier with more short cuts. Vol: Faulted layers has the same offset layers but fewer visible cut planes than the prototype, whose dark fault faces read more strongly, and shows some fine hatching on steep drag zones in the fnlab view.
data.plan_changes: 1. 4D is written, the plan said not attempted. Normals are points on the hypersphere kept away from the pure xz and yw planes, and slip and strike are the two quaternion turns perpendicular to the normal and to each other. The choice is arbitrary as the plan said, but it tiles. Dip and Dip Slip are 3D only. 2. Family direction tables are per node, not per seed. Lanes can each carry their own seed and a table lookup per lane would be slow, so the seed turns the whole set by one hashed angle, about Y in 3D and in both GenTileable2D planes in 4D. Family angles therefore keep their relative spread across seeds. 3. Zone Width is limited to 1 - Boundary Jitter so it fits the thinnest slab; without that, Zone Resist 0 would still jump at the near boundary. The default 0.25 is not affected. 4. No ScaleOutput or VariableRange, since the output is the Source value. The prototype's clamp is dropped. 5. 6. Fault Count is capped at 16, for the fixed tables. 7. Prototype params outside the plan's member list are not members: pre, tipb, fold, lfreq, tilt, src, angjit, dirseed. tipb is fixed at 0. Review: 8. Tip has a floor of 0.1, since shorter values failed entry parity at the default Slip and gave NaN at 1e-40. 9. Dip is clamped to +-1000 and Throw to +-1e30. 10. Offset strata preset now has Grid Jitter 0.25, Feature Scale 26.

data.notes: Status is ok-with-notes rather than ok for two measured reasons. fnlab seams exits 1 at the default settings, which is the plan's design, and Zone Resist 0 is the continuous mode if a graph needs one. Feature set parity fails from 1e6 world units, between 5e5 and 1e6 at Feature Scale 64. Discontinuous output limits the default to textures and height fields: do not use it as a warp source or slope input without Zone Resist 0. Source must have structure: on plain FBm the faults show only as thin hairlines. Not tested: a real multi-seed batch, since the C API gives one seed per call, and any compiler other than clang-cl 23. I reviewed it against the plan and prototype, re-ran everything, and changed only metadata text. Build warnings: 4, all the same 'unused type alias' in FastSIMD's Trig.h, none in this node. Images read: 4 of 6, all contact sheets. REVIEW: numbers above were replaced by the reviewer's on 04f5b79. The far limit in the old text moved a little with the new hash: 1e6 now fails on 1 of 4 seeds rather than always. Multi seed lanes are now tested through CellularLookup: 0 FAIL.
data.review: Independent review of 723cc58. Defects fixed in 04f5b79: slab hash correlation (nearby slab slips, worst |corr| 0.41 at lag 1 and 0.48 at lag 2 across seeds, measured on the real node as -0.325 at seed 1382 lag 1, now +0.011); NaN at huge or tiny members; Fault Count text had the offset direction backwards.

data.versus_proto: Never prototyped, so there is no prototype image; compared with stock Perlin. Phase 0 matches Perlin. Phase 0.3 looked a little streakier to the eye, but the numbers do not back that: angular spectrum max/min over half a loop 1.24 to 1.49 against stock 1.43, axis against diagonal slope 0.994 to 1.005 in 2D and 0.897 to 0.998 in 3D against stock 0.954 (review/flow_aniso.txt), so no anisotropy pulse beyond what Perlin has. No video eval exists and nothing was watched in motion: the image and numbers stand. Spatial std is flat over the loop (0.302 to 0.306 in 2D). Mean step between 24 frames is 0.099 to 0.100 in 2D. Correlation with frame 0 at eighths of the loop: +1.00 +0.36 -0.50 -0.36 -0.01 -0.35 -0.50 +0.35. Verdict: dull as a still, worth shipping only for the loop.
data.plan_changes: Phase is in turns and is wrapped with a floor first, so whole numbers give identical bits. Plain Perlin-Neyret rotates every gradient at one rate, which makes Phase + 0.5 the exact negative of the field (author measured |f(0) + f(.5)| max 1.79e-07), so half the corners turn the other way at twice the speed: correlation at half a turn goes from -1.00 to -0.01. 2D and 4D use one gradient dot with the offset rotated; 3D has no such rotation and takes two dots, hash and hash ^ 2. Review: an infinite or NaN Phase is treated as turn 0.

data.name: FlowShingle
data.check: fnlab check: 0 FAIL, 2 WARN on default and all 5 presets. Both WARNs are the continuity check on 2D and 4D, which is the jump by design: "WARN  continuity 2D: worst step ratio 1.00 on axis 0 (8 = Lipschitz, ~1 = jumps), max slope 453.734 per feature" on default. SSE2, SSE41 and AVX512 against AVX2: 0.0000% of samples off by more than 1e-2 on all 6, worst max diff 1.23e-04 (Brush strokes, AVX512, 2D). Entry parity worst 2.16e-05. 36 edge settings run: Size, Elongation, Jitter, Priority Jitter, Bristle, Chevron, Rim, Rim Width, Tone, Detail, Base, Tilt, Angle and Feature Scale at extremes, White on Angle and Interior: 0 NaN/Inf on all 36. FAIL lines seen, all off the presets. Size 0 and -3: "FAIL  non-constant: std 0.00000", stamps floor at 1e-3 cells so the output really is Base. Angle 1e6: "FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 8.31e-01 3D 1.21e-01 4D 7.23e-01, samples off by >1e-2: 29.7689%" and the same for SSE41; Angle -1e9: "FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 1.37e+00 3D 2.00e+00 4D 1.39e+00, samples off by >1e-2: 89.8071%" and the same for SSE41; Angle 3e5: 18.1885%; Angle 1e5 passes. This is PolyMath::SinCos without FMA, a limit stated on the Angle member. Interior Scale U 1e6: "FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 1.13e-01 3D 2.86e-06 4D 8.93e-02, samples off by >1e-2: 11.7981%", "FAIL  simd parity AVX512 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 6.76e-02 3D 0.00e+00 4D 6.73e-02, samples off by >1e-2: 3.8432%", "FAIL  entry parity 2D: grid vs positions 7.99e-02, grid vs single 6.97e-02"; U 1e5: "FAIL  entry parity 2D: grid vs positions 8.12e-03, grid vs single 6.50e-03"; U 1e4 passes. Feature Scale 1e-3 (1000 cells per world unit): "FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 5.76e-01 3D 8.08e-02 4D 6.14e-01, samples off by >1e-2: 1.7639%", "FAIL  entry parity 2D: grid vs positions 3.92e-01, grid vs single 1.48e-02"; Feature Scale 0.1 passes. Probable cause, not isolated: float positions round differently at about 5e5 cells, and a discontinuous output turns that into jumps.
data.seams: GATE FAILS AS WRITTEN, BY DESIGN: fnlab seams exits 1 on default and all 5 presets. 2D and 4D jump at every stamp edge: default 2D 4000 of 4000 worst 1.1369, 4D 4000 of 4000 worst 1.1809; Brush strokes 2D 2268 of 4000 worst 1.8246; Feather barbs 2D 2119 of 4000 worst 1.6401. 3D is a continuous density: 0 of 4000 on all 6, worst 0.0014, and 0 of 4000 at the Size cap, worst 0.0103. Since fnlab seams cannot tell a stamp edge from a lattice seam in 2D and 4D, I tested the window directly. Real build against a control build with no batch skip and a window two cells wider per axis, 14 configs including Size at the cap, shuffled and sorted lanes, 800000 samples 2D, 400000 3D, 120000 4D: 0 samples off by more than 1e-3, except 1 of 800000 in 2D at 1.5e-3 on Stroke at the cap, rounding at the taper. Worst off all others 2.1e-4. So the window cuts no stamp and the batch skip drops none. Positive control, both builds with the Size cap removed: Size 1.3 Elongation 2 Jitter 1 gives 3D 4.3% off worst 2.0, 4D 13.1% worst 0.945; Stroke Size 1 Elongation 3 Jitter 1 gives 2D 45.2% worst 1.714, 3D 9.8%, 4D 14.0%. Straddling scan, % of pairs 2e-3 apart with a jump over 0.02, on lines the window switches on against lines it does not, Jitter 1 at the cap: 2D y 0.369 vs 0.306, x even rows 0.221 vs 0.220, x odd rows 0.220 vs 0.207; 4D 0.368 vs 0.380. At default Jitter 0.3 the 4D rate differs (0.657 vs 0.377) and 2D is lower on window lines (y 0.065 vs 0.180): edges cluster at a set distance from cell centres at low jitter; the wider window comparison above shows 0 window cuts on the same config. The 3D column of that scan counts slopes, thin plates are steep at eps 1e-3, worst 0.046 vs 0.050.
data.far: check far coordinate test passes on all 6. Wrapped in DomainOffset 1e5, 1e6 and 1e7 world units at Feature Scale 48: exit 0, std 0.265, 0.256, 0.253, 0.0000% parity off, entry parity 0. 3D continuity falls to WARN as float positions start to step: ratio 2.00 at 1e5, 1.00 at 1e6, 1.01 at 1e7. No description text: the same float rounding hits every node, and priority is relative to the sample so order stays correct.
data.tile: Real 4D form, so it tiles by construction. check seam ratio: default 0.99, Fish scales 0.87, Roof tiles 0.55, Brush strokes 1.70 after the reviewer's 4D fix (1.97 before), Feather barbs 0.95, Slate plates 0.87. fnlab tile: Fish scales 0.66, Roof tiles 1.16, Brush strokes 1.13 after the fix (2.59 before), Feather barbs 1.13, Slate plates 1.05. One image's seam is few pixel pairs on a jumping output, so I averaged 16 seeds: default 1.41, Fish scales 1.39, Roof tiles 2.30, Brush strokes 1.00, Feather barbs 1.34, Slate plates 1.62. That excess is not a seam: the mean step on the seam row pair matches the pair at b = pi and near pi/2, for example default rows 0.0511 seam, 0.0460 at pi, 0.0484 near pi/2, all rows 0.0319; Roof tiles 0.0165, 0.0163, 0.0160, all 0.0081. Rows where the torus runs along a lattice axis have about 1.5x to 2x the edges of other rows. I did not see bands in the Fish scales tile image, but this is a real unevenness and I did not view it on Roof tiles. Limits: stamps in the tile are sections of 4D stamps, so sizes vary much more than in 2D and rows do not form. 4D draws every shape with Scale shading on its own outline (reviewer fix 9ffa8dd: before it 4D used Elongation for all shapes, so Disc with Elongation 4 had an identical 2D output but a 4D tile std of 0.092 instead of 0.223, and Elongation 1000 emptied the Disc tile). After the fix Disc tiles at std 0.238 whatever Elongation is, and Brush strokes tiles at std 0.337 instead of 0.194, still gappy: 66.3% at its minimum value (69.7% before) because Size 0.45 stamps are thin. Description states the Scale shading, the Stroke loss of taper and Bristle, and the varied sizes.
data.range: ScaleOutput( value, -1, 1 ) over a clamp to -1..1, with VariableRange. The prototype's gain and offset already centre the output, so I kept them instead of stretching to the measured maximum, which by arithmetic would move the default mean to about +0.26. Measured 2D, 1024^2, 4 seeds. Scale default -1..0.555 mean -0.023 std 0.255. Scale with Perlin Interior -1..0.728. Roof params -1..0.835 mean -0.049 std 0.309. Feather params -1..1.000 mean 0.011 std 0.319. Stroke default -1..0.718 mean 0.032 std 0.350. Stroke best params -1..0.915 mean -0.068 std 0.454, 9.2% at -1. Disc default -1..0.558 mean 0.064 std 0.309. So default output does not reach +1: it tops out at 0.555 and only high Detail or Tone gets near it. 3D is -1..1 by construction, saturated inside and far from plates. 4D Scale from tile: -1..0.498 on Fish scales. Base is on the same -1..1 scale, before Output Min and Max.

For scale AVX2: Perlin 0.91 / 2.15 / 4.10, CellularDistance 3.80 / 12.11 / 40.59. Stroke AVX2 6.16 / 10.20 / 30.26. Disc AVX2 4.55 / 10.22 / 30.07. Perlin Interior AVX2 6.14 / 10.16 / 34.85. Feature Scale 8 AVX2 6.66 / 12.11 / 36.70, Feature Scale 400 AVX2 5.00 / 6.48 / 21.06: the batch skip depends on lane coherence. Presets: Fish scales SSE41 17.04 / 28.49 / 77.97, AVX2 7.82 / 12.81 / 38.74, AVX512 5.88 / 10.49 / 28.49. Roof tiles AVX2 7.20 / 10.13 / 31.51. Brush strokes AVX2 11.03 / 14.38 / 49.41. Feather barbs AVX2 9.86 / 13.34 / 44.35. Slate plates AVX2 6.97 / 12.54 / 33.47. Random positions, batch skip idle, min of 2 timed passes through the C API with Python overhead: SSE41 21.39 / 37.55 / 133.58, AVX2 10.45 / 17.02 / 69.66, AVX512 8.30 / 15.62 / 52.29; Fish scales AVX2 14.65 / 20.22 / 78.92. data.versus_proto: Side by side in one sheet: sheet of Fish scales at Feature Scale 48 against the prototype's scales sheet, roof relief, plates vol. Sheet stats nearly match: real mean -0.008 std 0.274 skew -0.35 kurt 2.88 beta 3.34, prototype mean -0.040 std 0.274 skew -0.32 kurt 2.87 beta 3.33. Same rows of blunt scales with striped interiors and the same threshold topology, different individual stamps because the draws differ. Real graph has a curling Angle and the prototype sheet its own flow. Roof relief: same tiles with vertical streaks; the real one at Output -0.28..0.28 is a little spikier and its tiles a little smaller. Vol: same stacked lens plates tilted the same way; the prototype's cube is cut where one plate fills the top face and its flow runs differently, so the two look different in layout but not in kind. FFT: both have the broad star of jump edges. The real 3D XZ slice shows more plates than the prototype's, I did not establish why; different y slice is my guess. Default with no Interior connected has no streaks at all, the prototype had a built in Perlin: the presets connect one. I did not view Stroke or Feather at the final Feature Scale beside a prototype image at those exact params, only the earlier sheet with prototype image, which matches in kind: tapered grooved strokes with black gaps.
data.plan_changes: 1. 4D is written, the plan said not written. Scale shape only over 81 cells, as the plan said it would be. Flow goes round the xz and yw planes, so GenTileable2D shows Angle as the image direction; with a fixed plane the flow would flip across the tile. Cost: a flat 4D slice loses the flow. Stamps are 1.2x larger in 4D to close holes. 2. Each 2D row takes its own four nearest columns, so brick rows no longer shrink the reach on one side. Reach is 2 - Jitter / 2 on both axes and the prototype's reachfix problem goes away. 3. Size cap is exact: the outline's farthest point from the largest eigenvalue of the Chevron sheared quadratic form, instead of the 1.15 fudge. 3D keeps 1.22x under the window so a plate saturates before it leaves. 4. One MixHash per candidate with bit fields instead of one mix per value: 8 bit jitter, size, priority; 6 and 4 bits in 4D. Inverse size is drawn, uniform in 1/s over 0.85s to s, so the loop has no division. 5. Added a whole batch skip with FS::AnyMask, not in the plan: AVX2 went from 11.31 / 15.59 / 67.51 to 5.39 / 10.13 / 30.54 on grids, along with one less multiply in the hash. 6. Priority is relative to the sample, not world position, since only the order at one sample counts. Priority Jitter has a floor of 1e-3 to break exact ties, without it Jitter 0 could pick a different stamp per feature set. 7. 3D output is the prototype's default solid density. Shape, Rim, Interior, Tone, Base and Priority Jitter do nothing in 3D, and in 4D Shape sets only the outline lengths (Stroke symmetric, Disc round, since reviewer fix 9ffa8dd) while Bristle and Chevron do nothing. The plan's cost line counted an Interior eval in every dimension; 3D has none. 8. Interior gets a per stamp seed, not the prototype's coordinate offset, as StampScatter does, and its V follows Chevron. Prototype's Bend, Soft and Stagger are not members, as in the plan's member list; brick rows are always on. 9. No per shape range constants: see range. gMetadataVectorSize left alone.

data.notes: Status is ok-with-notes rather than ok because fnlab seams exits 1 on 2D and 4D: every stamp edge is a jump by design, as the plan says. The wider window comparison is what shows those jumps are not window seams. Discontinuous output limits it to textures: not usable as a warp source or a slope input. Limits: 3D and 4D are other forms, not the 2D look extended. Tiled output has uneven edge density by row. Interior unconnected gives no streaks. Images read: 4 of 6. The control builds were removed after use. To rebuild one: replace the three AnyMask tests with true and widen each window by two cells; the cap-off control also sets size2D, size3D and size4D to mSize and mSize * kSize4D in both builds. REVIEW: rebuilt the DLL; check on default and the 5 presets at seeds 0 and 1234 all 0 FAIL 2 WARN (the by-design continuity WARNs); seams exits 1 on all 6 with 3D 0 of 4000, as reported; 33 further edge settings (Elongation 0.05 and -5, Chevron on Disc and Stroke, Tilt 0, -1.2 and 1e9, negative Interior Scales, Priority Jitter -5 and 1e-9, Rim -1, Rim Width 1e6, Detail -2, Tone -1, Size 1e3 at Jitter 1, Feature Scale 1, 1e9 and 0, FlowShingle as its own Angle and Interior, Angle 1e5, -1e5, pi and a fast Perlin, Seed Offset INT_MIN) gave 0 NaN/Inf and no crash; only Feature Scale 0 and Size 1e-3 are constant, which is degenerate input. Bench re-run matched within noise: default AVX2 5.40 / 10.15 / 30.42, Fish scales 7.71 / 12.69 / 38.86, and after the fix 5.40 / 10.25 / 30.48, Brush strokes 11.05 / 14.64 / 49.12. data.versus_proto: Real beside the prototype. Same mechanism and look: cells grade from large to tiny, mid bands bud small cells along big cell walls with shared walls, not a cross fade. Differences: 1) the prototype images are at levels=5 ratio=2 (result.json), the plan's params are 9 and 1.41, the same total span of about 16x, so the real default steps more gently. The Stained glass preset uses 5 and 2 and is the closer match. 2) The prototype thumb has one big ramp of level across the frame because of its Perlin and seed, with level 0 cells along the bottom. In the real render a Remap of From -1..1 showed few large cells, so the presets map From -.7...7 or -.6...6 to reach level 0. 3) Crack uses Crack Width where the prototype had a fixed gain of 4, Width .25 matches it. 4) Vol iso differs by mapping: prototype F1 is b1 * 1.6 - 1 with iso 0, that is F1 .625, real is 2 * F1 / 1.15 - 1, so about +.09; the preset uses .05. Real pores have a stronger size gradient than the prototype's pore volume; at vol's default window 4 and lsf .1 its cube spans .4 of a period of its level noise, the preset's spans about 1.8. 5) Pillow and F1 relief on their own are spiky columns and cones, since values are in local cell units and fine cells stand as tall as large ones. The prototype relief of out=5 is busy too and its note calls relief not the idea's best view. So no plain relief preset: the relief preset adds Crack to a terrain. REVIEW: a real Pillow at Levels 5 Ratio 2 with a vertical Gradient Level ramp (0 at the bottom, 4 at the top, Feature Scale 32) rendered beside the prototype Pillow panel of the thumbnail shows the same picture: large flat cells at the bottom, a mid band where small cells bud along the big cell walls and share them, tiny cells at the top. Walls are thinner in the real one at Crack Width .12 against the prototype's .25.
data.plan_changes: 1) Blend floor 1.44, not 1.4: F2 of a level is at most 1 + jitter radius, 1.437 in 2D, 1.396 in 3D, 1.366 in 4D (at the cell centre the second nearest centre is 1 away). The result.json bound of 1.144 is F1's, not F2's, and the prototype's 'k>=1.0 is clean' was only on one ramp; the control above shows jumps at 1.0. 2) 4D built, the plan said not built: GenT over the pack with CellWindow gives it for free, and a local site means no 62 KB stack frame. 3) Level 0 cell size is Feature Scale, prototype base .5 dropped. 4) Levels clamped 2 to 16, Ratio .1 to 4, Grid Jitter 0 to 1, Crack Width at least 1e-4. Levels fits the 4 bits of the frequency power. 5) Crack uses Crack Width, not gain 4. 6) Frequency per level by binary powers with MaskedMul instead of Exp or Log: PolyMath.inl records 2% error in FS::Log, and this gives each level one exact number from either pass, by multiplies only. 7) kLevelSeedStride 1013 where the prototype had 31. gMetadataVectorSize untouched. 9) REVIEW FIX: the per level frequency is capped at 65536x (FS::Min after the binary power product, so both passes still agree exactly). The plan's 'Ratio 0.1 to 4 so that the top frequency stays under 2^30' was the wrong bound: position times frequency goes through Convert<int32_t> in CellWindow, so 2^30 overflows at 2 cells of Feature Scale from the origin and the output was a constant 1.0.

data.name: GradientNoise
api: GradientNoise::Simplex( seed, pos... ) -> value, grad[D]   (r^2 = 0.5, stock tables; equals stock Simplex in 2D only)
GradientNoise::SimplexHessian( seed, pos... ) -> value, grad[D], hessian[D(D+1)/2] packed upper triangle by row
GradientNoise::PerlinChannels<C>( seed, valueAmp, pos... ) -> channel[C].value, channel[C].grad[D], C in 1..3
notes: Positions are noise space: after ScalePositions multiply grad by the frequency and hessian by its square. Add mSeedOffset to the seed yourself.
Values are in [-1,1] (PerlinChannels: +-(1 + valueAmp)); derivatives share the scale and are not normalised.

Review fix eea599d+: PerlinChannels channel 2 read its value bits from 28..31, but bit 31 of HashPrimes is always 0, so it had 3 live bits, mean -0.5 x valueAmp and a lower std. Value bits now sit at 19..22, 23..26 and 27..30 (channel 2 through a zero extending shift).

PerlinChannels<3> 4D on AVX2 measures 30 ns after the fix against 19 ns before, at the same instruction count (3835 vs 3858) and spill count; a clang layout effect in a register starved function, not an algorithm change. Channels<1> and <2> are unchanged. Consumers compiling the kernel into their own node will see their own layout.
Only clang-cl 23 was built and run.

SDF clamps at -1 and saturates outside at 1 - reach - 1.25 Smoothness; measured defaults -0.415..0.300, flagstones -0.254..0.100. Stones cross 0 at the surface. Density gain is Max( 2.5, 1 / saturation ), 3.33 at defaults and 10 on flagstones, so edges of big or flat stones get steeper, with no other effect.
data.bench: ns/sample 2D / 3D, min of 2 fnlab bench runs on grids, Feature Scale 32, 2-octave Perlin Height. Height alone SSE41 5.63 / 10.27, AVX2 2.67 / 5.28, AVX512 1.92 / 3.20. Default SSE41 32.50 / 60.15, AVX2 15.24 / 27.24, AVX512 12.24 / 21.40. Constant Height AVX2 8.30 / 17.12. Facet 0 AVX2 13.90 / 24.71. Tilt SSE41 43.51 / 100.97, AVX2 20.98 / 46.12, AVX512 16.65 / 35.88. Exponent 4 AVX2 18.20 / 29.55. Stones Only AVX2 12.88 / 24.52. One timed pass on random positions, where far column skips rarely fire, AVX2: 24.1 / 63.3, Tilt 33.1 / 113.2. The plan's stock CellularLookup rival is 36.8 ns, not re-measured. Plan estimate was 55 ns, 140 with Tilt. REVIEW re-measured, min of 2 rounds, after the Height clamp: default SSE41 30.73 / 59.07, AVX2 13.81 / 25.76, AVX512 11.53 / 20.45; Tilt SSE41 40.59 / 94.95, AVX2 18.45 / 41.19, AVX512 15.56 / 33.46. Within 10% of the report.
data.versus_proto: Chiselled and smooth rubble against the prototype: same broken rock look and same rest on the ground; the proto image is more zoomed out. Flagstones against the prototype: the proto shows larger slabs, with one standing at an angle to the ground near the top of its hill; the real slabs lie along the slope, with more of them because the preset uses Feature Scale 32. That difference fits a sign error in the prototype's alignToNormal, read from its formula: it rotates +y onto the normal, not the normal onto +y, which would tilt a slab 2 theta from the ground. Not run on the prototype. The real thin axis is 0.1 to 0.2 degrees off the normal on 26.6 and 38.9 degree slopes, 26.6 and 38.9 without Tilt. Floating, voxel flood at 16 per column on 3 seeds: 0 floating of 40 to 119 stone clumps per config over 9 configs, control Sink -0.5 floats 46 of 46. REVIEW: node beside the prototype: same chiselled rubble resting on the ground; the prototype image shows two small fragments detached above the hill at its top left, the real render shows none.
data.plan_changes: 1. Added a Rotation float, 0 axis aligned to 1 any rotation. The plan's Exponent note gives flagstones but its best params need rot=0, and the plan had no member for it. Partial rotation comes with it, from the prototype. 2. Tilt rotates the normal onto +y, opposite to the prototype, and uses c d + A x d + A ( A . d ) / ( 1 + c ) with no sqrt or special case. 3. Height evals: 10, or 28 with Tilt, not 9 and 27, as Union Density also reads the ground at the sample. Connected Density adds up to 9. Height is read in 2D from the two axes that are not Up, in units of Feature Scale; share it with a 3D terrain through RemoveDimension. 4. Size cap also takes Slab above 1, Exponent above 2 (3^( 1/2 - 1/e )) and Smoothness, keeping reach + 1.25 Smoothness at most 0.9 columns. The prototype only took Aspect and clamped distance at 1. 5. Stones add a Max with in plane distance - reach, a lower bound of true distance, and output saturates below 1 - reach - 1.25 Smoothness: a stone that leaves the window then has no effect. Without this the approximate SDF of a flat stone is far below true distance at the window edge. 6. Smoothness capped at 0.2, see seams. 7. Jitter stays fixed at the prototype's 1, there is no member in the plan. 8. Facet is capped at 6: fixed icosahedron axes, both sides, 4 hash bits per plane, the prototype's fixn=1 form. 9. 2D: 3 columns along one axis on a fixed row, Height on the line v = 0.37 cells, as in the prototype; Up Axis Z gives a slice at z = 0 through the 3 x 3 columns. Top down height output not written. 10. Whole batch skip of columns too far on every lane to matter, margin 5 Smoothness: AVX2 3D 60.46 to 28.98 ns on the same grid and graph, Tilt 114.10 to 51.36. Lane mix leaves results unchanged (exact 0). No help on random positions.

data.name: HeightBlend
data.check: 0 FAIL on every preset and on an edge matrix (Output modes, connected heights, depth and fade, Height Scale 0, -1, 4, 1e30, Depth 0, -1, 1e-3, 1000, 1e30, zero and reversed fade range). SSE2, SSE41, AVX512 parity against AVX2: 0.0000% of samples off by more than 1e-2 on all of them; worst max diff 4.15e-3 is on the pebble graph and is the same 4.15e-3 on its source A alone. Only FAIL lines seen: "non-constant: std 0.00000" on two deliberately constant test graphs (Constant sources), which is the test input and not the node. WARN range on graphs whose sources exceed 1 (stock FractalRidged reaches 1.87). WARN continuity on graphs with jumping or very steep sources, on connected Simplex heights (the handbook lists Simplex 3D and 4D jumps as pre-existing), on Depth 0, and on Weight where the probe lands in a saturated flat area (slope 0). The seams scan on the same graphs with Perlin heights finds nothing, so those are not node jumps. REVIEW: re-ran on a fresh build: 0 FAIL on all 5 presets and on a 33 case edge matrix with Simplex/ridged Simplex sources at seed 1337 (each hybrid and float at 0, negative, 1e-30, 1e30, zero and reversed fade range, connected Depth and Fade Min/Max, Gradient controls 1e6 and 1e-6). Found and fixed: Depth >= about 1e38 gave 1990609 NaN/Inf (weightA + weightB overflowed and the reciprocal went NaN) and Depth=1e38 failed AVX512 vs AVX2 parity on 98% of samples; Depth is now clamped to at most 1e30, after which Depth 3.4e38, 1e39 connected, and Height Scale 3.4e38 with Depth 3.4e38 all pass with 0 NaN. Value output is bit identical before and after the fix on a 256^2 raw dump. Height B=White() fails SSE2/SSE41 and grid vs positions parity, but White() alone fails the same way, so that is the test input.
data.seams: None above 0.02 of 4000 in 2D, 3D, 4D with smooth sources for Value, Weight and Composite Height, connected heights, and Depth 0.02. Feature Scale 1 sources: 1 of 4000 at exactly 0.0200 over 0.000977, a slope; the same graph at Feature Scale 10 worst 0.0023. Pebbles in sand: 1026 of 4000 in 2D, all inherited from CellularValue tone in source A, which alone shows 1754 of 4000 with the same worst size. Pebble field height: 2 of 4000 at 0.0247, from the vertical rim of the sqrt dome amplified by 1 / Depth; a parabolic dome gives 0 with worst 0.0028. Depth 0: 3951 of 4000, a hard switch by design, stated in the description. REVIEW: Interlock mask and Veins 0 of 4000 in 2D/3D/4D; Value sources Composite Height at Height Scale 4 Depth 0.02 0 of 4000. Simplex sources at Height Scale 2 Depth 0.05: 5 of 4000 in 3D, worst 0.0818. Simplex(50) alone has worst 0.0064 in 3D and the same graph at Height Scale 0 or with Perlin sources has 0 jumps, so the node magnifies small source steps by up to Height Scale / (2 Depth); now stated in the description.
data.far: Passes the check far coordinate test on every graph above. The node adds no coordinate math, so it inherits source precision.
data.tile: Follows the sources: check seam ratio 0.94 on Mountains from plains, fnlab tile ratio 0.83 on Interlock mask. A Gradient control does not tile, as expected.
data.range: No ScaleOutput or VariableRange: Value and Composite Height are convex combinations, Weight is 2w - 1. Measured Weight -1.000..1.000. Measured hull: Max(A,B) - value and value - Min(A,B) both have minimum -0.000 on Perlin/Simplex and on stock ridged/Simplex sources. Exact ends measured as output minus source: Control at Fade Min minus A and Control at Fade Max minus B both 0.000 for Height Scale 0, 1, 2, 4, -3, Depth 0, and a stock ridged source with range up to 1.87. REVIEW measured on 256^2 raw dumps: end purity exact (max diff 0 at Control = Fade Min for Height Scale 100, 1e5, 1e7; 2.98e-8 at Fade Max); Composite Height with unconnected heights minus Value = 0; Value minus Lerp(A, B, (Weight+1)/2) max 5.96e-8; Depth 0 gives exactly A or B on every sample; hull violation 2.98e-8. Height Scale 0 is NOT a plain linear fade: implied weight is 2f/(1+2f) below the midpoint (0.167, 0.333, 0.444 at f = 0.1, 0.25, 0.4), up to 0.086 off Fade in weight and 0.080 in value on the Mountains sources. Descriptions reworded.
data.bench: ns/sample 2D / 3D / 4D, min of 3 fnlab bench runs, two 4-octave Perlin FBm sources and a Perlin control. HeightBlend reuse: SSE41 22.58 / 41.25 / 81.59, AVX2 9.83 / 20.45 / 37.53, AVX512 7.06 / 12.14 / 30.20. Fade: SSE41 21.46 / 40.23 / 80.76, AVX2 9.40 / 19.78 / 36.54, AVX512 6.04 / 11.76 / 29.27. Re-evaluating graph: SSE41 41.74 / 76.74 / 153.26, AVX2 18.03 / 38.48 / 69.80, AVX512 12.33 / 22.68 / 56.29. Same fractals connected as heights: SSE41 40.78 / 75.53 / 153.04, AVX2 17.83 / 38.45 / 70.58, AVX512 12.03 / 22.39 / 56.79. Min of 2 runs on single Perlin sources with a constant control, AVX2: HeightBlend 2.51 / 4.91 / 9.16, Fade 2.05 / 4.42 / 8.26. AVX2 3D and 4D had outliers up to 1.7x between runs, on Fade as well; the min is reported. REVIEW single runs on the same kind of graph (4-octave Perlin FBm sources, Perlin control): HeightBlend AVX2 10.01-10.12 / 20.33-20.41 / 37.27, SSE41 22.51 / 41.17 / 81.79, AVX512 7.07-7.48 / 12.02-12.69 / 29.60-31.40; Fade AVX2 9.48 / 20.57 / 38.02; re-evaluating graph AVX2 19.09 / 40.21 / 75.43. Matches the report within noise; AVX2 3D/4D outliers of 25-46 ns appeared on Fade and HeightBlend alike. The Depth clamp added no measurable cost.
data.versus_proto: Pebbles in sand against the prototype thumb and relief: same interlock, pebbles stay whole and sand fills the gaps first, where Fade on the same sources fogs over them. The real graph uses one dome radius for all cells, since stock cellular has no per cell radius, so pebbles look more uniform and there are fewer tiny ones than in the prototype. The Composite Height relief has no trench along the blend, because the prototype formula was replaced. REVIEW: rendered the prototype critic pair 3 setup (two FBm, noise control, bright A dark B, Depth 0.1) with the real node beside the prototype: same interlocking regions with the fbm detail fringing the border instead of a fog; the prototype border is more speckled because its fbm has more high-frequency content (lacunarity 2.03, 1.25x gain) and its control saturates more.
data.plan_changes: 1. Control reach is Height Scale + Depth instead of 1, and the height lead saturates at Height Scale, so Fade Min and Fade Max are exactly 100% A and 100% B for any source range. Without the saturation, stock FractalRidged poked through at Fade Max (max difference 2.81 measured); the prototype formula also lets heights bleed through at both ends once Height Scale passes 1 (from its formula, not measured). At Control midpoint with heights in range it is the prototype formula. Height Scale 0 or a very large Depth now gives a plain fade instead of a step. 2. An unconnected Height A or B adds its number to the reused value as a bias, default 0 so reuse is unchanged; otherwise the number box would silently do nothing. 3. Composite Height is Lerp( heights, weight ), not the prototype max( a, b ) - 1 - hs / 2, which by its formula dips 0.5 in the middle of a blend. With unconnected heights it equals Value (measured difference 0.000). 4. Connection test reads the source member base pointer, not the SIMD pointer, to stay clear of pending Gen dispatch changes. 5. gMetadataVectorSize left alone: reservation only.

data.check: Final build. 0 FAIL, 0 WARN on the default node, on Kernel Parabola, and on the 5 presets on seeds 1337, 42, 7, 15 runs. SSE2, SSE41 and AVX512 against AVX2 on seed 1337: 0.0000% of samples off by more than 1e-2, max diff 2.21e-04. Continuity on the default 7.86 / 7.61 / 7.25, presets 4.92 to 7.31. Edge matrix: FAIL on feature set parity where the strain runs away: Steps=16 0.66% of samples, Amplitude=1 Steps=16 3.37%, Lacunarity=4 3.78%. Steps=14: entry parity 2D 3.97e-03. Steps=32: saturates, std 0.00003, non-constant FAIL. Constant by construction and so non-constant FAIL: Amplitude=0, Contrast=0, Contrast=1000. Clean: Steps 1, 10, 12 (2 WARN), Amplitude -0.5 and 0.75, Gain 0, Lacunarity 1 and 1.5, Contrast 0.1 and 0.5, Golden, Periodic 3, Parabola, --scale 4 and 0.25. Amplitude=100 Gain=2 Steps=32 saturates to +1 with no NaN, through the compare after the chain, so it only has the non-constant FAIL. Seed grain over 24 seeds: seeds agree 0.109 on Pairs, 0.103 on Golden, 0.168 on Parabola, under the 0.20 of random directions. Reviewer, on 382a3e3: the author's 15 preset runs and 20 more on seeds 0, -1, 99, 2000000000 and at --scale 4 and 0.25, 0 FAIL, 0 WARN, and the edge list repeats the numbers above. Tangent checked against a central difference Jacobian of the same chain run as DomainWarpShear with the seed rotation replicated, 40000 points: |diff| median 2.0e-03 Pairs noise 2D, 2.7e-03 3D, 2.6e-03 4D, 3.0e-04 Periodic 3 and 2.6e-04 Parabola 3D, so the analytic slopes are right in every dimension and kernel. Odd values: 1500 random graphs per feature set shared with the warp, 0 non finite results. data.versus_proto: Never prototyped, so there is no image to compare. Judged by eye: the strongest of the four. Contour lines, Marble, Wood rings and Engraving all read at once and take one extra node. A graph cannot make any of them today, as no node applies a wave to a source. Chebyshev is the weakest mode, visually near a Sine at lower Order, and is kept for its low cost and hard bounds. REVIEW: the plan names no prototype image and the prototypes have none for this node. Looked and at Marble and Engraving: bands read as described. Aliasing limit reproduced on seed 2024: 18.2 on Perlin 100, 6.8 on Perlin 40. data.plan_changes: 1) PWM is called Pulse, as in the catalogue. 2) Triangle added, it shares its code with Skew. 3) Skew is not the catalogue's Sin( phi + k Sin( phi ) ): that needs 2 Sin and stops at about 26% rising. Here it is a skewed triangle through a smoothstep, with no trig and an exact rising share from Duty. So Duty is the only shape member and there is no Skew member. 4) Pulse compares against a triangle, not a sine, for an exact width with no trig. 5) Edge and Order added, as Pulse and Chebyshev need them. 6) Phase, Steps and Band Guard left out: a Phase is an Add before the node, and the guard costs D source evals. The aliasing rule is in the description instead. 7) Costs replaced by bench numbers.
data.notes: Sources with values far beyond -1..1 work for every mode except Chebyshev, which clamps. Sine is the only mode with trig, and FS::Cos only sees -pi..pi after the wrap. Dune ripples was rendered at --hscale 14. DomainTwist's Spiral bands uses this node and Wood rings uses Stamp.

Author's angular spectrum: 1.41 vs stock 1.41 in 2D, 1.50 vs 1.59 in 3D, 1.78 vs 1.74 in 4D, not rerun because the field did not change. Inside a fractal the higher octaves repeat within the tile, which reads as slightly regular detail in the FBm thumb at Period 8.
data.plan_changes: The catalogue said the Simplex family cannot use this. On the stock lattice it can only be exact in 3D, where the skew is rational. A skew of 1/3 in any dimension makes world ( 3m, 0, .. ) the lattice vector ( 4m, m, .. ), so Simplex takes a separate path with that skew, kernels of r^2 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.47 and its own bounds. Period rounds to the nearest multiple of 3 and scales the noise by what is left, so the tile is always exactly Period * Feature Scale: 3x at Period 1, 1.5x at 2, 0.75x at 4, 1.125x at 8. Review: positions wrap in integers before the skew, centred on 0, replacing the author's tile count pass on the base vertex, so the tile is bit exact and SIMD parity does not depend on distance. Period is an early return to a separate never inlined GenPeriodic and the stock bodies are otherwise untouched. GenPeriodic deliberately has no FS_VECTORCALL because of the LLVM regcall sibcall bug. Period is capped at 1 << 24. One Period for all axes as planned. Fractals cannot pass a period to their source, so there is no octave doubling; a Fractal member would be the fix if repetition inside the tile matters. Costs in the plan replaced with the author's measurements; Simplex 4D is now 6.54 against the row's 6.45.

data.tile: fnlab tile is seamless: seam ratio 1.38 at Feature Scale 40, 1.05 at 64, 0.29 to 1.60 over the battery. It does not keep the look, viewed: plane waves in 4D torus space do not stay stripes in the image, so a tile shows soft blobs with no constant width. This is in the node description. data.versus_proto: Same zoom, gray panels. Labyrinth: node std 0.353, mid gray 19.0%, radial peak 14, centroid 16.7 cycles per panel; prototype 0.349, 19.8%, 13, 16.7. Fingerprint: node 0.352, 19.3%, 21, 20.8; prototype 0.351, 19.5%, 21, 20.8. Same worms and same combed flow with short breaks. The patterns differ cell by cell because kernels hash differently, and the Direction source is stock Perlin. 3D is real SuperSimplex vertices against the prototype's searched BCC and reads the same as a sponge of sheets. Lattice imprint, the critic's folded gradient energy over 12 seeds: Hex foldCV 0.343, maxmin 3.03, Jittered 0.077, 1.59, steered Hex 0.195, 2.03, steered Jittered 0.059, 1.36. The critic had 0.38, 0.09, 0.17 and 0.09 on prototype kernels. Bragg peak not measured. Frequency sweep viewed: clean to about 2.5, straight walled domains at 3 to 5, as the plan and the member help say.
data.plan_changes: 4D Hex falloff radius squared is 0.72, not stock's 0.8, see seams. Jittered does not use the prototype's jitter 1, R 1.5: by that prototype's own seam rule R must not pass 1.5 - jitter / 2. The node uses CellWindow with displacement 0.38 / 0.30 / 0.24 and radius 1.12 / 1.20 / 1.26, which leaves no site outside the window in range and no sample without a kernel, in place of holes that would jump. Direction turns kernels in the XY plane in every dimension, and in 3D and 4D Spread is a blend toward +X then renormalised; the prototype's 3D had a base vector and an elevation, this node has only the angle in the plan. Kernel sine and cosine are a local cheap turn form, accurate to about 1e-3, in place of PolyMath::SinCos, a third faster and the only part of the K4 kernel swapped. All kernel fields come from one MixHash split into bit fields: 16 / 16 in 2D, 11 / 11 / 10 in 3D, 8 / 8 / 8 / 8 in 4D. Triangle and Pulse are multiplied by the softened phasor's length, the prototype's were not and would jump at each singularity. Pulse duty is fixed at 0.5 with an edge width of 0.2, the member list has no Duty. Amplitude gain is fixed at the prototype's 1.4. Arms costs one complex multiply per extra arm, not two: Arms 3 adds 0.18 ns. No Coherent mode. Setter clamps: Spread and Phase Jitter 0..1, Epsilon at least 0.001, Arms 1..8, Frequency at Gen time +-1000. The enum shows Sin Phase and Cos Phase with spaces, as stock names do; the DSL ignores spaces.

Bevel 0 above .02 on 8 of 11; 3 at Grid Jitter 1 have 50 to 812 ppm, worst .027, and that is ordinary slope on thin plates: at pair spacing 2e-5 cells the worst falls to .004 with 0 above .02. Margin and Bevel are continuous by construction now: a window column's walls and plates are capped by the room left before it leaves the window, which is 0 at the line. Written into the description. Review: fnlab tile gives the same .0005 vs .0008, ratio .62. On floats the mean mirror diff is 1.5e-06 about columns and 1.3e-06 about rows of a std of .878, so it is an exact mirror as the description says.

data.versus_proto: Author: real beside the prototype, plus real vol beside the prototype. Same mechanism and same look: rigid polygons with wedge gaps, tilted slabs, texture that turns with each plate, plates of plates. What differs: 1) The real reliefs show about twice the plates per frame, which is my Feature Scale choice, not the node. 2) Plate sizes vary a little less, since K3's jitter is a fixed radius (.35 at Grid Jitter .8) where the proto used a box of .4 per axis. 3) Margin is not doubled and clipped, so it is a roof over each plate and not a plateau; the proto's clamp hid the ratio spikes next to thin plates, and those stay visible as dark creases. 4) TiltedHeight reaches near Output Max; the proto's plates stopped at about .6. 5) Lookup samples with the plate's site as origin and a seed per plate, and does get z; the proto used fixed offsets and no z in Extruded. 6) Nested Lookup looks like the proto discovery and is still rather noisy, so it is not a preset. 7) Full at Gap .35 reads as crisp separate polyhedra, close to the proto's vol; the proto's chunks are smaller and more scattered at its own settings. 8) Drift uses a box inside the Drift circle, Rotation is a rational turn, 0.93 radians at 1, both invisible at normal values. Review, at the proto's plate density, Feature Scale 80, real beside r_tilt, r_bevel, thumb_lookup, v1: same mechanism and same look, rigid polygons with wedge gaps and tilted slabs. Real plates vary less in size, as the author says, and real Bevel relief reads more in rows. That is not a stronger lattice than the proto: in one numpy Bevel model the node's ring of .35 gives a lattice peak of 277 times the ring median and the proto's box of .4 gives 465. Top down at .8 and 1 no lattice shows. Real vol at Gap .35 is more packed than v1. My real Lookup frame used a larger source than the proto's thumb, so its look is not a fair comparison.
data.plan_changes: Author: 1) The plan's window audit was not enough. 'Clamp Drift to .3, 3x3 is sound to there' was wrong as a seam claim: real jumps exist at defaults (66 ppm, worst .052) and get large at Grid Jitter 1 or Rotation .8, and fnlab seams misses them. Replaced by a fade: walls and plates are capped by the room their site has before it leaves the window, over the last eighth of a cell, so Margin and Bevel are C0 at any setting. Cost about .8 ns. The clamp stays because past it more plates get cut. Against the first build, the fade and the rule in point 2 together change .010% of Margin samples and .039% of Bevel samples by more than .05 at the defaults, and 1.1% to 1.3% at Grid Jitter 1. Cut plates show as straight edges at n + .375 at extreme settings only: at Drift .3 Rotation 1 Gap .1 Grid Jitter 1 the edge rate there is 1018 ppm with Priority Random against about 370 on other lines, and no excess at the defaults. 2) 9 x 8 dots became walls only between sites in touching cells, 20 pairs in 2D and 158 in 3D, each used in both directions. Against all pairs in the window it changes .03% of samples at the defaults and 1% at Grid Jitter 1; the contact sheet at Grid Jitter 1 shows no visible difference, and it took Full from 91.9 to 68.2 ns. 3) Exact division instead of FS::Reciprocal, for AVX512 parity, see check. 4) 4D is the Extruded form, plates in x and y, and the description says so, per D4. 5) TiltedHeight native range is -1 to Min( .4 + |Tilt|, 1 ), and Gap Value is in that native space. The file names in the plan are as written. Added the far lane rule and a line in the Lookup text. Touching-cell walls checked against a 7x7 model: off by more than .05 on .0083% of samples at the defaults and 1.33% at Grid Jitter 1, worst .39, against .0267% with all pairs in 3x3.

data.review: Reviewer rebuilt fb65340 from source with a forced recompile, read the full diff (4 files, registration at the bottom of FastSIMD_Build.inl, no test node, no trailers, control flow per lane by mask and Select, every member read in Gen, metadata defaults and enum orders match the plan table, hash fields disjoint), re-ran check, seams, straddle, far, tile, range and bench, wrote a NaN battery and a separate numpy model of the maths, and committed 212b0bc. The measurements reproduced. Fixes: 1) NaN at degenerate input and a zero division past 2^24 cells, by sending those lanes to the origin. 2) The Lookup text now says gradient noise reads 0 at a plate's origin: Lookup of Perlin keeps 68% of its std at twice the plate's Feature Scale, 36% at 4x, 9% at 16x; the proto has the same property. 3) The lost plan edits, see plan_changes. Disagreements: 'no NaN' only held for the trees tried; the plan edit the author reports was not in the file. Left as they are, maintainer's call: default Grid Jitter .8 per the plan. Bevel lattice peak over 6 seeds is 599 axis and 160 diagonal, at Grid Jitter 1 it is 22 and 8, stock CellularDistance 108 and 149, but at 1 the touching-cell walls are off on 1.3% of samples. MSVC not built. Tilt near 1e38 can overflow to NaN inside the clamp, which x86's Min removes; ARM and WASM were not run. 2 images read.

data.tile: Fails as a tile, as the plan said, and the description says so. GenTileable2D wraps with no seam: 'tile: seam diff 0.0234 vs interior diff 0.0502 (ratio 0.47, ~1 = seamless)', check's tileable ok at ratio 0.49. The image is a warped slice through the rhombohedra with lens shapes and no rhombs (viewed). Rows v and -v are equal on 100.0% of pixels, so it mirrors top to bottom, since dropping w leaves z = R cos v. Columns are not mirrored, 4.9% equal. An aperiodic tiling has no periodic form, so no 4D form would give rhombs that repeat.
data.versus_proto: Viewed before the final cosmetic rebuild; pixel compares show the presets did not change. Same character in the plain floor, thick and thin rhombs, stars and decagons, no long lines, and in the 3D rhombohedra with crisp faces. Differences. The tiling for a seed is not the prototype's, since the gamma hash differs and 3D also takes Rotation. Bevel uses the critic's type coded heights, scaled so the highest stone reaches 1 where the prototype stopped at about 0.65. Grout margin is width / 4 instead of a fixed 0.01, the same at the default. EdgeDistance divides by the real half thickness instead of a cap of 0.45, so it has no flat top. The prototype's Lookup is its own FBm times 1.6 clamped; the node takes any source, and the terraces preset uses plain FBm with Grout Width 0, which is lower and has no cracks. In relief the real stones at Feature Scale 64 look smaller than the prototype's window. fnlab sheet stats: real axis 20.71, isoCV 0.72, beta 3.77 at Feature Scale 40, prototype axis 13.89, isoCV 0.92, beta 4.19 at its own window, so the tile size differs and these are not a like for like measure. Weak view: EdgeDistance in gray is soft, relief is where it reads.
data.plan_changes: 1. Far coordinates: the plan assumed float32 limits with margin selection hiding them. The port does not take ceil of a float t. It writes each tile relative to its crossing, which cancels the large terms and leaves only ceil( t ) - t, and gets that in wrapping 32 bit fixed point, so defects are 0 up to 3e4 tile edges and .1% at 1e6. No per pair inverse tables or V0 sums are needed. 2. Tables are built at compile time with constexpr, no load time float maths and the same on every platform, and do not depend on Rotation, which rotates the sample. MSVC compiled them with no step limit error; that is the only MSVC check. 3. Rotation also applies in 3D, around Z. 4. Bevel is the critic's type coded out=11 scaled to reach 1, not out=6. 5. EdgeDistance is normalised by the real half thickness per family, not a cap. 6. Gamma comes from GetValueCoord, zero sum in 2D only as the prototype does. 7. 4D is the 3D form with w ignored, written as a GenT overload. 8. Tried and dropped: sharing line products across combinations, 2% at Five and nothing at Seven.
