data.tile: No fifth axis for First Hit, so 4D is not a real form and the description now says so in those words: First Hit marches along the torus normal, Shadow and AO turn the point along the circles. Both are periodic. Reviewer, fnlab tile at size 1024: ratio Overhang mesas 0.81, Broken cliffs 0.97, Craggy highlands 0.82, Baked shadows 0.71, Cavity map 0.87. Wrap pair percentile against interior over every row and column: 30 and 12, 71 and 44, 70 and 2, 6 and 9, 0 and 0. Low means the wrap is smoother than the interior, which comes from the rows nearest the lattice plane w = 0 of the 4D source, not from a seam. Shadow on small tiles of 64 and 128 px reads ratio up to 7.65 by the one row test, but over 6 seeds its wrap percentile runs 0 to 98 with no bias, so no seam. Limits as the author states: a ray changes the circle radius by up to 0.35 x Length each way, so features along the ray scale against 2D, Shadow and AO rays stop at a quarter of the tile, and 3D First Hit needs a 4D source: a source with no real 4D form ignores the ray.
data.range: VariableRange. First Hit and Shadow are exact by construction, ScaleOutput( value, -1, 1 ), measured -1.000..1.000 on every First Hit preset and default Shadow. AO is 1 - 2 x mean sine of the horizon, analytic -1..1, measured -0.667..1.000 at defaults over 1024 world units, -0.973 at Rise 0.5: a measured constant would be wrong as Rise moves it. Defaults at 1024 world units: First Hit mean 0.081 std 0.443, 44% below 0; Shadow 23% of area shadowed at Rise 2.
data.bench: Reviewer rerun at 22a836c, one round each, ns/sample 2D / 3D / 4D. Source Perlin(Feature Scale=64) alone: SSE41 2.08 / 4.06 / 8.60, AVX2 1.47 / 2.09 / 4.09 (2D is the first bench of the run and reads high, author's 0.93 fits the rest), AVX512 0.61 / 1.25 / 3.07. First Hit Steps 8 (default): SSE41 47.04 / 87.93 / 90.90, AVX2 22.11 / 38.43 / 39.28, AVX512 13.24 / 30.87 / 34.75. It evaluates Steps + 1 times one dimension up. Steps 16: SSE41 85.87 / 160.70 / 165.97, AVX2 41.66 / 72.39 / 99.81, AVX512 27.66 / 68.42 / 59.03. Shadow Steps 8: SSE41 21.49 / 37.25 / 95.63, AVX2 9.28 / 19.14 / 42.54, AVX512 6.33 / 11.24 / 33.33. AO Steps 8, 33 evaluations: SSE41 79.66 / 140.55 / 356.47, AVX2 34.62 / 70.80 / 158.45, AVX512 24.18 / 42.02 / 144.27. Presets: Overhang mesas SSE41 87.15 / 165.40 / 169.78, AVX2 42.86 / 74.47 / 75.57, AVX512 25.62 / 62.88 / 68.49. Broken cliffs SSE41 264.38 / 493.15 / 499.42, AVX2 129.35 / 224.71 / 296.05, AVX512 80.84 / 182.85 / 172.14. Craggy highlands SSE41 258.02 / 480.31 / 485.02, AVX2 122.71 / 276.21 / 229.12, AVX512 73.38 / 172.76 / 175.50. The First Hit rewrite costs no more than before: author's AVX2 Steps 8 was 21.05 / 37.89 / 41.58. Shadow and AO unchanged within noise. AVX2 3D and 4D rounds spike up to 40%.
data.versus_proto: Reviewer, properly framed, with member values worked out from the prototype's: First Hit against dyn_lens 15 at N 16, bias 1, 2 features of ray, both 8 features wide. The surfaces have the same character, rolling hills cut by cliffs. The prototype takes a hard crossing and leaves jagged fins at walls, the real one has continuous walls. Shadow against smp_lens 3 at Length 87, Rise 0.48, Steps 8, Direction 0.7: same dark regions trailing the same way with soft edges at Softness 0.1, larger area in the real one, cause not isolated, most likely source height. AO against smp_lens 4: same web of bright crests and dark hollows, 4 directions against 6. Disagreement with the author's first check: step banding was visible. With the same parameters as the prototype, the author's First Hit showed contour rings on hillsides in relief that the prototype does not have, and on a linear density its height slope ran 0.515 to 1.396 of ideal, worst at Bias 0.5 Steps 16, default Softness. Now 1.000 at Steps 4 to 64 and Softness 0.02 and 0.05, no rings at 4, 8, 16, 32 steps. It also converges faster at the same cost: rms against 64 steps at Length 128 on one octave 0.148, 0.043, 0.011, 0.002 at 4, 8, 16, 32 steps, was 0.198, 0.114, 0.070, 0.034; on 4 octaves 0.261, 0.164, 0.070, 0.023, was 0.289, 0.198, 0.104, 0.043. Relief is the honest view: Overhang mesas, Broken cliffs and Craggy highlands read as flat capped mesas with sheer walls. At 4 steps silhouettes differ, 8 is close to 32 with small differences, 16 and 32 match by eye.
data.plan_changes: 1. Direction is one float angle in radians, was a per dimension vector: a vector cannot be followed on the tile circles, and 0 in all axes means no direction. 2. Length default 200, was 20: on the default Perlin Length 20 reads like the source itself, First Hit needs about 2 features of ray. Steps stays 8, which looks right at default. 3. Members Bias 0.5, Rise 2 and Softness 0.05 added. Bias is what makes every ray end in solid; the catalogue had it and the plan row dropped it. Rise is how far a light ray climbs over Length, so at Rise 2 no bump in -1..1 is cut off. Softness keeps walls continuous. 4. VariableRange added, every output is a normalised mask or height. 5. Shadow and AO step quadratically: against 64 steps, 8 err by 0.31 rms against 0.62 for even spacing and 0.425 for power 1.5 on a 2 octave Shadow. 6. Catalogue modes Mean and Transmittance and its StepGrowth, Start, Threshold and Density not built, the plan row did not ask for them. Volumetric Transmittance on a 3D node is therefore not covered: 3D Shadow and AO work on XZ slices with Y up, matching SurfaceProbe Hillshade. gMetadataVectorSize left alone. Reviewer: First Hit stops rays by the running peak of density, integrated evenly over -Softness to Softness, in place of per sample opacity. Shadow and AO cap the gain on the closest steps at 256, which changes nothing up to Steps 16. The plan's cost and first check rows updated.

data.name: SimplexFacet
data.check: Reviewer rerun after the fixes. fnlab check on the default at Feature Scale 40: 'check passed: 0 FAIL, 0 WARN'. Parity: SSE2 and SSE41 vs AVX2 max diff 9.54e-07 2D, 8.34e-07 3D, 5.96e-07 4D, AVX512 0, all '0.0000%' off by more than 1e-2. Entry parity 2.38e-07. Continuity ratios 7.90 / 7.85 / 7.90. JitteredGrid with Warp Amplitude 0: also 0 FAIL, 0 WARN, parity at most 4.77e-07, continuity 7.98 / 7.98 / 7.91. 54 setups. The author's script wrote Source=White, which fnlab reads as the number 0, so no node was connected. It now says White(). 52 'check passed'. The other 2 are JitteredGrid with White() as Source, 4 FAIL lines in all: 'FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 4.39e-02 3D 8.43e-01 4D 7.15e-07, samples off by >1e-2: 32.2042%', SSE41 33.4412%, and with warp 33.4880% and 34.9101%. White hashes the bits of the float position, and a vertex differs by a float step between feature sets. Not fixed: stock CellularLookup with White() as Lookup fails the same way, 92.59% AVX512 vs AVX2, and stock DomainWarpSimplex with White() as Source, 87.57%. Perlin, Checkerboard and CellularValue as Source pass parity. 56 WARN: 54 continuity ratios near 1 on exactly the 18 setups that jump by design, 2 'seed sensitivity' on Tent with no warp on the Simplex lattice and on JitteredGrid at Grid Jitter 0. 26 more setups, the 5 presets, seeds 7, 42, 99, negative and huge Warp Amplitude and Warp Frequency, Grid Jitter -3 and 5, Slope 0, -3 and 1000, Face Offset -1 and 7, Feature Scale -40, Output Min above Max: 26 'check passed', 0 FAIL; 21 continuity WARN on the outputs that jump, 2 range WARN, one on the FBm preset (stock FBm of Simplex reads -1.578..1.700) and one where Output Min and Max were set to 3 and -2. 2160 runs over every float and hybrid member at 0, negative and up to +-3e38, all Outputs, both Lattices, 2D 3D 4D: non finite output only at Feature Scale 1e-38 in Lerp and Tent on the simplex lattice, and Feature Scale 0 is NaN too. Stock Simplex, Perlin, SuperSimplex and CellularDistance give NaN at the same values, so it is left as the shared mixin's limit. Parity at far coordinates to 1e20: no row off above 0.2% for any Output but Tilted. Tilted splits from 1e6 features, 2D no, 3D JitteredGrid SSE2 42% and SSE41 38% vs AVX2, since a float step there is 1/16 of a feature and the plane reads it directly. It is near the limit the description states and shows no seam. MSVC 19.51 builds with no error and no warning in these files, 16 minutes with 4 jobs, from 584496e. fnlab check on the default: 0 FAIL, 0 WARN. 180 rows against clang-cl over 4 feature sets, 0 gross, off by more than 1e-2 on at most 0.013% of samples, all on outputs that jump, where rounding picks the other facet at an edge. Not done: no Linux or ARM build.
data.bench: fnlab bench, ns/sample, 2D / 3D / 4D, Feature Scale 40, rerun after the fixes. Default with warp: SSE41 3.70 / 5.53 / 7.77, AVX2 1.87 / 2.67 / 3.76, AVX512 1.21 / 1.76 / 2.91. Bare (Warp Amplitude 0): SSE41 1.92 / 3.09 / 3.86, AVX2 0.99 / 1.49 / 2.04, AVX512 0.65 / 0.95 / 1.57. JitteredGrid bare: SSE41 14.30 / 73.03, AVX2 6.79 / 34.65, AVX512 4.96 / 25.52, its 4D is the simplex lattice. JitteredGrid with warp AVX2 7.58 / 35.33. Same run: Perlin SSE41 2.11 / 4.10 / 8.74, AVX2 0.93 / 2.13 / 4.12, AVX512 0.62 / 1.25 / 3.44. Simplex AVX2 1.19 / 2.09 / 3.17. CellularDistance AVX2 3.89 / 12.36 / 41.47. So on AVX2 bare is 1.1x / 0.70x / 0.50x Perlin, default 2.0x / 1.3x / 0.91x, JitteredGrid 7.3x / 16x Perlin and 1.7x / 2.8x CellularDistance. Outputs bare AVX2: Tent 0.79 / 1.34 / 1.89, Flat 0.95 / 1.66 / 2.24, Tilted 1.49 / 2.19 / 3.44, Face Offset 0.3 1.09 / 1.62 / 2.17. JitteredGrid: Tent 6.59 / 34.79, Flat 6.58 / 45.09, Tilted 8.25 / 49.04; the 45.09 is noise, the run before read 33.90. Source as 4 octave Perlin FBm (4.10 / 8.73 / 16.35 alone): Simplex lattice 13.23 / 36.13 / 98.24, a single run read 13.30 / 36.22 / 85.52, JitteredGrid 20.24 / 83.08, one evaluation per vertex. The author's report matches within noise except these fixes: the unfixed commit in the same run read default AVX2 1.81 / 2.65 / 3.63, so the warp path costs about 3% more and the bare path nothing. MSVC 19.51, one fnlab bench run: default SSE41 5.70 / 10.25 / 15.05, AVX2 3.18 / 5.41 / 7.44, AVX512 5.11 / 6.91 / 10.13; bare AVX2 2.11 / 3.67 / 4.35; JitteredGrid bare AVX2 8.99 / 53.22, AVX512 22.19 / 101.41; Perlin AVX2 0.95 / 2.00 / 4.11. So MSVC is 1.3x to 2.5x clang-cl on this node, while Perlin matches, and its AVX512 is slower than its AVX2, 2.5x on the 2D grid.
data.seams: fnlab seams on the default: 'after bisection worst 0.0001 over 0.000977, jumps above 0.02: 0 of 4000' in 2D, 3D and 4D, 'SEAMS: none found'. JitteredGrid with Warp Amplitude 0: worst 0.0003 / 0.0001 / 0.0001, 0 of 4000, 'SEAMS: none found'. Over the 54 setups 36 report none, and 18 jump by design, exactly Flat, Tilted and Face Offset. White as a real node, 7 setups on both lattices on all 4 feature sets: on 7f10785 all 28 jumped, for example the bare Simplex lattice on AVX2 at 'jumps above 0.02: 4000 of 4000'; now all 28 report none on clang-cl and on MSVC. About 2e7 sample pairs: a facet centre that read two White values 37133 times now does so 2 times, not traced, the test takes equal Flat values to mean the same facet so a chance equal value counts. Tiny Grid Jitter, 1e-7 to 0.01, all feature sets: none on clang-cl. MSVC AVX512 jumped up to 123 of 4000 between 1e-7 and 1e-5, none on 6 seeds from 2e-5 up to 0.99, so the setter snaps below 1e-4 to 0, which also reads none. That last commit was not rebuilt on MSVC. In the 26 reviewer setups Warp Amplitude 50 with Warp Frequency 3 reports jumps of 0.025 to 0.035. It is a steep slope, not a jump: steep_vs_jump.py halves the step and the change halves with it down to float resolution.
data.range: Native ranges by construction, no fitted constant except the grid reach below. ScaleOutput( v, -1, 1 ) on Lerp, Flat, Tent. Measured over 1M samples per dimension on 2 seeds. Lerp Simplex with warp 2D -0.9973..0.9962, 3D -0.9907..0.9837, 4D -0.9662..0.9736, std 0.408 / 0.365 / 0.333. Lerp JitteredGrid 2D -0.9966..0.9949. Tent -1.0001..0.9994 at worst, mean -0.333 / -0.50 / -0.60. Flat -1.0000..1.0000, std 0.577. Tilted is ScaleOutput( v, -b, b ) with b = 0.5 + |Slope| R, where R is the exact vertex to centre distance on the Simplex lattice (0.4714, 0.5590, 0.6325), and on JitteredGrid a fit to measured peaks (0.745 + 0.5 J in 2D, 0.935 + 0.35 J in 3D), with a clamp to +-b for rarer facets. The fit was measured with the half range Y jitter, the reviewer measured it again after the fix: at Slope 1e4 at most 3 of 3M samples reach the clamp at any Grid Jitter, so it stays. Tilted measured: Simplex 2D -0.9672..0.9714, JitteredGrid 2D -0.9229..0.9280, 3D -0.8810..0.8810. Std 0.343 Simplex, 0.230 JitteredGrid in 2D, so JitteredGrid Tilted is lower in contrast. A connected Source passes its own range through in Lerp and Flat. Output Min/Max through VariableRange.
data.far: fnlab check far coordinates: ok on the default, 'std 0.447 vs near 0.351'. Mean |step| / step for a step of 0.02 features or 4 float steps there, whichever is larger. Simplex lattice with warp 2D: 1.13 near, 1.22 at 1e3, 1.17 at 1e4, 1.24 at 1e5, 1.05 at 1e6, 0.60 at 3e6, 0.19 at 1e7. JitteredGrid bare 2D: 0.89, 0.96, 0.86, 0.92, 0.82, 0.43, 0.12. 3D reads the same way. So facets hold to about 1e6 features, degrade by 3e6 where the float step is a quarter of a feature, and are gone by 1e7. This is the float32 position limit, there is no separate failure before it, and the description says past about 1e6. Output is finite to 1e20 in the setups tested. Int conversion agrees across feature sets to 1e20 except Tilted, see check.
data.tile: Works without a seam, with limits in the description. fnlab tile on the default: 'seam diff 0.0186 vs interior diff 0.0174 (ratio 1.07, ~1 = seamless)', range -0.648..0.869, check's tileable ok at ratio 0.91 by its own measure, std 0.239. Viewed by the reviewer: no seam in the 2 x 2 repeat, but the torus bends through the 4D mesh, so facets are soft and creases curved, some axis aligned bands show, and contrast is lower than the 2D form. JitteredGrid has no 4D form, so its tile with warp is the same image as the default, and the jittered mesh never appears. With Warp Amplitude 0 the ratio is 1.02.
data.versus_proto: Reviewer view after the fixes. The node against both prototypes, all viewed. Same character in all views: flat facets and straight creases, polygons of varied size with the warp, triangles of varied size on the grid, cut crystal planes in the bare 3D volume. At Feature Scale 64 the real thumbs sit at about the prototype's scale and read the same. The Feature Scale 40 thumbs are busier only because more features fit. Numeric match: folded area of the warp at amplitude 0.6, frequency 1.3 on the real node, 2D, is 23.89%, against the prototype's 23.92%. The commit under review did not match, since its warp X was half range with a constant offset, and read 2.21% against the 6.55% it now reads at product 0.5. Differences that remain. The hash is the node's, so a seed does not give the prototype's field and the volume has different cave shapes. Warp is turned 30 degrees in 3D and 4D too, the prototype did so in 2D only. Tilted is normalised where the prototype overshot to -1.28..1.43. Face Offset blends instead of adding. fnlab sheet stats at the default after the fixes: std 0.403, axis 17.68, isoCV 0.77, beta 4.96. Default over seeds 1, 2, 3, 7, 42, 1337: axis 49.76, 28.81, 30.09, 27.93, 35.87, 17.68. Grid over the same seeds: axis 23.47, 18.52, 12.42, 26.00, 15.63, 57.25, beta 4.99 to 5.04; prototype axis 45.51, 33.91, 44.13, 47.67, 16.91, 16.42, beta 5.00 to 5.08. The axis metric swings by seed in both. Critic's call holds: the warp at Feature Scale 40 reads as crumpled paper, bare 3D is the best volume, and the grid is the best 2D low poly.
data.plan_changes: 1. Face Offset is a blend towards a per facet random level, clamped to 0..1, not an addition: the prototype's form leaves the range. Same look at small values, and 1 means Flat. 2. Source: the plan said D+1 vertices. That is Lerp only. Flat and Tilted sample it once at the facet centre, which gives a low poly map for one evaluation, and Tent ignores it. A plain number is ignored and vertices take random values, stated in the help. 3. The facet value comes from a hash of the sum of all the facet's vertex hashes, not a kind code added to the base hash, which is what the plan warned about. Measured correlation across an edge is within +-0.005. It is the same code for both lattices. 4. Point location keeps max( min( weight ) ) from the prototype but on unnormalised weights, since only the facet holding the sample has them all positive. One division per sample instead of 8 or 48, and the prototype's port note of a Reciprocal per triangle is dropped. 3D cross products are shared per hexahedron, 41.7 to 34.7 ns on AVX2. 5. Quad split decisions read only the jitter offsets, and vertex positions for Source are summed as integers and converted once. The first form summed floats, and /fp:fast reassociated them so vertices disagreed in the last bits. A real White() node now shows no seam on any feature set. 6. Warp lattice turned 30 degrees around Z in every dimension, the prototype did 2D only. 7. Grid Jitter clamped to 0.99, the prototype went to 1, and 3D uses at most 0.33 as the prototype did. 8. Tilted normalised by 0.5 + |Slope| R, with a clamp on JitteredGrid's rarer facets. 9. Folding text: measured on the fixed node, 2D 0% at the default, 0.04% at product 0.325, 6.56% at 0.5, 23.89% at .6 x 1.3, 32.33% at 1. 3D and 4D fold a little earlier, 0.01% and 0.03% at the default, 10.35% and 15.14% at 0.5, 39.61% and 44.15% at 1. The help gives the 2D numbers and the 3D ones. 10. Reviewer: 11. Warp Frequency is clamped to +-1e9, Slope to +-1e30 and Warp Amplitude per lane to +-1e30, so a huge value can not overflow to NaN. 12. Grid Jitter below 1e-4 snaps to 0. 13. 2D grid jitter uses 15 bits per axis. 14.

data.notes: Status after review: the default and every realistic setup pass all gates on the commit above, three real defects were found and fixed, not merged. Fixed. 1. HashPrimes always clears bit 31, its result is a 31 bit hash. The warp read a field starting at bit 31, so warp X lay in 0..amplitude with mean amplitude / 2 while the other axes were +-amplitude, on every dimension. Measured on the unfixed DLL with a Gradient as Source: 2D X 0.0005..0.4984 mean 0.25, Y -0.4969..0.4983 mean 0. Now X -0.4979..0.4979 mean 0. 2. The same bit: 2D grid Y jitter read bits 16 to 31, so corners stayed in the low half of their cell in Y while X used the whole cell. Facet centres read frac mean 0.5002 in X and 0.6424 in Y. Now 0.4999 and 0.4997. 3D jitter never reached bit 31. Neither shows in fnlab check, seams or a correlation test. 3. Vertex positions for Source were not bit exact: /fp:fast reassociates float sums, the build uses it on clang-cl and MSVC. White as a real node jumped at every facet edge. Now summed as integers. A smooth Source was never affected visibly. 4. NaN at Warp Frequency 1e38, Warp Amplitude 3e38 and Slope 3e38, now clamped. 5. MSVC AVX512 seams at Grid Jitter 1e-7 to 1e-5, now snapped to 0. 6. Help text: the Output help now says Tent ignores the seed with a fixed mesh, and the Warp Amplitude help says a connected node bends facets and gives 3D folding. Disagreement with the author. 'White as a Source proves it' was not a test: Source=White parses as the number 0 in fnlab, so those setups ran with no Source, and the claim was false when tested. 'Stated in the Output help' for Tent and the seed was not in the file. The folding numbers in the help described a model that the committed node did not match, 2.21% and 22.05% where it said 6.5% and 32%; they are right now. The bench and range numbers checked out within noise. Open. Gate 1 fails on one corner: JitteredGrid with White() as Source fails SSE parity, as stock CellularLookup and DomainWarpSimplex do with White(). Tilted parity splits past 1e6 features. Remaining limits. JitteredGrid has no 4D form and uses the simplex lattice there, stated in the description. GenTileable2D has no seam but bends facets, stated. JitteredGrid in 3D is 16x Perlin and the prototyper and critic both said it looks no better than the bare simplex lattice in 3D; it is kept because the plan merges it. The bare Simplex lattice in 2D is a regular 60 degree quilt, which is why warp is the default. JitteredGrid's Tilted reach is a fit to measured peaks, not a proof. Feature Scale 0 gives NaN as every stock node does. MSVC runs this node at 1.3x to 2.5x clang-cl, and slower on AVX512 than AVX2. MSVC was built from 584496e, the last commit changes only the Grid Jitter setter. No Linux or ARM build. fnlab's DSL reads a bare node name on a hybrid as the number 0, use White(). The build uses /fp:fast, so a float sum is not bit reproducible between code paths.

data.name: SpanningMaze
data.check: Reviewer rerun on a84dd31 (rebuilt DLL): SpanningMaze(Feature Scale=40) 'check passed: 0 FAIL, 0 WARN', parity SSE2/SSE41 vs AVX2 max diff 1.01e-06, AVX512 2.38e-07, 0.0000% off by more than 1e-2. gates.sh battery rerun, 41 runs (the author's run): the only FAIL is 'FAIL non-constant: std 0.00000' at Gain=0, same WARN kinds as before (tileable ratio on flat rows, continuity and seed sensitivity at Feature Scale 1000 and 1e5, FBm range, Gain 1000 step). Reviewer battery of 23 setups the author did not show: seeds 12345 and INT_MIN, Feature Scale 0, -40, 1e9, Gain 1e30, 1e-30, -1e39, -0.5 with Levels 12, Levels 0, 100, -5, Output Min=Max=0, Output Min/Max +-1e30, Seed Offset INT_MAX, Cap False with each Output and a negative Gain at seeds 3, 4, 11, the presets at seeds 99, 5, 77, Levels 3 at --scale 0.37. 0 NaN/Inf in every run. Only non-trivial findings: Feature Scale=0 is finite but ISA dependent (parity FAIL 67%, Perlin at Feature Scale=0 is all NaN, so not node specific), and Output Min/Max=+-1e30 fails parity on the check's absolute 1e-2 threshold at 1e30 magnitudes. Acceptance reruns on the fixed DLL: proof.py GRAPH PASS and CAP EQUIVALENCE PASS (33 region and seed combinations, 0 cycles, every block cells - 1 edges and one piece); connect.py 0 enclosed pieces unwarped in 2D and 3D, block aligned windows one piece, presets 0 enclosed with 0 to 4 specks. Reviewer's own review.py reads the edges from the Signed output at face middles (asserted exactly +-1) instead of CorridorDistance: 0 cycles in 8 setups including origin (1048576, -2097152) in 2D, (65536, -65536, 131072) in 3D, Levels 12, Cap False, 4D; raster flood fill on unaligned windows 0 enclosed; open share per axis 0.50 / 0.33 / 0.25.
data.bench: fnlab bench, ns/sample, 2D / 3D / 4D, Feature Scale 40, reviewer run on a84dd31. Default: SSE41 3.16 / 6.13 / 8.96, AVX2 1.95 / 3.17 / 4.67, AVX512 1.17 / 2.46 / 3.46. Perlin in the same run: SSE41 2.12 / 4.14 / 8.78, AVX2 0.93 / 2.19 / 4.20, AVX512 0.62 / 1.27 / 3.52. CellularDistance AVX2 3.90 / 12.41 / 41.57. So 2.1x / 1.4x / 1.1x Perlin on AVX2. CorridorDistance AVX2 1.86 / 3.11 / 4.55, WallDistance 1.93 / 3.18 / 4.67, Levels 1 1.99 / 3.23 / 4.74, Levels 12 1.99 / 3.23 / 4.82. Cap Distances False, the 3^D window: SSE41 26.22 / 149.85 / 717.98, AVX2 12.83 / 74.64 / 354.47, AVX512 8.87 / 52.22 / 253.58. Presets AVX2: Warped labyrinth 4.11 / 6.58 / 11.87, Walled maze 4.19 / 6.89 / 11.55, Cave block 3.13 / 4.95 / 8.10. The author's numbers on 11fcfde match within noise; the hash key fix adds one int multiply per edge test and is not measurable. The plan estimated 5.4-9.9 / 40-60 / 250.
data.seams: fnlab seams on the default: 0 jumps above 0.02 of 4000 in each of 2D, 3D, 4D, worst 0.0001 over 0.000977 after bisection. 40 of the first 41 battery runs report 'SEAMS: none found'. Gain=1000 reports 'jumps above 0.02: 3716 of 4000' in 2D, 3420 in 3D, 3154 in 4D, and Gain=1e39 also reports jumps: at those gains the output is a step at the maze outline, by the user's choice. Gain=16 is clean. Reviewer rerun on a84dd31: default 0 jumps of 4000 in 2D, 3D, 4D, worst 0.0001 over 0.000977; the battery's only seams exits are Gain 1000 and 1e39 (a step by choice) and Output Min/Max +-1e30 (magnitude).
data.range: Native range is [-1,1] by construction, ScaleOutput( v, -1, 1 ) with no fitted constant. Measured -1.0000 to 1.0000 on all 3 outputs, with and without the cap, over up to 2M samples per dimension and 2 seeds. Corridor centre lines are exactly +1 and closed walls exactly -1 at Gain 2. Below Gain 2 the Signed output does not fill the range (Gain 1 is [-0.5, 0.5]). Signed mean 0.000 / -0.410 / -0.622 and share above 0 is 50% / 22% / 9% in 2D / 3D / 4D, since corridors are lines and walls are faces.
data.far: fnlab check far coordinates ok on every battery run with a normal Feature Scale. Edge graph read back at offsets 65536, 1048576 and 4194304 at Feature Scale 1 in 2D, 3D, 4D: 18 of 18 with 0 cycles. Output is finite and in range up to 1e30 on all outputs. Positions quantise as float does: 200000 samples over 64 cells give 3241 distinct values at 1e5, 57 at 1e6, 5 at 3e6, 1 at 1e7. No node specific far limit found so none is in the description; Perlin was not run at these offsets here, TubeNoise's notes saw it collapse near 1e6.
data.tile: Fails as a maze, passes as a wrap, and the description says so. GenTileable2D wraps with no seam: at Feature Scale 11 the wrap step has mean 0.17111 and max 0.3609, the steps beside it have means 0.17043, 0.16038, 0.09706, 0.15921 and max 0.3609 to 0.3628. But the torus is a slice through the 4D maze, so the image is window pane fragments: 1024 px at Feature Scale 11 has 3146 and 3107 enclosed corridor pieces on 2 seeds, largest 0.3%, and all walls in one piece. Same result as the prototype. Native tiling would need cells wrapped by a period, not built. Reviewer: fnlab tile on the fixed DLL, default Feature Scale 11, seam diff 0.1884 vs interior 0.1920 (ratio 0.98). The Cave block preset reports ratio 3.15 (0.0068 vs 0.0021) because the torus slice of the inverted 4D output is almost all plateau; the largest pixel step anywhere in that tile image, wrap lines included, is 14 of 255 against a maze wall step of 255, so there is no seam.
data.versus_proto: Same character: even corridors, T branches and dead ends, nothing enclosed, block with tunnels in 3D, same fragments on the tile. Not the same field: hashes and the cut order differ. Warped labyrinth uses DomainWarpGradient where the prototype warps with Perlin, so bends are more angular and it shows more cells at Feature Scale 24. Sheet stats: real axis 19.99, isoCV 0.86, beta 5.42, prototype axis 14.46, isoCV 1.22, beta 5.08. The prototype's relief at Gain 2 is rounder and lower than real at Feature Scale 64, where fnlab relief makes walls tall and spiky, so the relief preset uses Gain 6 with flat floors and a small output range. Measured edge shares differ on purpose: the prototype's fixed order gives axis shares 1:2, 1:2:4, 1:2:4:8; real gives 0.50 / 0.50, 0.33 each, 0.25 each. Degree mix is close to the critic's numbers: dead ends 28%, branches 22%, 4-way 3%. Long straight walls at the larger cuts remain visible in plain views. Reviewer: the comparison regenerated from a84dd31 and viewed, plus an own seed 42 thumb and Levels 3 vol beside the prototype thumb. Same character as described; the hash change alters which edges open, not the look.
data.plan_changes: 1. Capped distances use D edge tests, not 18 / 81 / 324. With a forest that spans all cells, an edge missing the cell centre or a face missing the nearest corner is at least half a cell away, the centre always has an open edge, and a square of 4 edges cannot be open all round, so the rest is fixed geometry. Measured against the full window on CorridorDistance and WallDistance: largest difference 2.38e-07 over 400k, 200k and 60k samples in 2D, 3D, 4D. 2. Cut order is hashed per cube rather than fixed. The plan's fixed kd order was built and measured first: open edge share 0.33 / 0.67 in 2D, 0.14 / 0.29 / 0.57 in 3D, 0.07 / 0.13 / 0.27 / 0.53 in 4D, and every even edge on the last axis forced open, visible as columns. Hashed gives equal shares and costs 35-50% more (AVX2 1.43 / 2.34 / 3.15 before). Still recursive division. This goes beyond the plan, drop it by restoring a fixed order if the plan's exact rule is wanted. 3. The critic's one hash merged rule is replaced by one cube hash plus one block hash per edge. The top rule picks the first axis in the cube's order. Gates over 9 levels share hash bits, which only correlates them. 4. Levels clamped to 1..12 and Gain to +-1e30 in the setters. 5. Cap Distances False stays as a real window search, and has no effect on CorridorDistance and WallDistance, which clamp at half a cell as in the prototype. 6. The risk note that thresholding far from 0 loses connectivity did not reproduce unwarped: t = +-0.97 has 0 enclosed at 200 px per cell. At 15 px per cell t = +-0.9 shows over 1000 pieces, which is sampling of thin necks. Warp limit measured per node and written into the plan. 7 (reviewer). The cube hash key is seed ^ lowBit * 0x9E3779B1 instead of seed ^ lowBit, see notes.

data.notes: Limits to know. The guarantee holds in the evaluated dimension only: a slice or the tile torus is fragments. Warps: DomainWarpGradient with Warp Amplitude up to 0.3x its Feature Scale gave 0 enclosed pieces in 2D and 3D with 0 to 3 specks under 6 px on the presets, and some specks persist at 3000 px, so they may be real folds rather than sampling; 0.4x gave 1 to 2 enclosed, 0.5x gave 5 to 13 per phase. DomainWarpSimplex breaks at 0.2x (61 to 76 enclosed per phase) and shows 1 enclosed wall piece per seed already at 0.15x; DomainWarpSuperSimplex shows its first enclosed piece at 0.25x. Blocks of 2^Levels link by one passage in +axis direction, so components are infinite but directionally biased at that scale. Connectivity tests were repeated by the reviewer on the fixed DLL (proof.py, connect.py identical in kind, plus review.py with an independent edge reading). Metadata.cpp reservation sizes not touched. Reviewer: one defect fixed and committed as a84dd31 (cube hash key), see the review field.

review.found: seed ^ lowBit flips one key bit per level, so a cube and the sub cube sharing its corner had correlated cube hashes and the cut order is read straight from those bits. Measured through the node (2D, Levels 5, seed 0): P(first cut axis equal between a cube and its corner sub cube) 0.477 / 0.421 / 0.465 / 0.386 at levels 1..4 vs the lower level, 0.5 if independent. Emulation: per bit P(equal) of the two cube hashes 0.04 to 0.92 at level 11. The gate hash goes through a second HashPrimes and was already clean (0.499 to 0.502).
review.fix: HashPrimes( seed ^ ( lowBit * 0x9E3779B1 ), primedCube ). nestcorr after: 0.500 / 0.499 / 0.508 / 0.489. All gates, proof, connect, review reruns and gallery renders are from the fixed DLL.
review.not_changed: Levels above 9 overlap the 9 bit gate fields (author's note, correlates gate positions only, Levels 10 to 12 are cubes of 1024+ cells). Feature Scale 0 is finite but ISA dependent, Perlin is NaN there. Gain NaN would pass std::clamp, as in every other node. Metadata.cpp reservations untouched, 56 nodes registered against 47 reserved, a reservation only.
review.disagreements: None on substance. The author's numbers reproduced. The description's 'never form a loop or an enclosed piece' is right; it does not promise one connected maze, and blocks only ever link in the +axis direction so a finite window can show pieces that join outside it (the author notes this).

data.name: SplineRemap
data.check: clang-cl 23, real rebuild at 5669693, no warning from the node. 5 presets at seed 555111, and again at seed 8675309 and --scale 4: 'check passed: 0 FAIL, 0 WARN' on all, SSE2 and SSE41 vs AVX2 up to 4.05e-05 and AVX512 up to 1.69e-03 across both nodes' presets, 0.0000% off by more than 1e-2. 8 new setups at seed 2024 (SuperSimplex fractal with a plateau, CellularSmooth as Source and as Knot Out, all 8 knots from Perlin, knots past the Source range, inside FractalFBm and a warp): 0 FAIL except 'FAIL  non-constant: std 0.00000' on knots wholly past the Source range, where the curve is flat over Source, and WARN range on unclamped or summed trees. fnlab check tests finiteness on AVX2 only and its parity line cannot see NaN, so odd values went through a harness on all 4 feature sets at scattered, lattice, half lattice and far positions: 564 trees of constant values (0, -0, 1e-30, 1e-6, -1, 1e6, 1e30, 3e38, inf, nan on each Knot In and Knot Out, Knot Count from -2147483648 to 2147483647, all knots equal) and 90 trees through a Knot Out node give no NaN or Inf. The one exception is a Source of inf or nan with Clamp Output off, which passes through as stock Remap does. Fixed in this pass: a Knot Out node giving inf, nan or 3e38 gave NaN or Inf on up to every sample, while the same constant was clamped in the setter. The clamp moved into GenT: output is bit identical to before over 396 comparisons on 33 sane trees, and the cost is not separable from noise: AVX2 2D at 4 knots reads 2.31 to 2.38 on 4 of 6 runs and 2.89 and 3.36 on the other two, against 2.30 to 2.34 on 4 runs of the old DLL, and the first reviewer's 2.63 shows the old one spikes too. 2 and 8 knots read the same as before. Against a separate double precision reference written from Steffen 1990, 300 random knot sets in 4 feature sets: worst error 8.43e-06. Hybrid knots lane by lane against constant knots on scattered positions: exactly 0 in all 4 feature sets. Encoded round trip exact, including all defaults, reversed knots and knots set last to first. Parity on scattered positions over 450 random trees: 0 of 150 over the check's 0.2% limit with sorted knots and Clamp Output on, 2 of 150 with it off, 14 of 150 with unsorted knots, worst '99.46% off, max diff 2.30e+01' at |out| 2.4e6. These are stock AVX512 differences in the Source, such as 5e-05 from CellularDistance's own sites, multiplied by slopes in the thousands; mostly tiny against the output, up to 19% in a nested unclamped tree. Not a node defect, but a very steep curve does not hold fnlab's absolute parity. Other FAIL lines: 'FAIL non-constant: std 0.00000' at Knot 2 In of 1e30, where the curve is flat over Source, and 'FAIL simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 4.00e+24 3D 2.61e+24 4D 3.36e+24, samples off by >1e-2: 78.8452%' at Knot 2 Out of 1e30, rounding of values that size.
data.bench: ns/sample 2D / 3D / 4D, fnlab bench at 5669693, final run; single runs swing 10 to 30 percent, so expect AVX2 3D here to read 3.4 to 4.7 at 4 knots. Perlin alone: SSE41 2.17 / 4.20 / 8.95, AVX2 0.94 / 2.24 / 4.29, AVX512 0.64 / 1.30 / 3.47. 2 knots: SSE41 4.99 / 7.07 / 11.64, AVX2 1.90 / 3.15 / 5.04, AVX512 1.15 / 1.90 / 3.90. 4 knots: SSE41 5.08 / 7.20 / 11.79, AVX2 2.38 / 4.51 / 5.74, AVX512 1.59 / 2.29 / 4.27. 4 knots clamped: SSE41 4.74 / 7.11 / 11.55, AVX2 2.28 / 3.43 / 5.43, AVX512 1.50 / 2.24 / 4.24. 8 knots: SSE41 7.42 / 9.87 / 14.44, AVX2 3.56 / 4.79 / 6.72, AVX512 2.37 / 3.06 / 5.06. 4 knots with one Perlin Knot Out: AVX2 3.36 / 5.73 / 9.65, a rerun, as the first read 5.54 in 2D. Nested Ranges: SSE41 38.37 / 65.69 / 125.75, AVX2 17.28 / 35.08 / 68.48, AVX512 12.01 / 20.35 / 47.56. These agree with the author's table within noise.
data.range: No ScaleOutput or VariableRange: output is what the knots say, like Remap. Reviewer fuzz over 400 random knot sets: overshoot past the lowest and highest Knot Out at most 3.6e-07, between the end knots and anywhere when clamped. Without Clamp Output the curve carries on at the end slope, and a steep last segment throws far: [-0.658, 3.436] on the author's unclamped Coastal Shelf, and [-1326, -5.6] with reversed knots, where all of Source is below the first knot. All presets clamp.
data.seams: fnlab seams: 'SEAMS: none found' on the 5 presets (seeds -2024, 8675310 at --scale 4) and 8 new setups, 0 of 4000 in each dimension. Reference and C1: 1816 pairs of one sided cubic fits at inner knots give a median slope difference of 1.31e-06 and a max of 9.81e-05, overshoot past the lowest and highest Knot Out at most 2.98e-07, and no monotonic input came out non monotonic. Author's Simplex limit re-run, it holds: Mesa Country over Simplex reports 'jumps above 0.02' of 1 to 3 of 4000 in 3D and 0 to 2 in 4D on 3 seeds, worst 0.0421, against 0.0031 to 0.0058 for plain Simplex FBm, which reports none. The description states this.
data.far: Inherits Source. fnlab's far test only goes to 400 units here. Measured to 1e20 at Feature Scale 40: std over Perlin 0.326 to 0.329 up to 1e8, the same as stock Perlin, and both read a flat 0 from 1e9 on.
data.tile: Inherits Source, has a real 4D form because it is pointwise. 'tileable: seam 0.0039 interior 0.0028 (ratio 1.38)' on the default, no WARN on any preset. The tile image repeats with no visible seam.
data.versus_proto: The plan names no prototype and the catalogue says not prototyped as it is standard math, so there is no image to compare. A reviewer looked at the 5 presets on a new seed, 24601: Mesa Country has plateaus with cliffs, Coastal Shelf shelves into water, Folded Strata ledges, Nested Ranges lowlands with ranges, Cave Sheets thin membranes. No artifacts. Worth shipping.
data.plan_changes: Author: Knot In and Knot Out became 8 numbered slots because metadata has no arrays. Defaults changed from 0.0 and 0.0, which is no curve, to knots on the identity line, so any Knot Count starts as a pass through (reviewer measured max error 4.8e-07 at Knot Count 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8). No Slope members and no Extrapolate enum, following the plan's member list: slopes are automatic with Steffen's 1990 limiter, which rules out overshoot and works per lane with hybrid knots. So this is not a full Minecraft shaper with explicit derivatives. Clamp Output holds the end values and sets end slopes to 0, which keeps it C1, rather than clamping the result. As planned, all hybrid knots run for all lanes with no AnyMask skip. ScaleOutput does not apply. Reviewer adds what the author's list left out: the plan's data had Knot In as a hybrid, and it is a float here. The catalogue asks for constant locations, and limited slopes per lane need them sorted when set, so I agree with it, but it is a change. The catalogue's Coordinate is named Source. Reversed knots are spread 0.001 apart rather than sorted, which with Clamp Output off and identity Outs gives output down to -1326: seams reports 'jumps above 0.02: 4000 of 4000', a steep slope of about 50 per world unit and not a jump. Knot In's description warns of this. Review: nothing else left out silently. Knot Out is now clamped to +-1e30 in GenT and not in the setter, so a constant and a node behave the same.

data.name: Stamp
data.check: The default fails on geometry: fnlab check "Stamp()" gives 'FAIL  non-constant: std 0.00000' and 'CHECK FAILED: 1 FAIL, 5 WARN', because the check's 24 windows nearest reach is 145 world units from the origin and the default radius is 100, so every sample it reads is the 0 outside the stamp. That is the node doing what it says. With a radius that reaches them, each of the 7 profiles as Stamp(Feature Scale=6000) at --scale 40 on seeds 1337, 42, -7: 0 FAIL. Under StampScatter, each profile with defaults, plus 5 presets: 0 FAIL. 21 graphs. Worst feature set difference from AVX2 6.1e-06 (SSE2, SSE41), 2.3e-03 (AVX512), 0% off by more than 1e-2; the AVX512 figure is StampScatter's site jitter, standalone stays near 1e-06. WARNs: standalone 'WARN  seed sensitivity: mean |seed - seed+1| 0.0000' at Variation 0, 'WARN  far coordinates: std 0.000', 'WARN  tileable: seam 0.0000 interior 0.0000', all by design. Dome only: 'WARN  continuity 2D: worst step ratio 2.85 on axis 0', 3.36 in 3D, from its vertical edge, with no seams. Under StampScatter 'WARN  range: observed [0.000, 1.338]' from its Variance Preserving combine. Odd members (Feature Scale 0, -500, 1e-30, 1e30, Width 0, -1, 5, Count 0, -1, 100, Variation -1, 5): no NaN and no crash; the FAILs among them are the same non-constant. REVIEW: rebuilt and rerun by the reviewer. The default still fails gate 1 on seeds 9001 and 0 with 'FAIL  non-constant: std 0.00000', and this is geometry and not the node: Stamp(Feature Scale=150) at --scale 1 reads 0 FAIL. The same check's continuity probes do see the default's shape, 2D ratio 3.00. Keeping 100 is right, since the stamp fills StampScatter at equal Feature Scale, which also defaults to 100. data.versus_proto: All beside the prototype's own images, same world sizes, different hash so different stamps. Crater relief against the prototype: same flat floored big craters with rims and peaks in saturated small craters, hard to tell apart as a look; the real one has a few more faded shallow craters, because the soft Density fade is always on where the prototype's best params gate hard. Bubble relief against the prototype: same pack, domes have flatter tops and straight steep sides where the prototype has round hemispheres; 1 - q^2 in place of a sphere cap, chosen for the finite rim slope. Balls and Swiss cheese volumes against the prototype: same, the real Swiss cheese preset at Feature Scale 160 has the same hole sizes. Pebble relief against the prototype: same stones, a little flatter on top for the same reason. Pebble Stone Value against the prototype: same mosaic. Leaf against the prototype: same leaves and shadows, real one has darker midtones because its height is normalised to a bound where the prototype scales 1.6x and clamps. The prototype's 3D Leaf was an ellipsoid; the real 3D and 4D Leaf is a spindle around its axis. Pebble 3D is a flattened spheroid where the prototype had 3 radii, and there is no vol preset for it. REVIEW: rendered the prototype fresh at the plan's best params beside the real Moon craters preset and the real default at Feature Scale 400 (scratch contact sheet, 4 reliefs). Real and prototype at best params match: same big flat floored craters with peaks, same dense spiky carpet of mid sized rims between them. The gallery relief is smoother than the prototype at its stated best params, so that gallery image was not made with them; the real node matches the prototype, not that image.
data.plan_changes: 1. Feature Scale is the cell size of the first layer on every shape, so proto f0 moves into Feature Scale: f0=0.2 at the prototype's 80 px per unit is Feature Scale 400. 2. Base default 0, not 0.05, and it is a ground height: the prototype's 0.05 weighted a built in FBm. A constant 0.05 only shifts the level and pushes Bubble and Pebble past their range. Remap FBm to +-0.11 gives the prototype look, the Moon craters preset does that. Crater erases it, Bubble and Pebble sit on it, Leaf hides it, Stone Value and Layer Index show it in gaps. 3. Edge Softness default 0.03, not 0: at 0 every Leaf and Stone Value jumps by design, 0.03 is the prototype's best leaf and 0 stays available. 4. Pebble Height is Max of the stone tops, the prototype's comp=1 best params, not front to back as the plan row said. Stone Value, Layer Index and Leaf occlude. 5. Domes on Bubble and Pebble are 1 - q^2, not parabolic or a sphere cap: finite rim slope, rounder than the parabola, no sqrt. 6. Density fade band is relative to the layer's fill: an absolute 0.25 band left no whole craters on sparse layers, so Frequency Slope 3 lost its large craters and read range -0.28..0.30. Bubble's cell occupancy comes from the hash alone so that children can clear parents without reading Density, so a faded bubble still pushes others away. 7. Radius Power range is 1 to 8 and uses u^whole * lerp( 1, u, fraction ) in place of FS::Pow, which took Bubble from 28 to 60 ns on AVX2 with no visible gain. 8. Layers does not count the ground, the prototype's backstop layer did. Leaf default in the note is 9 for that reason. 9. Lattice rotations: 2D steps 90 degrees / golden ratio on every shape. 3D and 4D steps are the best of 200000 random rotations by largest entry over powers 1 to 16 (0.97 and 0.89). The prototype's 3D matrix is an exact 90 degree rotation, so it repeated every 4 levels. 10. Stones use one random axis from the hash rather than a rotation or quaternion: shared by all dimensions and cheaper. Pebble is a spheroid, Leaf a spindle. 11. Vein is max( 1 - 2y, 0 )^3 in place of exp. 12. Whole batch skips with FS::AnyMask, a stamp out of reach of every lane: Bubble AVX2 29.65 / 34.65 / 41.60 to 15.41 / 12.03 / 13.59, others 5 to 20%. Results unchanged: sorted against shuffled lanes differ by exactly 0, except 2.4e-7 on Leaf with shadow, cause not isolated. 13. Not split into classes: it stays one node as the plan says, but the members read as shape specific and defaults suit Crater only, so Layers and Lacunarity carry per-shape values in their notes. The 2-cell top level stays out as planned.

Batch skips checked by hand: a skipped stamp contributes exactly 0 on Crater, Bubble, Pebble and Leaf without shadow, and the Leaf shadow band fits inside the confinement radius for Shadow Fit 0.38 (worst point at the leaf tip). One defect fixed: Stone Value drew UnitLow of MixHash salt 5, the same bits as Pebble's height jitter and Leaf's height offset, so Stone Value was an exact function of the stone's height; LayerValue now uses salt 6. Not changed, noted: Shadow Strength 0 against any positive value changes the leaf length (length = radius - 1.2 band only when a shadow is cast), a parameter step not a spatial one; Bubble children only clear the parent in the cell that holds their centre, so a child can overlap a parent across a parent cell wall; Base is erased by craters where the prototype added its FBm after the fold; Edge Softness is in cells of each layer, so on fine Crater layers at Feature Scale 100 the band is sub pixel and Stone Value is hard edged in practice. Disagreement with the author: the crater relief claim should be read against the prototype at its best params, not against the gallery image.

Preset WARNs the author did not list: continuity ratio 2.1 / 1.9 / 2.1 on Pebble mosaic and 3.7 / 3.5 in 3D / 4D on Crater field, cusps inherited from the stamp graphs (sqrt dome, clamped cone), seams 0 of 4000. Parity FAILs only on setups that are discontinuous or absurd: Source White (97%), Density White (SSE2 17% in 3D, White reads float bits at Round() * Feature Scale), Stamp Zoom 1e6, Feature Scale 1e6 with a Feature Scale 100 Perlin (67%). AVX512 cause confirmed: Jitter 0 takes the Zoom 64 max diff from 3.8e-3 to 1e-5, and FastSIMD InvSqrt is _mm256_rsqrt_ps on AVX2 but _mm512_rsqrt14_ps on AVX512, so CellWindow's jitter differs by up to ~2e-4 cells. The limit is Source features per stamp radius, not Stamp Zoom alone: Perlin at 64 and 128 features per radius pass (max diff 6.7e-3), 256 gives 0.0224% off, 1e4 fails. Member description rewritten to say so.

data.versus_proto: Stripes against the prototype: same labyrinth, same stroke width and stroke lengths, hard to tell apart as a look. Not the same pixels: real sites use K3's disc jitter and hash. Craters against the prototype relief: same bowls with a flat plain between, the rims are sharper because the stamp is a stock graph with piecewise linear profiles and not the prototype's smoothsteps; Crater field range -2.03..0.46 against the critic's -2.35..0.60. Dense domes against the prototype: same bright domes with thin dark creases. I did not put the ribbon volume beside the prototype's stripes volume: the gallery volume I viewed uses a different stamp. Real stamps need stock nodes for their shape, so domes, craters and stripes are small graphs in the presets instead of the prototype's built in sources. REVIEW: stripes thumb beside the prototype: same labyrinth and stroke width to stamp ratio; the real preset at Feature Scale 48 draws its stamps about two thirds the size of the prototype thumb, so more of them per image.
data.plan_changes: 1. Size cap is 1.5 - kCellJitter<D> * Jitter, about 1.5 - 0.44 Jitter, not 1.5 - 0.5 Jitter: the node uses K3's disc jitter. 2. Density reads the stamp's lattice point and not the jittered centre: that float is identical from every sample, while site + sample rounds per sample and could flip a stamp on and off. 3. Source frame: stamp radius maps to Feature Scale world units times Stamp Zoom, so a default Source has about one feature per radius; the prototype's frame was radius 1 with its own built in sources. 4. Overlap Count ramps each stamp from 0 to 1 over the outer eighth of ( 1 - q ) in place of a hard count, so it stays continuous and passes the jump scan; it reads count / 4 - 1 as in the prototype. 5. CellTopK::Insert is not used: with it and runtime slot loops clang 23 kept slots in memory and lowered Select to vmaskmovps on AVX2, so K=4 cost 123 ns in 3D against 102 on SSE41. Fixed index insertion in Scatter.inl: 47 ns, 0 vmaskmov in Gen. CellularEdge has 0 vmaskmov in AVX2 Gen, so this is not a problem in that node. 6. Whole batch skips added with FS::AnyMask, sites out of reach of every lane and slots with zero weight on every lane: K=2 AVX2 3D went from 92.36 to 46.15 ns before the insert fix, Density evals 27 down to the sites in reach. Not a per lane branch, and lane mix leaves results unchanged (exact 0). 7. 4D rotation is a left quaternion product rather than two plane rotations, no extra hash, no fixed plane. gMetadataVectorSize left alone. I did not run it to clear that.

data.check: fnlab check on the default node and on the 6 preset and candidate trees: 0 FAIL, 0 WARN each, including SSE2, SSE41, AVX2 and AVX512 parity (default: SSE2 and SSE41 max diff 3.28e-06, AVX512 0, 0.0000% of samples off by more than 1e-2). Wider battery of 33 runs over both direction modes, both topologies, both outputs, Envelope Normalise, hybrid Strength, Octaves 1, 8 and 16, scales 0.37 and 3, degenerate parameters, FractalFBm and DomainWarpGradient over the node: 30 pass, 0 NaN/Inf in any run. The 3 that fail, verbatim. Octaves=16, Gain=1: 'FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 6.48e-02 3D 3.26e-02 4D 3.25e-02, samples off by >1e-2: 4.9927%', the same line for SSE41, 'FAIL  entry parity 2D: grid vs positions 1.15e-02, grid vs single 6.41e-03'. Stock FractalFBm of Perlin at Octaves=16, Gain=1 fails the same three checks (2.28e-02, 0.2482%), this is float position precision at 2^15 times the frequency, made worse here by the rounding of the octave rotation. Sweep over even octave counts: 0 FAIL through 16 octaves at Gain 0.6 and through 14 at Gain 0.8, entry parity fails first at 16 at Gain 0.8 and 14 at Gain 1, and 14 octaves at Gain 0.8 already WARNs 4 times. Angle=1e9: 'FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 8.14e-02 3D 3.23e-02 4D 2.05e-02, samples off by >1e-2: 41.0624%' and the same for SSE41, PolyMath::SinCos is only accurate without FMA up to about 1e5 rad; Angle=1e4 passes. All setters at their clamps (Anisotropy Sum=100, Min Eigenvalue=-3, Gain=100, Lacunarity=100, Octaves=99): 'FAIL  non-constant: std 0.00001', the top octave at 8^15 times the frequency has lost all fraction and dominates at Gain 4. WARN lines on usable settings: range -1.168 at 8 octaves Gain 0.8 Lacunarity 1.9, range -1.252 at 16 octaves Gain 1; Output Min=0, Output Max=5 WARNs on range by design. Reviewer re-run on a fresh -j4 build, 38 check + seams cases: the 5 presets at seed 7, Strength 0, -5, 100 and a Perlin crossing 0, Angle -1000, Octave Rotation off at angles 0 and pi/2, Min Eigenvalue 0, -7 and 100 with Sheets, Anisotropy Sum 0, -9 and 1e30, Gain 0, -1 and 2, Lacunarity 0, -3 and 0.5 with 6 octaves, Octaves 0, -4 and 1 in both outputs, Envelope Normalise at 1 octave, Vector mode with all directions 0, +-1e30, +-1e-9 and 4 Perlin sources with Sheets in 4D, Feature Scale -40, Seed Offset -2147483647, FractalRidged and DomainWarpGradient over the node: 36 pass with 0 FAIL, 0 NaN/Inf anywhere, SEAMS none found. Feature Scale=0.001 fails 'FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 1.02e-01 3D 8.58e-02 4D 6.22e-02, samples off by >1e-2: 18.3695%' and entry parity 3.41e-02, where stock Perlin(Feature Scale=0.001) fails the same three lines (1.32e-02, 0.2482%) and FractalFBm of it 4.38e-02, 1.6317%. FractalRidged over the node WARNs range 1.748 exactly as stock FractalRidged of Perlin does (1.750). data.versus_proto: 2D Angle field: same character as the prototype, swirling combed grain with even width, the hillshade reads as boughs or feathers. Not the same field: the port uses the stock 8 gradient table where the prototype used random unit vectors, and the angle source is stock Perlin at +-6.28 rad, not the prototype's unit gradient perlin2 times 2 pi, so individual curls differ. Measured at 1 octave: aspect 2.63-2.79 over 7 angles, flat, standard deviation flat to 1.5%, lattice imprint 25-33x, 1.7-2.3x with Envelope Normalise; 4 octaves 5.4-6.5x, 1.4-1.7x with Envelope Normalise. These agree with the prototype's 2.9, 21-31x, 2.1x, 5.3x and 1.6x; my L estimator is a derivative ratio, not the prototype's, so aspect is not directly comparable. 3D Sheets: the same torn laminated slabs. 3D differs in the direction source, the prototype took the gradient of one Perlin and the node has no gradient input, so renders use separate Perlin hybrids. With equal Feature Scale all of them are 0 at the same lattice vertices and left a concentric rosette there, and even with different scales one remained at the origin, which a bias on one axis removes. 3D Fibres at 2 octaves is a sponge like the prototype's image, at 4 octaves its surface is much rougher, and the fibre aspect is weak in both (measured 1.7). Sheets aspect 2.4. Reviewer, the image, viewed, numbers: prototype thumb at --window 8 --seed 1337 (64 px per feature) against the node at Feature Scale 64 with Angle Perlin(Feature Scale 427, +-6.28) seed 1337, gray panels: std 0.135 vs 0.143, mean gradient 0.0435 vs 0.0455, structure tensor coherence 0.715 vs 0.709, spectral slope -3.05 vs -3.08, peak 5 vs 6 cycles per panel. Same combed swirl; the curls differ as the author says. A node relief at Feature Scale 40 and 80 looked much spikier than the prototype's relief, which is a window and height scale mismatch in my renders, not the node.
data.plan_changes: Angle is in radians, matching DomainRotate, the plan did not say; a noise source needs Output Min/Max of about +-6. Topology applies to 3D and 4D with 2D ignoring it, the plan said 3D only: 4D Sheets has 3 slow axes and 1 fast. Added amplitude compensation sqrt( 3.6 / sum ); the reviewer measured that it holds only near the default sum (std 0.235 at 2, 0.183 at 1 against 0.250), the header comment and help text were corrected to say so. Ridged uses 1 - 2 |n| per octave normalised by the summed amplitudes, not the prototype's 0.75 - 2.5 |n| with root sum square normalisation, because a mean of 0.4 makes the root sum square form overshoot. Envelope floor is 0.004 D on the unsquared form, equal to the prototype's 0.004 on the form divided by D. Setters clamp: Anisotropy Sum 0.1..3.99, Min Eigenvalue at least 0 and at Gen time at most what keeps every eigenvalue non negative, Octaves 1..16, Gain 0..4, Lacunarity 0.125..8. Member list, defaults and the absence of the 4x4 window follow the plan.

data.review: Independent review, commit 37e8c34. Code read in full: no per-lane branches (every branch is on a uniform member), one hash per corner with the stock HashPrimes XOR, int conversion identical to Perlin, no division that can reach 0 (1e-12 on the direction length, 0.004 D under the envelope root, clamps on sum, octaves, gain and lacunarity), every member used, metadata defaults equal the plan table, registration last in FastSIMD_Build.inl, no test node in the diff. SinCos argument order, the 3D rotation (orthonormal, det 1), the 4D quaternion matrix and the 2D gradient length behind kEnvelopeGradient were checked by hand. Hybrids are sampled with the incoming seed before Seed Offset, as Cellular does. Gates re-run on a fresh -j4 build: check, seams, bench, far, tile, and a matched-window comparison with the prototype, all above. One change made: the sqrt( 3.6 / sum ) amplitude claim of 'within 5%' was false below sum 2 (27% quiet at 1), so the header comment and the Anisotropy Sum help text now state the measured falloff; no behaviour changed. Not re-measured: ARM, WASM, MSVC and GCC builds, the author's grain aspect numbers, 3D renders against the prototype vol images.
data.notes: Usable with limits. Grain length is capped by the 2 corner window: aspect near 3 in 2D, 1.7 for 3D Fibres, 2.4 for 3D Sheets. Tiling is seamless but loses the grain. Min Eigenvalue under 0.5 buys little length for more lattice imprint: aspect 2.70 at 0.5, 3.18 at 0.3 with sum 3.9, 3.52 at 0.05, imprint 28x, 51x, 64x. Vector mode with Perlin sources at equal scale leaves a rosette at each lattice vertex, stated in the Direction description. Vortex and Tree rings are centred for the 512 and 256 unit views, panning moves the centre. Licence provenance, plainly: I read the paper's text from the PDF on the Disney Animation publications page, and wrote the port from its algorithm 1 and section 3.1, with the bound's proof derived myself (the lattice weighted mean of v' G v over a cell's corners is at most tr( G ) / 4, in any dimension). I never opened the unlicensed reference repo. I could not find the supplemental, the publication page lists none, so the closed form metric, the eigenvalue split, the octave scheme and envelope normalisation are not from it. This is not a clean room: as instructed I read the lab prototype first, whose own header says it was not clean room either, and the octave scheme, Fibres and Sheets split and envelope formula follow its behaviour and the plan; the code is new. 3D and 4D constants were measured on clang-cl 23 x86 only, no ARM, WASM, MSVC or GCC build was run. Not re-measured here: the critic's graph match at constant angle and the loss of flow under a parent FractalFBm. Strata preset rendered and viewed but cut to keep 5.

Shrunken islands "WARN  tileable: seam 0.0141 interior 0.0015 (ratio 9.49), std 0.795". Odd values: every mode with Radius, Rotation and Amount at 0, -1, -50, 1e-6, 1e6, 1e9, 1e30, -1e30, 1e38, -1e38 and Taps at -5, 0, 1, 2, 3, 16, 17, 999: 0 crash, 0 NaN or Inf. data.seams: fnlab seams at --scale 1: 0 jumps of 4000 in 2D, 3D and 4D on the 4 continuous presets (worst 0.0049 over 0.000977) and every mode x Taps x Radius in the sweep with Taps 6 and 16. Taps 3: Local Rank Radius 40 shows 1 of 4000 in 4D at 0.0368, gone at --scale 0.25 (0.0009 over 0.000244), a steep point and not a jump. Taps 2 was flagged by Peak Margin and Local Rank (isolated points where both taps meet the centre), so the floor is now 3. Peak Margin and Local Rank at --scale 4 and 16: 0 jumps. Pebble mosaic and Paving stones FAIL the scan with 4000 of 4000 on all dimensions, worst 1.97 and 1.58: that is CellularValue, which shows 4000 of 4000 at 1.99 on its own. A filter of a discontinuous source keeps the jumps, Rank and Local Rank only move them. Reviewer rerun: same on all 6 presets, also at --seed 777. Peak Margin at Amount 0 is flagged as jumps by the scan, 1746 of 4000 at 0.0989 over 0.000977, but the worst step scales with the bisection step (0.0178 over 0.000244), so it is a hard disc edge and not a jump.
data.far: check far coordinate test passes on all presets. Wrapped in DomainOffset 1e5, 1e6, 1e7 on Blue noise dots: range -1 to 1, mean -0.837, -0.845, -0.840, std 0.518, 0.505, 0.514, so the look holds. Continuity ratio there 1.97, 1.01, 1.26, max slope 8.4, 60, 507 against 1.9 near: plain Perlin under the same wrap reads ratio 3.00, 1.00, 1.02, so that is float position steps scaled up by the margin. Not in the description.
data.tile: Real 4D form with 4D taps, GenTileable2D works. fnlab tile at size 1024: Blue noise dots ratio 5.38, Pebble mosaic 1.15, Paving stones 1.11, Slope web 1.06, Rounded summits 1.09, Shrunken islands 1.38. The 5.38 is the tool comparing one row against one row on a sparse mask. Measured over every row and column of the tile instead (8 bit), the wrap row sits at the 52nd percentile of the interior rows for dots, at the 2nd to 75th for all 6, so no preset has a raised seam. In 4D the taps spread over both circles of the torus, so an image sees about 0.7 x Radius: stated on the Radius member. Reviewer rerun at size 1024 gives the same ratios. Wrap pair percentile against interior over every row and column: Blue noise dots 41 and 61, Pebble mosaic 21 and 26, Paving stones 4 and 23, Slope web 2 and 4, Rounded summits 85 and 43, Shrunken islands 74 and 77: no raised seam.
data.range: No ScaleOutput and no VariableRange, as the plan has it: Blur, Sharpen, Erode, Dilate and Rank follow the source, so no constant fits. Measured on 2 octave Perlin, Taps 6: Blur -0.942..0.960 at Radius 8, -0.428..0.416 at 40. Sharpen -1.155..1.208 and -1.860..2.016. Erode down to -1.142, Dilate up to 1.162, Rank -0.991..0.991 and -0.586..0.626. Range, Peak Margin and Local Rank are clamped to -1..1 by construction and measured there: Range -0.971..1.000, Peak Margin and Local Rank -1.000..1.000. Sharpen leaving the range is stated on its Mode line. Reviewer on a wider window of 1024 world units, default Taps 6, sees wider extremes as expected: Blur -1.044..1.031 at Radius 8, Sharpen -2.153..2.078 at Radius 40, Rank -1.071..1.064 at Radius 8. No mode claims a fixed range it misses.

data.versus_proto: Reviewer, properly framed: smp_lens mode 2 at r 0.625, K 8, w 0.05 over 8 features has 40 blobs of median diameter 0.47 features. Real Blue noise dots over 8 features has 37 blobs, also 0.47 features. They agree. The cause of the framing trouble the author hit: fnlab.exe and smp_lens.exe predate --panel, ignore it and show 512 px of world in a 256 px panel; fnlab_hq.exe honours it. Looked at side by side the two read the same: separated polygonal blobs on the peaks with thin soft edges, some elongated. The author's blob figures do not reproduce. Over 6 seeds and 1024 world units at f > 0: 283 blobs, median diameter 19 world units, not 10; Clark-Evans 1.41 (1.39 to 1.43), 1.33 with an edge guard, not 1.58. 70 blobs and 1.58 fit one seed in a 512 window, where edge bias and seed spread (1.39 to 1.56) reach that value. Blobs keep a weak lock to a Perlin source's lattice: first harmonic 0.12 and 0.07, where uniform reads 0.02. On Simplex 0.04 and 0.02. Looks at the reviewer's sheet: Rank on CellularValue gives rounded pebbles with some small notches, Local Rank on CellularValue gives convincing paving, Range gives a worm web, Erode on a hard mask shows the speck rings the author reports. Author on rotation stands: rotation turns the stencil polygons and does not hide them. Erode and Dilate as no slope limiter stands: max slope per world unit 0.0999 source, 0.1003 Dilate, 0.0928 Erode, 0.0486 Blur at Radius 14, Taps 12 on 4 octaves.
data.plan_changes: 1. Modes added: Range, Rank (from rank-taps) and Local Rank (from local-rank). The plan said it absorbs those but listed no mode for them. 2. Radius default 20, was 5: Blur at 5 on the default Perlin moved the source by 0.004 rms against its std 0.318 (1.3%), 20 moves it 0.052 (16%). 3. Members Rotation and Amount added, the plan row had neither though it asked for rotated taps and Sharpen. 4. Taps clamped 3 to 16, table built when set. 5. Peak Margin is 2 x ( c - hi ) / ( Amount x ( c - lo ) ) mapped to a -1 to 1 mask, in place of the prototype ( c - hi ) / w with w in source height: the same setting now works at any source height. Normalising by the tap spread instead lost elongated peaks (17 of 66 tops pass with this form at default Radius, it was 7). Default Radius 20 on Feature Scale 100 is still sparse and dim, Radius near half the Feature Scale is what looks good, and the Mode line says so. 6. Local Rank width comes from the local spread, for the same reason. 7. 4D taps are a lattice on the Clifford torus, not super-Fibonacci as first written: at Taps 6 covariance anisotropy 0.73 against 0.20 and tile footprint 0.69 against 0.40, where 1 is even. 8. The plan claimed Erode and Dilate stand in for slope limiting (terrain lens hole 2). Measured they do not: max slope per feature on 4 octave FBm, 0.064 source, 0.061 Dilate, 0.072 Erode, 0.033 Blur. Why text and the gaps row changed to say no. gMetadataVectorSize left alone. Reviewer: Amount is floored at 0.01 of the spread in Peak Margin and Local Rank. The plan why text said Clark-Evans 1.58, which the review could not reproduce, corrected to 1.41. Not in the report above: the catalogue modes HighPass, PitMargin, Roughness and LocalNormalize, and the PeakMask and Contrast modes of local-rank, are not built. The plan row did not ask for them.

data.check: After the reviewer's fix, gates.py: 26 graphs on seeds 1337, 42, -7, 78 runs: 0 FAIL, 56 WARN. New run at seeds 2026 and -123456, 17 graphs, the 5 presets plus new sources and member values: 0 FAIL on every ordinary setup. FAILs only on degenerate members, none NaN: Feature Scale=0 'FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 1.17e-01 3D 5.45e-02 4D 4.99e-02, samples off by >1e-2: 1.1434%', the same for SSE41, since frequency clamps to 1e6 and cells are below a float step; Mean=inf, which clamps to 1e30, and Mean=1e30 fail parity with output near 1e30, for example 'FAIL  simd parity SSE2 vs AVX2: max diff 2D 9.82e+23 3D 8.69e+23 4D 8.69e+23, samples off by >1e-2: 93.7744%', 'FAIL  entry parity 2D: grid vs positions 4.91e+23, grid vs single 2.64e+23'. Default on Perlin(Feature Scale=30), seed 1337: 0 FAIL, 1 WARN 'range: observed [-1.001, 1.227]', the Variance Preserving limit in the range field. SSE2 and SSE41 vs AVX2 max diff 5.51e-06 2D, 5.98e-06 3D, 3.21e-06 4D; AVX512 vs AVX2 3.90e-06, 3.38e-06, 3.73e-06; 0.0000% of samples off by >1e-2; grid vs positions 2.26e-06; continuity ratio 7.90 / 7.87 / 7.91. Worst parity in any run 1.89e-03, Shard mosaic, 0.0000% off by >1e-2. WARNs: the node's own are range on Variance Preserving; the rest are the source's, FractalFBm of Simplex, Euclidean cellular, Checkerboard. Odd values: 216 configs, every member at 0, -0, -5, 1e-42, 1e-6, 1e12, +-1e30, +-3.4e38, +-inf, NaN, all modes, SSE2, SSE41, AVX2, AVX512, positions, grid, tile, positions to 3e38. Non finite only where Source itself outputs inf, NaN or 3.4e38 (8 configs). Before the fix Mean=+-3.4e38, +-inf and NaN gave NaN on Variance Preserving. Not built with MSVC or GCC, clang-cl 23 only.
data.seams: fnlab seams on the same 78 runs: none, 0 of 4000 above 0.02, worst 0.0002 in 2D and 3D, 0.0001 in 4D on the default, except the Checker mosaic preset on all 3 seeds, the Checkerboard's own jump (2.0 at spacing 0.000977). Seeds 2026, -123456: the same, plus the degenerate Feature Scale=0 and Mean=inf. The weights are barycentric, exactly 0 on the faces where a vertex leaves, raised to at least power 2, so there are no creases on simplex faces from the node.

data.range: Inherits the source's range with no ScaleOutput and no VariableRange, as a domain modifier: the output is a blend of source values, so gate 4's constant does not apply, and a constant cannot fit an unknown source. Variance Preserving is the exception that leaves it. Plan's first check, histogram across blend zones, default Sharpness, patch 80, 2D, core = largest weight > 0.8 (12% of samples), blend = largest weight < 0.5 (25%). Variance Preserving, std alone / core / blend: Perlin 0.325 / 0.316 / 0.324, FBm 0.375 / 0.373 / 0.368, Simplex 0.543 / 0.545 / 0.542, Value 0.433 / 0.445 / 0.432, Euclidean cellular with Mean -0.58 0.190 / 0.191 / 0.190, Sine 0.498 / 0.498 / 0.496, Checker 1.000 / 1.000 / 0.999. Mean stays within 0.021. So variance holds, but shape does not on non Gaussian sources: kurtosis in blend zones Simplex 1.80 to 2.16, Checker 1.00 to 1.62. Samples outside [-1, 1]: Perlin 0.018%, Simplex 1.49%, Sine 1.37%, Checker 49.1% with extremes +-1.731, the theoretical sqrt(3). check flags it above 1.15, and now does on the default on Perlin at seed 1337. Linear stays within the source's values and loses 10 to 11% of std on all of these. Height stays within too and leans upward, mean Perlin +0.076, FBm +0.100, Simplex +0.211, Sine +0.181, Cellular +0.026, Checker +0.688. With Rotation 0 and Offset 0, all copies equal: Linear returns the source to 6.6e-07, Variance Preserving swells by 1.000 to 1.728, median 1.072.

data.versus_proto: A prototype does exist, the author's report missed it: mat_inv mode 9, PatchRot, the catalogue's PatchTuft, a triangular lattice with a variance preserving blend of 3 stretched sources. Reviewer rendered it beside the Straw tangle preset: the same look, crossed clumps of straw in patches of similar size and grain. The prototype has much more contrast because it multiplies by 1.6 and clamps to [-1, 1]; the node can't clamp an unknown source, so it is softer, range [-1.356, 1.319], std 0.373. Other presets re-rendered after the fix: turned squares on a checker, interlocked shards with Height on crackle, fibres in the volume. Tile without repeats: correlation at lag 128 falls from 1.000 on the bare tile to within +-0.037 at seeds 1337, 2026, and stays 0.976 with Offset 0, so the Offset text is right. The tile's motif still recurs at random spots, so this removes the grid and not the motif. Neighbouring lattice vertices draw unrelated patches: turn angle correlation at most 0.0011, shift 0.0035, over lags to 8. The author's TileDomain brick try is not repeated, so the catalogue's plank to herringbone claim stays untested. Worth shipping on anisotropic sources; on isotropic noise near the feature size it earns little.
data.plan_changes: 1) Mode gains Height from the catalogue beside the plan's Linear. 2) Rotation (hybrid, 0 to 1), Offset, Sharpness and Mean added from the catalogue: Rotation 0 is what keeps directions meaningful, Offset must reach a repeating source's period, Sharpness keeps high contrast sources, and without Mean a cellular source goes dark at patch centres (mean -0.666 vs -0.578 alone). 3) Left out to keep it small: scale jitter, the per vertex seed toggle, Sharpen. 4) Weights are barycentric from sorted skewed fractions, not Simplex falloff kernels, so they are exactly 0 on simplex faces in every dimension, where the 0.6 radius kernels of 3D and 4D Simplex jump. 5) Rotation uses no trig: complex numbers in 2D, quaternions in 3D and 4D, from a triangular hash value, 36 bin orientation histogram max/min 1.12 in 2D. Slope of a linear source deep in a patch is 0.987 to 1.013 of the source's in all dimensions, so the turn is rigid. 7) Reviewer: shift fields are 7 bits, since HashPrimes leaves bit 31 clear, and Mean is held to +-1e30. Also not mentioned by the author: the catalogue's Height Influence member and its w - 0.75 max w step were left out, a fixed 0.9 factor plus Sharpness does that job.

data.check: 14 graphs on seeds 1337, 42, -7: each Mode, Direction along z, connected Length, Decay 1, Taps 1, all presets: 0 FAIL. Worst feature set difference from AVX2 1.5e-05 (SSE2, SSE41) and 4.2e-04 (AVX512), the latter from StampScatter spots, 0% off by more than 1e-2. Grid, positions and single agree to 3.8e-06. WARNs: 'WARN  range: observed [-0.976, 1.206]' on FBm, whose own range that is. On Rust runs and Uneven drips, seed 1337 only, 'WARN  tileable: seam 0.0038 interior 0.0009 (ratio 4.13), std 0.050': that image is sparse dots, so the ratio turns on whether a seam row crosses one. Seeds 42 and -7 read clean. Odd members (Taps 0, -3, 1000, Decay 0, -1, 5, Length 0, -100, 1e30, -1e30, Direction 1e30, 1e-30, all 0): 0 FAIL, no NaN. Exact identities against the source, largest difference: Taps 1 0, Length 0 in Max and Min 0, in Mean 1.8e-07, Direction all 0 in Max 0, Direction only along Z in 2D 0. REVIEW: rebuilt and rerun by the reviewer. All 5 presets on seed 9001 and 6 new graphs (diagonal Direction, Direction along W, negative Length, Min on CellularDistance, Decay 0.001 at Taps 2, a source from 0 to 5) on seeds 9001 and 0: 0 FAIL, and the 14 graphs of the author rerun on the final Gen, total FAIL 0. Formula against numpy for Max, Min and Mean: at most 4.1e-08. One defect, fixed: a Length or Direction that overflowed gave NaN on every sample in Mean, Length 1e39, Direction X 1e39, and a hybrid Length from a node giving inf or NaN. Max and Min hid it on x86 only. Now a non finite spacing means no smear, and Direction is held to +-1e38, so it normalises as usual. 1e38 and under behaved already. A source that gives inf or NaN still passes it on, as every node does.
data.seams: fnlab seams on the 14 graphs: 0 of 4000 above 0.02 in 2D, 3D, 4D, worst 0.0012 over 0.001. Note a Length from a node with jumps carries them over: an early Uneven drips used CellularValue and its cell edges showed as cuts in the streaks, so the preset uses Perlin and the member note warns of it.
data.far: DomainOffset on x and y, Perlin 70: follows the source, std 0.29 to 0.35, p99 step 0.027 to 0.030 up to 1e7 with the source 0.027 to 0.030, and 0.185 at 1e8 with the source 0.19. Finite. Nothing to add to the description.
data.tile: Seamless but it loses the look, and this one matters. fnlab tile ratio 0.76 to 1.55 at --scale 1, seam rank over 10 seeds mean 0.31, so no seam. But the tails run in 4D, off the surface of the torus: Rust runs as a tile shows the bright spots with no streaks. The catalogue's claim that offsets happen before the torus mapping is wrong, as a node only ever sees the 4D position. The description says so. A real fix needs the 4D form to turn the two torus planes instead of moving along an axis, which assumes a tile, so it was not done.
data.range: Follows the source, with no ScaleOutput or VariableRange: a tap can only fade a value, so it never leaves the source's range, and gate 4's constant does not apply. Measured over 3 seeds, Perlin source -0.889 to 0.866: Max -0.885 to 0.866, Mean -0.785 to 0.731, Min -0.889 to 0.851. FBm source -1.102 to 1.184: Max -0.852 to 1.184, Mean -0.759 to 0.735, Min -1.102 to 0.825. Direction: a spot at y 128 with Direction Y=1 has its tail at larger y, which is down in fnlab's images: -1 above it, -0.219 at y 160, -0.752 at y 200, -0.985 at y 215 with Length 80.
data.bench: fnlab bench, ns/sample, 2D / 3D / 4D, smaller of 2 runs. On Perlin(Feature Scale=70), alone SSE41 2.10 / 4.08 / 8.65, AVX2 0.91 / 2.12 / 4.11, AVX512 0.62 / 1.25 / 3.13: Max Taps 8 SSE41 18.31 / 34.59 / 70.36, AVX2 7.72 / 17.35 / 31.99, AVX512 5.22 / 10.10 / 26.65. Taps 32 AVX2 30.15 / 67.31 / 125.47. Mean Taps 8 AVX2 7.33 / 16.59 / 31.87. So Taps x source plus under 0.1 ns per tap. On Constant, Taps 8: Max AVX2 1.64 / 1.91 / 2.16. fnlab bench has no SSE2 row. Presets are not cheap, because a clean long streak needs many taps of a costly source, AVX2: Rust runs 180.97 / 488.21 / 1520.68, Uneven drips 257.02 / 663.56 / 2074.87, Rain stains 298.39 / 597.16 / 1063.05, Brush strokes 117.54 / 296.72 / 405.40, Curtain folds 196.65 / 418.35 / 788.30. REVIEW, fnlab bench, smaller of 2 runs: reproduced within noise, before and after the guard. Max 8 on Perlin AVX2 8.07 / 17.26 / 32.16 before, 7.92 / 17.72 / 32.59 after, SSE41 18.62 / 35.23 / 71.37, AVX512 5.35 / 10.22 / 25.76. Max 8 on Constant AVX2 1.61 / 1.94 / 2.23. Rust runs 182.64 / 498.36 / 1552.19.
data.versus_proto: Never prototyped, so there is no image to compare. Judged by eye: worth shipping for Max on sparse bright spots, where Rust runs and Uneven drips look like real weathering, and for Rain stains. Mean is an ordinary one-sided blur (Brush strokes), fine but plain. Max on dense FBm (Curtain folds) reads as hanging folds and shows some terracing in the tails at Taps 64. A Snow drift relief and a Brushed metal attempt were dull and were left out. REVIEW: the plan names no prototype image and the prototypes have none for this node. Looked, Rust runs and Rain stains: tails read as described, and Curtain folds does show terracing in its tails at Taps 64.
data.plan_changes: 1) Decay is now the weight left at the last tap, default 0.1, not a weight per tap of 0.7: per tap, doubling Taps to fix banding also halved the streak. 0.7 per tap over 8 taps was 0.08, so the look is the same. 2) Mode added with Max as the default: the plan's list has only a mean, which does not make drips. Accumulate from the catalogue left out, a Remap upstream of Mean gives it. 3) Direction is 4 floats and not a per dimension variable so that the default can be Y = 1, normalised over the axes in use as in BurgersSteepen. All 0 was the plan's default, which does nothing. 4) Length is a hybrid, default 100, not 10, which barely shows on a default source. 5) Max and Min fade toward -1 and 1 and leave values already past them alone, so the source passes through unchanged at Length 0. 6) Costs replaced by bench numbers, and the banding check is measured: on a Bump of radius 10, Length 200, tail ripple 0.068 of a range of 2 at a spacing of 0.32 radii, 0.158 at 0.43, 0.396 at 0.65, 0.785 at 1, 1.2 to 1.4 past that, which is a row of copies. So the Taps note says a third of the radius.
data.notes: Taps runs 1 to 64. A clean streak on small sharp spots wants 48 to 64 taps, which is why the presets cost hundreds of ns per sample.

data.seams: None above 0.02 of 4000 in 2D, 3D, 4D on all 15 output and stencil combinations, worst 0.0074 / 0.0069 / 0.0128 over 0.000977, all Crest. All 6 graphs none on 3 seeds. Default node none. Scale 0.01 and 0.25 none, which covers the 4D origin where the radii vanish. Two things it did flag. 1) Band at --scale 8: 6 of 4000 at 0.05 over 0.0078 in 4D. The worst shrinks with the segment (0.0096 at 0.00195, 0.0207 at 0.0039, 0.05 at 0.0078), so it is a steep slope of about 5 per world unit, not a jump. 2) A real inherited jump: Crest at Sample Distance 3 on 2 octave SuperSimplex Feature Scale 150 gives 1 to 2 of 4000 at about 0.05 in 4D, with 2D and 3D clean. Zooming in, the jump stays 0.06 from spacing 0.01 to 0.0002. One tap of that stencil sits on a stock SuperSimplex 4D jump of 7e-5 that does not shrink with spacing, while the other 8 taps do shrink, and second differences amplify it. Perlin gives none, Sample Distance 5 gives none (worst 0.0063). Stated on the Source member. REVIEW: presets at seed 99, default, Hillshade Jet, Laplacian Jet, Crest on Perlin, Band with Sample Distance node crossing 0, Normal X at Sample Distance -0.5, Slope at scale 0.02: none found.
