data.far: Measured with DomainOffset, 2 octaves, Feature Scale 100, at 0, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 3e6, 1e7, 3e7 world units. No NaN. Slope at Sample Distance 10: std 0.243 to 0.248, mean neighbour step 0.0182 near, 0.0199 at 1e7, 0.0250 at 3e7. At Sample Distance 2: 0.0201 near, 0.0293 at 1e7, 0.0662 at 3e7, so rounding noise starts around 1e7 world units (1e5 features) with small steps. Band and Signed Distance stay flat in both up to 3e7. Laplacian and Crest use the fourth root law and smooth out instead: Laplacian std 0.223 near, 0.169 at 1e7, 0.136 at 3e7 at Sample Distance 10; Crest std 0.204, 0.185, 0.160. The check's far coordinate test passes on all. Nothing to write into the description. Gradient outputs pass Sample Distance straight to the stencil as K2 advises, only second order outputs pay for the law. These far numbers were taken before the last Laplacian gain limit edit, which does not change them at this Sample Distance: gain there is 6.25.
data.tile: Every output tiles, Crest included, which the plan said it would not. 4D is not a real 4D form: the stencil runs in the tangent plane of the two GenTileable2D circles, taps turning the point along them, so a tile reads like the 2D output at 2D tap counts. fnlab tile seam ratio 0.95 Hillshade, 1.06 Band, 1.69 Crest (few thin lines per column; the per column test gives 0.42 to 1.26). Exact check: Normal X of a linear field along x matches its sin( angle ) profile to 0.003 in an 8 bit tile. The description says 4D only serves tileable output. At other 4D positions the output is continuous but measures along circles around the origin, not along axes.

data.versus_proto: Same world sizes, looked at both. Slope: same mask and same creases, real is brighter (range to 0.97 where the prototype reaches 0.82 over 8 seeds), the source differs: real Simplex against the prototype's simplex2. Band: same thin even line with the same small loops, not the same layout since the hash differs. Crest: same open drainage net of bright ridges and dark valleys with dashes and dots, about equal density using the critic's a=0.2, b=0.7, rc=0.05, which are now fixed constants. 3D crest: both give torn membranes with windows and many loose pieces, the real one on SuperSimplex has flatter sheets and fewer ring shapes than the prototype's r2 0.5 simplex. 3D band: same constant thickness shell in both. Hillshade and Normal were not in the prototype's best params, I judged them on their own: the real default is flatter than prototype hscale=1, height scale over feature size 0.25 against 0.5. REVIEW: looked at the render and the plan's image, then rendered the real node at the critic's membrane ratios (SuperSimplex Feature Scale 60, Sample Distance 1.2, Band Width 2.4, iso 0.5) and the prototype at its listed params mode=0 oct=1 fq=0.4 h=0.05 w=0.1 eig=1 iso 0.5. Both are torn sheets with holes and loose pieces, the real one finer because its cube holds more features. Neither reproduces the connected foam in the discovery image at those params, so the real node matches the prototype, not the discovery image.
data.plan_changes: 1. Slope Reference default 25, not 0.5, and it is a world height, not a dimensionless number: the prototype's k is a length (k=0.5 at fq=0.5 is 25 at Feature Scale 100), so 0.5 in world units renders blank. I first tried Sample Distance / 0.5, which kept the plan's 0.5 but made brightness change with Sample Distance, so Slope went blank when the step was made smaller. Rejected. 2. Band Width default 3, not 0.06: 0.06 is prototype units (feature 2.5), invisible in world units. It is the half width, and doubles as the Signed Distance clamp and as the Crest line half width, since the plan has no other members for those. 3. Crest outputs crest minus valley, the prototype's best mode=2, with the critic's constants a=0.2, b=0.7, rc=0.05 fixed, plus a rounding floor. 4. 4D is the tangent stencil on the GenTileable2D circles for every output, not 'same code': Crest tiles after all, 4D Crest is 9 taps instead of 33, a tile reads like the 2D output. Price: no real 4 axis derivative, said so in the description. 5. Stencil only applies to Slope, Hillshade, Normal, Laplacian; Signed Distance and Band need per axis second differences for the floor and Crest needs corners, so they are always Central. They use K2 Internal Snap, Ulp and AxisTap; K2 itself is unchanged. 6. Slope, Hillshade and Normal pass Sample Distance straight to the stencil; only Laplacian, Signed Distance, Band and Crest use K2 Step, as its own comment advises. 7. Hillshade in 3D runs a 2D stencil over the XZ slice with Y up, as the prototype did, so 4 taps instead of 6. Normal X/Y/Z in 3D is the full gradient, regularised: with a large Slope Reference it approaches the isosurface normal. 8. Sample Distance floored at 0.01, plus rounding limits: distance slope floor 4e-6, Crest curvature floor 1.6e-5, Laplacian gain limit 2500. Outputs go flat rather than noisy when the step is far too small, at the price of amplitude independence below about 1e-4 source amplitude (estimated from the floors, not measured). 9. Level is read once per sample at the point, not at each tap, so a connected Level should vary slowly. gMetadataVectorSize left alone.

data.notes: All gates pass; status is ok-with-notes for these limits, weigh them at merge. 4D is not a real 4 axis form. Band thickness is even only at 1 to 3 octaves with Sample Distance near Band Width. Signed Distance is a first order estimate, good near Level. Crest is a look for 1 to 2 octaves; that fragmenting at higher counts is the critic's statistic, not re-measured on the node. 3D crest is torn sheets with loose pieces. Crest on 4D SuperSimplex inherits tiny jumps at small steps. Slope, Hillshade, Normal and Laplacian follow Slope Reference as a world height, so rescaling a source needs rescaling that too. Plan gate 4 asked for a measured ScaleOutput constant; none exists because every native range is bounded by construction, measured ranges are in the range field. Hillshade and Normal presets were judged by eye only, no prototype best image to compare. The volume render is SurfaceProbe(Output=Band, Sample Distance=4, Band Width=7, Source=FractalFBm(Octaves=2, Source=SuperSimplex(Feature Scale=110))) at iso 0, a constant thickness shell, passes the same gates. REVIEW (ba32582): code read for unmasked per-lane flow, hash reuse, far coordinate int conversion, division by zero, unused members, metadata defaults, registration order: nothing found; registration is last, defaults match the header, no test node committed, diff touches 4 files. Fixed: two description notes (Crest Sample Distance floor for feature set parity, Band Width node crossing 0). Disagreements with the author: none on the numbers, which reproduce. The 3D crest 'connected membrane' from the plan's discovery image is not what the node or the prototype give at the critic's listed params; the honest description is torn sheets, which the author already states. Crest parity is the one gate 1 item that is parameter dependent: clean at the defaults and presets, degrading below 1/50 of the wavelength. Not verified: MSVC and GCC builds (only clang-cl here); the corner tap lambda expands the enclosing index pack, valid C++17 but worth a glance on the first MSVC build.

data.far: Holds to about 1e6 threads, and the description says where it goes. Measured by Repeat closure: Repeat 8 at Feature Scale 40, samples a whole number of periods away against the same samples near the origin, 100k samples. Weave off by > 0.05: 0% at 1e3 and 1e4 threads, 0.32% at 1e5 (worst 0.066), 65% at 1e6 (float step 0.1 thread, worst 0.690), 85% at 3e6, and at 1e7 the field is flat, std 0.000. Knit: 0% at 1e4, 4.15% at 1e5, 73% at 1e6, 86% at 3e6, std 0.334 at 1e7, flat at 1e8. At Feature Scale 1: Weave 0% at 1e5, 51% at 1e6. data.tile: Fails as cloth, and the description says so. GenTileable2D wraps with no seam: 'tile: seam diff 0.0014 vs interior diff 0.0012 (ratio 1.20, ~1 = seamless)', Knit ratio 1.18, check's tileable ok at ratio 1.28. The image is round yarn sections on black, range -1.000 to 0.048 (viewed), since the torus cuts across the plies. Repeat is the tile route and it closes: worst |f(x + P) - f(x)| over 200k samples is 0.00002 Weave, 0.00003 Knit, 0.00017 Weave Round, 0.0014 Knit Round in 2D, 0.00001 in 3D and 4D, on sets including Repeat 7 rounding up to 8 at N 4, and to 10 at N 5. ThreadTone flips only next to a jump, 0.0005% of samples. A 2 x 2 layout of one period (viewed) shows no seam, wrap step over interior step 0.57 Weave, 0.53 Knit. Repeat needs a grid of Repeat * Feature Scale, and does not help GenTileable2D.
data.versus_proto: Viewed by the reviewer, prototype and node side by side at the same scale, plus the author's comparison, which predates the contact fix. Twill N 4 K 2 Parabola at Feature Scale 64 beside the prototype with prof=1: same floats, same twist lines, same weight. The author read the prototype's rounder crowns as its Round default, and with prof=1 they do match. Rings beside the plan's src=4,k=1.2,cell=0.3,mode=2,prof=1, whose unset N and K default to 2 and 1: the plain weave at the matched scale has the same short over and under arcs as the prototype, while the author's preset at N 4 K 2 had long runs and black gaps, so the preset now sets N 2 K 1. Wire mesh: the prototype's wires are tall ovals that touch at each crossing. The author's round wire left a gap of 0.31 cells at every crossing and rendered as loose floating arcs, so the crossing threads now touch at any width (value 0.000 at z 0 for Thread Width 0.46, 0.35, 0.22, 0.10). It reads as a wire mesh again, rounder and flatter than the prototype's. The preset now also sets Wobble 0, as the plan's wob=0 does; the plan's A=0.6 is a 2D crown and does not affect this 3D view, and Width Jitter 0 is not a member. At fnlab's default --hscale 90 the cloth reads as mountains and Output Min/Max cannot lower it because relief normalises by the observed range, so no preset uses relief. Sheet stats from the author: axis 138.54 Weave, 267.84 Knit against the prototype's 131 and 297, continuity 7.99 against 7.97. At Feature Scale 64 the cube faces of fnlab vol land on cell lines and mid ply and show a flat plate; that is the cut and not the field, as the author says, 51 shows it less. Knit vol and gray match in character and still read as rope columns up close as the plan warned. Field values do not match the prototype: its hashes are different.
data.plan_changes: 1. 3D Weave reads the two nearest threads per axis, not one. The prototype's single cell jumps at every cell line outside the yarn, which the seams gate would flag; the third thread is always past the clamp, so two are enough and the field is exactly continuous. 4.79 ns against the estimated 2.5, and I did not measure a one thread version. 2. 4D is real: the 3D tubes with w as a second ply axis. The plan had not run it. GenTileable2D still gives no cloth, so Repeat stays the tile route. 3. A and B: connected replaces the axis before Feature Scale, so it keeps its meaning of threads per world unit, unconnected adds the constant to the axis. B reads its source with seed + 1 so that one node wired to both gives two fields. No extra rate member is needed. 4. Repeat rounds up to a multiple of N in Weave and of 2 in Knit, where the prototype's closure relied on the caller. It also rounds the fibre and wobble rates. 5. Invalid N, K, Step sets fall back to Step 1. Clamps are done in UpdateDerived from raw members so the setter order cannot lose a value. 6. Thread Width in Knit maps 0.46 to the prototype's yarn of 0.25, capped there: the 3 row window only holds a yarn up to 0.25 with its jitter. 7. 3D thickness follows Thread Width up to 0.3 instead of a fixed 0.3, and a thread's centre sits one thickness off the ply, so crossing threads touch at any width. 8. Weft run formula: the prototype's Step special case equals the general formula at K 1, so it is dropped. 9. Hidden constants, none added as members: Crown 0.9, Width Jitter 0.04, Twist 0.25, Wobble rate 0.6, Ply Height 2, Yarn Jitter 0.08 and the stitch table, which is a literal table and not built per node. 10. Satin N 5 K 1 Step 2 is in the gallery and battery but not a preset, Knit took its slot. 11. 12. Reviewer: a Thread Width at or under 0 leaves no thread, height fades out under a width of 0.02. 13. Reviewer: one GenT over a pack in place of three Gen overloads, as the plan's decisions ask.

A connected Wobble source ran in Knit 3D and 4D for nothing, the author had noted it. 4. Three Gen overloads became one GenT, per the decisions; bit exact, worst 3.6e-07 on 17 setups. 5. Checked and found clean: no per lane control flow outside masks, hash bits independent (tone 0..7, jitter 8..15, fibre phase 16..23 of a MixHash, wobble from a salted MixHash), Mod over the full int range, far int conversion, all members used, metadata defaults equal an untouched node, setter order, registration at the very bottom, no test node committed, every plan member present. Found and expected: Round profile, worst 0.124, 1917 of 4000, a rim with infinite slope; Bevel=0, worst 0.72, hard edges; Split Stop driven by a node, worst 2.0, 751 of 4000, walls appear where the decision flips (stated in the member text). Found and traced to the input: Row Offset=Simplex 3D worst 0.132 (3 of 4000) and Mortar=Abs(Simplex) 3D worst 0.075 (6 of 4000), both clean with Perlin in place of Simplex (worst 0.0106 and 0.0115), so attributed to the Simplex 3D/4D jumps the handbook describes. Not jumps: preset parquet is flagged at scale 7.5 (worst 0.0253, 76 of 4000) but shrinks with the step, 0.0093 at scale 3 and 0.0031 at scale 1, none found, so it is its steep 0.03 bevel. A Fan with Bevel=Remap(Perlin) at 0.02-0.2 is flagged by 1 of 4000 at 0.0228, none found at a finer scale. REVIEW: presets at seeds 1337 and 7 at scale 0.25 x Feature Scale: none found except parquet 3D (7-8 of 4000 at 0.022-0.023, its 0.03 bevel at that step, as the author says). Chevron with Tile Height above about 1e4 at Feature Scale 1 shows jumps near the slanted edges (3e4: worst 0.034, 1e6: worst 0.91): float resolution of the strip coordinate grows with Tile Height; 1e3 is clean. Degenerate aspect ratio, not fixed.
data.far: fnlab check far coordinates ok: std 0.604 vs near 0.620. Extra test through the C API, 9 patterns at 1e2, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6 noise units from the origin, 40000 points: finite, range stays in -1..1, std steady, and 0.00% of samples off by >0.02 for SSE2, SSE41 and AVX512 against AVX2 in all 36 cases. That needed two fixes, see notes. REVIEW: period_test.py re-run on the rebuilt DLL: period fails 0, all 99 x/y lines 0.000%, far parity 0.00% in every row.
data.tile: GenTileable2D is seamless but not a useful image, and the description says so. fnlab tile: Grid seam 0.0012 vs interior 0.0020, Courses 0.0000 vs 0.0000, Fan 0.0004 vs 0.0006. GenTileable2D feeds XY with cos a, cos b, so the pattern comes out stretched and mirrored: measured, the image differs from its own mirror by at most 1e-4 in both axes. Native tiling is Period, tested through the C API on f(p) against f(p + period) with a Period 0 control: all 9 patterns, Period 4, 5, 6, outputs TileValue, Lookup with a Perlin Source, LocalU, with Split Levels 2 on box patterns, 40000 points: 0.000% off by >0.02 in x and y, control 60-89% off on TileValue and Lookup. 3D with Z Length 1.5, Lookup, Period 4 and 5: 0.000% in x, y and z. A Source that is not itself periodic in world z breaks Z tiling when Z Length is 0.
data.range: Value outputs use ScaleOutput( v, -1, 1 ) and EdgeDistance uses ScaleOutput( max( e - mortar, 0 ), 0, MaxEdge ), with Output Min/Max from the VariableRange mixin. Measured over 1e6 points and 4 seeds at Mortar 0: Lookup with constant Source +1 and -1 exactly -1..1 on all patterns; TileValue -1..1; EdgeDistance low -1, top 1.000 on Grid, RunningBond, Basket, Herringbone, Chevron, Fan, 0.999 Hex, 0.997 Scales, 0.989 Courses, so the per pattern MaxEdge bounds hold and are tight; TiltedHeight top 0.78-0.93; LocalU top 0.37-0.94 and LocalV 0.28-0.88 with the default bevel. Lookup stays in range only while Source does: preset parquet with its FBm Source measured -1.09..1.09.
data.versus_proto: Compared the prototype's patterns with the real node (Lookup with an FBm Source, Mortar 0.03, Bevel 0.12, gray and hillshade). All 9 patterns reproduce the prototype's geometry: bonds, basket blocks, herringbone, hex, chevron mitres, jittered courses, overlapping scales, fan rings. What differs: layouts differ because the hashes are not the prototype's; the prototype's wood and cell crack panels used its internal sources, the real node gets those from a graph (preset parquet, a stretched FBm, and the cellular plates test); Fan at Tile Width 4 has more and smaller cobbles because Ring and Cobble are fixed at 0.34 where the prototype's best used 0.42; mortar lines on Scales look heavier than the prototype's panel because the real sheet uses 0.03 / 0.12 everywhere. Relief and vol were judged on the real renders only, not side by side with the prototype. The TileSplit and recursive cut prototypes were not compared side by side either: Split was judged on its own renders, where Split Levels 3 reads as jumbled jointed blocks. REVIEW: compared the image myself. All nine layouts match the prototype: bond offsets, 3 plank baskets, herringbone, hex, chevron mitres, jittered courses, overlapping scales, fan rings. Differences seen: the real Fan has smaller cobbles and more rings per disc; the real Chevron and Basket panels are rendered at a smaller Feature Scale so the strips look narrower; the prototype wood grain panels have no counterpart because Source comes from the graph. Nothing in the real sheet looks wrong.
data.plan_changes: Added the VariableRange mixin (gate 4; the member table lists only Feature Scale and Seed Offset). Row Offset driven by a node shifts every other row by its value instead of row x value, whose slope grows without limit away from the origin; a constant still gives row x value. EdgeDistance is clamped at the mortar line and normalised by an analytic per pattern maximum, the prototype returned raw e - mortar. Split draws stop, cut and axis noise from 8 bit fields of one mix per level instead of 6 mixes (about 0.75 ns per level on AVX2 instead of about 1.0), and cuts Z only when Z Length is above 0. Z Length staggers by half a tile length (N x Tile Height on Basket and Herringbone) and gives Source a per slab Z, otherwise Source gets world Z. Bevel is floored at 1e-3 rather than exactly 0, sharp at any sensible scale. Split Balance is limited to 0.01-0.49 and negative Mortar is clamped to 0 to keep leaves non empty and the range honest. Period is rounded up to even on Basket and Chevron and to a multiple of 2N on Herringbone rather than rejected; Z repeats every Period slabs when even, 2 x Period when odd. Ring and Cobble stayed fixed at 0.34 as the plan says, so Fan ring count follows Tile Width. Estimated costs are replaced by the measured numbers in bench. REVIEW: Chevron edge now computed as ( h / 2 - |across| ) * cos instead of FNMulAdd( |across|, cos, h / 2 * cos ); identical to 3e-7 on every default pattern x output at 0, 1e3 and 1e5 noise units.
data.notes: Status is ok-with-notes for 2 reasons: there is no real 4D form (stated in the description, GenTileable2D gives a mirrored copy), and Bevel at or near 0 can fail fnlab entry parity on Hex and Fan (see check). Default node and every non zero bevel config tested pass all gates. Two findings: (1) a scalar 1.0f / member evaluated in Gen compiled to a different value per feature set, off by 1 ulp; on a steep output that broke parity far from the origin, 20-27% of Grid and Chevron samples at 1e5, so TileDomain computes reciprocals in its setters. A product minus a small value also fused to FMA on some feature sets, so offsets come off a fraction. (2) fnlab raw has no --ox or --oy option and silently ignores them, which made my first Period test vacuous; it was redone through the C API with a negative control, after a second test bug that passed a node pointer as a float. Only built with clang-cl through build_fn.sh, MSVC, GCC, ARM and WASM not tried. gMetadataVectorSize in Metadata.cpp not updated, it is a reservation only. fnlab relief normalises height, so Output Min/Max do not change a relief preset. Images read: 5. REVIEW (6d313c3): read the full diff; no test node, registration at the bottom of the list, all 20 plan members present with the plan defaults, no unused members, no per lane branches, division only by clamped or offset quantities. Hash bit fields in Split use distinct bytes of one mix. Int conversion of ids is in range below 2^31 tiles; Fan id2 = ring * 4096 + sector overflows only above about 5e5 rings (Tile Width above 3.5e5), cosmetic. Fixed one defect: Chevron slanted edge cancellation. Disagreements: none of substance. The EdgeDistance top is MaxEdge - Mortar over MaxEdge, so 1 is reached only with Mortar 0, which the member text does not quite say. gMetadataVectorSize still not bumped (reservation only). Reviewer logs: review_*.sh and review_compare.py.

data.seams: Author: 0 jumps above 0.02 in 219 + 63 dimension scans over all 15 Mode x Output combinations. Reviewer: 0 jumps in every scan with a constant or an always positive hybrid Radius (presets, other seeds and scales, Rope at Seed Offset 5, Length, Radius = 0.05 + 0.03 Simplex). Hybrid Radius nodes that go negative over part of the domain do report jumps: Radius=Perlin(Feature Scale=140) '4D: jumps above 0.02: 1 of 4000' at 0.0210, Radius=100 Simplex with Pipe and Radius=Simplex+0.1 with Rope also 'SEAMS: jumps found'. Cause: Radius is floored at 1e-4 features, and 1 - d / 1e-4 is a hairline with slope 1e4 per feature, which the 1e-3 bisection reads as a jump. The same graphs with the Radius kept positive scan clean, so this is the Radius definition at 0, now stated in the Radius description, and not a lattice seam.
data.range: Tunnel, Pipe and Rope clamp to [-1,1] by construction; measured -1.000 to 0.999. Distance is d - Radius clamped to [-1,1], so the real range is [-Radius, 1], measured [-0.100, 1.000] at Radius 0.1 and [-0.060, 1.000] at the default. Length peaks over about 16M samples per mode across 2D, 3D, 4D were 1.57 (Tube), 1.32 (Network), 1.28 (Sheet), so ScaleOutput uses native max 1.6, 1.35, 1.3 with a Min on top since a peak search is not a bound. FractalFBm(Octaves=3) over Sheet Distance reaches 1.750, which is FBm's own unnormalised sum.
data.far: fnlab check far coordinates ok on every combination in both batteries. Deeper through DomainOffset at Feature Scale 32: air fraction, std and max step stay normal through 3e5 features; at 1e6 features positions quantise and distinct values collapse, 175566 to 22644 for Network, and stock Perlin collapses at the same point, 846844 to 108550. No node specific far limit found, so none is in the description. Feature Scale 1e6 is a flat field with meaningless continuity WARNs, same as Perlin at that scale.
data.tile: Real 4D form, so GenTileable2D wraps by construction, at the 4D cost. The check's single row comparison WARNs on sparse Tunnel output on some seeds (ratio up to 7.19 on Tube at seed 2024, 4.42 on Network at seed 99, 3.51 on Rope with a Simplex Radius) because most of the field is clamped at -1 and its interior row can miss every tube. Compared against all interior rows and columns of the tile PNG, the seam's peak step is always below the interior peak step (0.059 vs 0.149, 0.102 vs 0.153), but its mean step ranks at the 40th to 92nd percentile of interior steps, so that comparison is suggestive, not a proof. Output=Distance, which is not clamped, never WARNed. Sheet tile rendered and viewed: no visible seam. As in 2D, Tube and Network are dots on the torus. Reviewer did not render a tile.
data.versus_proto: The comparison at seed 42, viewed by author and reviewer: same character in both, a round section worm tangle with no visible lattice pattern, Network denser and joined, Tube separate loops, small debris pieces in both. Not the same field: the K1 kernel has a different 2D gradient table, different value bits and a different normalisation, so tube positions differ. Real Tube looks thicker in that frame because it shows 5.4 lattice cells where the prototype image, if it used the critic's best params, shows about 6.9; those params are assumed. A few short straight rods are visible in the real renders; the prototype notes report one on seed 1337. Reviewer's own vol of the Cave network preset at seed 7 has the same look. Air and connectivity reproduce: Network 5.9% air with the largest component 93-94% of air (prototype 90%), Tube Radius 0.09 at 4.9-5.0% air with largest component 34-37% (prototype 28-37%). Radius uniformity was not re-measured on the real node; the radius CV of 0.13 is the prototype's number.
data.plan_changes: Radius default 0.06 instead of 0.085: the plan's value is in prototype units at f=0.674, which is 0.057 features, and 0.085 features measures 11.2% air against the intended 5-6%. Output Distance is signed d - Radius in features capped at 1, because the prototype form min(d/R, 2) - 1 is exactly -Tunnel. Length was never coded in the prototype (its switch falls through to Tunnel), so it is defined here as the plain channel magnitude, min over pairs in Network, same polarity as Distance, ignoring Radius and Damping. Rope in Sheet mode is Tunnel since one channel has no angle. Rope uses cos 6 th = T3(cos 2 th) instead of atan2, so K4 is not needed. Pipe and Rope use fixed wall 0.25 and 6 ribs with 0.3 depth, as the plan lists no members for them. No per dimension Damping scale: derived from the constants, the kernel's squared scale differs from the prototype's by 2.3x in 2D and 0.75x in 4D and matches in 3D; the 2D and 4D effect of this was not measured. The value term is scaled per dimension to the prototype's 0.35 of a root 2 gradient. Review: Damping is clamped to [1e-4, 1e6] in the setter (metadata range stays 1e-4..10).

4D distance is measured along all 4 axes, so a fixed w 3D slice is not a true slice distance. The prototype notes say an xyz only Jacobian looks cleaner with w as time; that was not ported, because it would be wrong for the torus tile and the plan has no member for it.
The thumbnail is the Contour lines preset, not the default, because default Network in 2D is only dots.
Only clang-cl 23 was built and run. No MSVC or Linux build.

Review 7b3012e: code read against the K1 kernel; channels take disjoint hash bits (5 gradient bits each from bit 0, 4 value bits each from bit 19), all control flow is on members, every divisor is floored (Radius 1e-4, det 1e-9, a2+b2 1e-12, Dot+Damping with Damping 1e-4), hybrid Radius is sampled with the pre offset seed before ScalePositions as Cellular does, registration is at the bottom of FastSIMD_Build.inl, no test node committed, every plan member present. Fixes: SetDamping now clamps to [1e-4, 1e6] because at Damping above about 2e38 or inf the solve is inf / inf = NaN, which x86 Max hides by returning 0 and NEON would not; Radius description now says a hairline stays at Radius 0 and a hybrid crossing 0 reads as a jump. Gen code is unchanged, so the author's bench and gallery still apply.
It does the same for ExchangeFoam. That is the checker expecting estimates, not a plan error.

data.versus_proto: Same zoom, gray panels. Zebra: node std 0.345, radial peak 11, centroid 12.5 cycles per panel, coherence 0.96; prototype 0.348, 11, 12.1, 0.95. Dune: node 0.294, 7, 8.9, 0.88; prototype 0.301, 7, 8.8, 0.90. Same long crests, Y merges and dark interdune flats. Individual forks differ because stock Perlin uses a gradient table and the prototype random unit vectors, and the node's B offset is in world units. Dune relief and 3D folded agate read the same as the prototype, with the same nested strata, at Radial Frequency 4.77 for the prototype's fr=30 radians. Low |z| samples near A's lattice points: 11.4% with the node's offset, 37.8% with no offset, 6.25% uniform; the critic's 13.9% and 62.5% came from prototype Perlin and another threshold.
data.plan_changes: Added the Feature Scale mixin, the plan listed only Seeded and Range: a plane carrier needs a world size, and sources keep their own scale. Frequency default is 5, not 1.5: the prototype's F=1.5 per unit at sf=0.3 is 5 stripes per source feature, which is what a user gets with equal Feature Scales. Frequency is in cycles for Radial too, the prototype's fr=30 radians is 4.77, so one range fits both and the plan's 'much higher values' note is gone. Seed Offset goes to the sources, the node has no lattice of its own. B at seed + 1 also when connected, or B equal to A gives no vortices. A non zero constant B is honoured, stripes bend without forks. The B offset is a fixed world offset of 137.31, -84.87, 52.46, -31.72 because the node cannot read a source's Feature Scale. Setter clamps: Charge 1..8, Softening at least 0.001, Duty 0..1, Stoss 0.05..0.95, Crest Round 0..1, Taper at least 0.001, Frequency +-1000. Crest Round above 1 could step at the wave wrap. Dune has no ripple, as the member list says.

review.check: All 5 presets re-run with --seed 7: 0 FAIL, 0 WARN each, SEAMS none found in 2D/3D/4D. Reviewer battery of 16 odd trees: negative Softening, Taper, Stoss, Crest Round, Duty, Charge, Charge 100 with Softening 1e9, Feature Scale 0 / 1e-9 / 1e9, Carrier Angle -1e30, B -0.3 / 1e30 / Constant node, Radial Frequency -7 and 1e9, Seed Offset 2147483647 on node and source: 0 NaN/Inf in every tree. FAILs only on degenerate settings: Softening 1e9 gives a constant (non-constant FAIL), A=White() fails parity and continuity exactly as stock White() does on its own, Radial Frequency 1e9 (clamped to 1000) fails entry parity at 1.87e-03 with 2739 of 4000 seams jumps, rounding of 1000 rings per unit magnitude. Feature Scale 1e-9 (5e9 stripes per world unit) shows precision jumps in seams, like SineWave would.
review.bench: fnlab bench ns/sample 2D / 3D / 4D, same run as stock Perlin AVX2 0.95 / 2.15 / 4.19. Cos default: SSE41 6.39 / 10.24 / 19.34, AVX2 2.65 / 5.32 / 9.03, AVX512 1.85 / 3.19 / 8.15. Dune: AVX2 3.59 / 6.05 / 9.96. Within 5% of the author's numbers.
review.versus_proto: Rendered fnlab thumb of the Zebra forks preset beside the prototype: same stripe density and fork style, the node's forks are a little more frequent and its stripes read slightly thinner at this zoom; the hillshade panels match.
review.notes: Code read in full: no unmasked per-lane control flow (switches are on members), hash fields not reused, all members used, metadata defaults match members, registration at the bottom of FastSIMD_Build.inl, no test node committed. Dune normalisation 1 - round * stoss * (1 - stoss) checked analytically for the quadratic SMin: correct. The 3D Hex delta un-reflection (delta - 2/3 sum) checked analytically: it returns the exact world delta.

Stock Perlin in the same run 0.92 / 2.75 / 4.23, so the node adds under 1.0 ns to the two source samples for Cos. The stock 21-node graph was measured earlier at 7.39-8.63 ns.
